author: rbuergi
body:
Refs #5274 · refs #5424 · refs #5426

## What this records

The `[DISPOSE-DISCARD]` family (#5274, #5424, #5426), checked against the code. None of the three is a missing `FailGate` or a skipped drain:

- **RetiringAnActivation covers init-fault retirements only.** Those are the only teardowns that have a cause more specific than the teardown itself. An overlay self-heal recycle or an Orleans grain deactivation has no such cause, so failing the gate first would say nothing the generic drain does not already say.
- **Draining first is not possible.** The parked deliveries are waiting for a bring-up that the teardown ends. TeardownLayers → *Handler turns* already documents this case: when a hub is torn down before it finishes starting, its parked work is answered `ShuttingDown` and reported. That answer is composed through `ShutdownNack.RetryForTheAuthoritativeAnswer` (#4866), so the transient classifiers re-probe.
- **The overlay self-heal does not loop.** Its watcher is armed in `WithInitialization` and its first emission is a replay. It can therefore fire before the gates open, and when it does the overlay is already obsolete. The only open question is the **Error level** for a bring-up discard from a foreign sender. That is a maintainer decision, recorded on #5426.

author: tiffygk
body:
## What

Part B of the docs refresh round: the published component library is brought current with what ships and reorganised as a reference. Components are grouped by where a player meets them (foundations, the board and layout, the hint ladder, coach chat, after the game) instead of by the date they shipped, and a new "Who it belongs to" card states the colour and shape rules for the player, mallow, the coach and the menu. The docs home's two descriptions of the library are updated to match.

## Why

An audit against the code found the library behind what ships:
- The conversion-reason example quoted the old mate nudge ("there was a faster mate. mate in 5 was there, now it's mate in 3"). The shipped lines are "still winning, but you have checkmate on the board right now." and "still winning, but there's a mate N moves faster. this move mates in X, the fastest mates in Y." (`server/annotator/classify.ts`, `conversionCopyFor`), and the nudge fires only within 8 moves of mate (`JUDGE_MATE_NUDGE_DEPTH`).
- The settings popover showed three toggles; the shipped popover also has judge strictness (gentle, standard, blunt) and coach voice (Claude (Recommended), Local Ollama, templates only).
- The lost-mate line was shown beside the nudge badge, but losing a forced mate goes to the warning tier, so it never renders there.

The owner then asked for less text, full-width captions, consistent padding, grouping by where a component lives, the round-review paper register removed (it is not in the game), the style described by who each component belongs to, and the coach called "the coach" in prose.

## How it was checked

- `npm run gate` on this branch: `GATE: PASS`.
- `npx vitest run tools/docsParity.test.ts`: 8 passed.
- `docs/component-library.html` is byte-identical to the owner's working copy (`cmp`).
- Rendered with agent-browser at 1512x982: caption and card widths match (1060px) in all 22 sections, no horizontal scroll. Visible words on the main tab went from 9,644 to 4,098.
- No test added: a static HTML reference page.

## Review

The owner reviewed the rendered page in three passes and approved it. Every shipped component specimen was kept (moved, not deleted), except the paper register; the single-toggle highlight tray, replaced by the move-pair badges, moved to the archive tab.

## Rulings

- Ruling: the lost-mate line is removed from the nudge example / shipped code routes a lost mate to the warning tier and the reason text renders only on a nudge / cost if wrong: one example row.
- Ruling: shipped UI strings containing "cookie" (the plate, "cookie is thinking…", "ask cookie") stay verbatim while prose says "the coach" / the library shows what ships / cost if wrong: a text sweep.
- Ruling: the arrow legend row reads "mallow's recommended move" / matches `analysisLegend.ts` and the 2026-08-05 owner ruling / cost if wrong: one label.

## Rollback

`git revert -m 1 <merge sha>` after merge. The round's rollback tag is `pre-architecture-page-2026-09-22`.

body:
## Purpose

New internally controlled successor experiment, **not an M10 replication**.
Add a separately versioned OpenAI Responses provider profile; preserve the old
offline broker contract and historical evidence unchanged.

## Changes

- Native seven-function protocol with bounded local mediation; no hosted tools.
- Canonical Responses/count request pair and broker independent recount.
- Full stateless provider-output replay, including encrypted reasoning state;
  deterministic `C2 = F(C1_raw_response, frozen_local_result)`.
- Raw response and usage preservation, no reasoning double count, fail-closed
  identity/config/cap/usage checks, known usage retained on rejected identity.
- Durable one-attempt transport, count/generation reservations, fixed lifetime
  admission latch, no retry/redirect/fallback or restart budget.
- Fixed Astra/medium configuration, C1/C2 cap4096 and last C3 cap64;
  maximum3 generation and12 count attempts. No live pilot entry point.
- Production-material + provider-profile seal and offline CI verification.
- Official-document provenance and A–L contract/budget/observability notes.

## Verification

- Full successor regression: **394 tests passed under `-W error`**.
- Includes **109 new profile/transport/mediation/conformance tests**.
- Real production preflight: T0 FRESH, sole intended T1 stale cause, unchanged
  fresh controls, production gate, AST counterexamples and compilation.
- New seal preparation and full reconstruction succeeded:
  `1153fd2ff04e4675f4ecfb17d8c789fb8da3c20c9c889b2b217acb2e7af8ed61`.
- Local native-tool compile test uses real `javac`; fake upstream receipts are
  explicitly fictional, never represented as real provider exact counts.
- `git diff --check` clean; production `tmf/`, README and historical results
  unchanged.

## Independent audit and execution status

The first complete independent audit rejected three concrete defects: request-only
cache fields required in Responses output, directory-entry crash durability, and
incorrect monetary completeness on rejected pricing identity. Commit `5cb1f6e`
fixes all three with eight additional regressions. Independent exact-snapshot
re-audit gave **READY (code/offline scope)**: 109 tests passed without skips,
15 extra probes passed, all 11 sealed files/8 official snapshots matched, and
full external seal reconstruction passed. No blocking code findings remain.

**Real generations=0, real count requests=0, live pilot runs=0.** No credential material
was read; a protected masked-entry request yielded no credential. Protected host credentials and enabled protected egress
are also prerequisites; neither is currently established. Independent READY is now recorded for this exact tested seal, but the
protected execution environment is not yet available, so no real API request
has been dispatched. Code readiness is not live-environment readiness.

Planned generation-only maximum, conditional on the frozen provider contract, is $0.7878 at the documented frozen rates without a
cache discount; count pricing remains unknown, so all-in USD maximum is unknown.
Immutable provider deployment/tokenizer revisions remain explicitly unavailable.

No merge or package release is requested by this PR. Six-arm live experiments
remain unauthorized even if future conformance succeeds.

## CI integration boundary

Generic unit-test jobs do not prefetch the frozen Guava jars; the three Java-dependent new checks now follow the repository's explicit integration prerequisite guard. The dedicated successor job must fetch the frozen dependencies, run the tests, and reconstruct the production seal without a skip path. With dependencies present, all109 new tests pass. A production-material offline E2E also passed all15 fictional POST operations (12 count /3 generation), with network denied and0 real calls.

author: githaltwastaken
body:
**Audit lead 1 — confirmed (critical).** The octave stage picks the accented atom class counting from the anchor seed's phase; section 0 is re-seeded during growth and can sit a whole atom away. Both engines applied the class unchanged, so on songs whose first beat falls on the eighth-note grid the first red line was written **half a beat late**.

| | first red line on the off-beat (8 plain renders) |
|---|---:|
| before | **5 / 8** (250 ms late at 120 BPM, 200 ms at 150) |
| after | **0 / 8** (all within 1 ms) |

**Fix.** Shift the class into section 0's frame by the rounded phase difference (halves as `floor(x + 0.5)` in both Python and Rust, for parity).

**The corpus had it too.** `fast-300` (300 BPM read at 150, first kick at 0.2 s) had its red line at 400.2 ms — on the snare — and passed because the benchmark scores modulo one 300 BPM beat. It now sits at 200.2 ms, on the kick. `bench/golden/fast-300.json` re-dumped for that reason only; the other 23 vectors are byte-identical.

**Gates.** 206/206 unit tests (new test fails 3/5 on the old code); benchmark 24/24, 0.0000 BPM / 0.16 ms; bpm-snapshot unchanged; golden 24/24; coverage / measures / signatures green; cargo test 178/178 (new test fails on the old code); overtone-bench golden 24/24.

author: bitemyapp
body:
Compiling [vesl-core](https://github.com/zkvesl/vesl-core)'s kernels with `master`'s honk and hoonc gives different bytes for all four (mint, guard, settle, forge). vesl opens its files with `/+` and `/-` imports, which nockchain's own kernels never use, so kernel parity never exercised them.

## What differed

1. **Spots after `/-`, `/+` and `/?`.** hoonc's `+pile-rule` consumes the import header before `++vest` parses the body, so the body carries one `%dbug`, starting at the body. hatch's `/` branch wraps the body in a second `%dbug` that starts at the first import line, and `wrap_hoon_with_trace` only dropped it for `/=`, `/*` and `/#`. In `mint.jam` the first difference is the entry spot: honk has `[[14 1] [%Q 3]]` (the `/+  *vesl-mint` line) where hoonc has `[[18 1] [%Q 3]]`. nockup's app templates (`/+  lib`) hit the same bug.
2. **Reading the header.** hatch skipped import lines and honk read them with separate line-based code. Compared with hoonc:
   - `/+  *alpha,  ::  note` followed by an indented `*beta` **silently dropped `*beta`**, because the comment was stripped after the lines were joined.
   - A `,` list continued onto an unindented line failed to compile.
   - An indented directive was folded into the one before it and failed to resolve.
3. **`/*` marks.** hoonc ignores the mark. A leaf whose name contains `.hoon` is compiled as Hoon, and anything else becomes `$octs`. honk rejected every mark except `%jam` and never compiled a Hoon leaf.
4. **`/dat` leaves.** hoonc evaluates every Hoon leaf under `/dat` at build time and keeps `|.(vaz)`. honk kept the deferred `+swet` trap for every `/dat` leaf except the pinned `softed-constraints`. That changes both standard and arbitrary artifacts for any other `/#` import, or a `/=` of a `/dat` file.

## Fix

- hatch has a new import-directive parser that follows `+pile-rule` (`gap`, `gaw`, `taut-rule`, `stap`). The `/` branch skips the header with it. honk's resolver reads imports through the same parser (`parse_import_header`), so the two can't disagree.
- `wrap_hoon_with_trace` collapses the spot for every import rune.
- A `/*` leaf is compiled or read as `$octs` depending on its file name, as in `+is-hoon`.
- A Hoon leaf under `/dat` is minted, evaluated, and wrapped in the eval-vase trap that the `softed-constraints` override already uses.

honk now also rejects some input that hoonc rejects: a single space after an import rune (`/+ foo`), a `*` face on `/*`, and a `/=` path without a leading `/`. It still accepts directives out of `+pile-rule` order. One divergence is unchanged on purpose: an entry outside the deps dir keeps its cwd-relative spot path, where hoonc bakes in the absolute path.

## Tests and CI

- The `wild_import` pairing only checked that both artifacts existed, and it fails strict parity on `master` because of the first bug. It is now a strict `cmp`.
- A new `import_syntax` pairing has one entry that uses every header form above. It also covers a library with comments between its imports and a `/#` file that imports a library.
- CI runs both pairings as `//crates/honk/test-assets:import_parity_test`. The parity workflow now also triggers on `crates/hatch/**`. The spot bug lived in hatch, and a hatch-only change never reached the parity gate.
- hatch unit tests cover the header grammar and check that the body spot starts after each header form. The spot test fails if the old rune set is restored. honk unit tests cover the comment, continuation and indentation cases and the `/*` leaf kinds.

## Validation

- **vesl-core kernels.** At vesl-core `fa4e16f`, compiled with hoonc and with this branch's honk (entry `hoon/lib/<k>-kernel.hoon`, deps `hoon`), mint, guard, settle and forge are byte-identical. On `master`, honk's output differs by 32 to 48 bytes.
- **vesl-core templates.** The self-contained ones (counter, data-registry, settle-report, graft-intent) are byte-identical to hoonc. All four differ on `master`.
- **Probe trees.** 43 probe trees cover every header form, `/dat` entries and imports, `/*` marks, standard-mode builds, and non-Hoon files in the deps dir. All are byte-identical to hoonc. The `/dat` import probe also matches cold and warm through `--cache-dir`.
- **nockchain kernels.** dumb, wal, miner, peek, bridge and roswell are byte-identical to `master`'s honk, and compile times are unchanged.
- **Test runs:**
  - `bazel test //crates/honk/test-assets:import_parity_test`: 2 passed
  - `cargo test --release -p hatch --lib`: 282 passed
  - `cargo test --release -p honk`: 242 passed (163 lib, 6 bin, 73 integration)
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

**Downstream impact.** vesl-core's committed JAMs and `scripts/CHECKSUMS.sha256` were built with a honk that has the spot bug. Rebuilding with this change changes their bytes, and the new bytes match hoonc's.

author: fajarhide
body:
@ahmadrosid

## Summary

An artifact written on behalf of an app user was unreachable: the listing skipped it and the content route answered 404. Closes #1193, retitled after the correction above.

**Before:** a session with an `appUserId` writes to `profiles/<id>/users/<hash>/artifacts/`, while `listArtifacts` and `readArtifactFile` resolved `getProfileArtifactsDir` whatever the caller was.
**After:** both take the same `X-Nakama-App-User-Id` the session routes already take, and resolve that user's folder when it is present.

One resolver, used by both read paths:

```ts
function artifactsDirFor(orgId, profileId, appUserId?) {
  const trimmed = appUserId?.trim();
  return trimmed
    ? path.join(getAppUserSoulDir(orgId, profileId, trimmed), "artifacts")
    : getProfileArtifactsDir(orgId, profileId);
}
```

Why safe:
1. No header means the old path, byte for byte. The dashboard, the local token and `org viewer can read artifact content` are untouched, and a test pins that an app-user-owned file stays out of the no-header listing.
2. The header is read inline at both call sites rather than through a helper, since it is one expression used twice.
3. Nothing moves on disk and no schema changes.

## The one judgement call

Isolation is strict: a request naming an app user sees only that user's folder, with no fallback to the shared one. That means artifacts created before app-user routing existed, which sit in the shared folder, are not visible to an app user.

I picked strict because a fallback makes which directory answered depend on whether a file happened to be there, and a 404 that moves is worse to debug than one that does not. Say the word if you would rather have the fallback; it does not weaken cross-user isolation either way, because one app user's files are never in the shared folder.

## Test plan
- [x] Three cases, as asked: an app user reads their own artifact, cannot reach another one's, and a request with no app user still gets the shared folder.
- [x] One of the three fails on `83d7407b`: two app users owning the same filename. The other two pass there as well, so they are guards rather than catchers, and I would rather say that than count them as proof.
- [x] `bun test packages/core apps/server`, base and branch on `83d7407b`: identical failure sets, `comm` empty both ways.
- [ ] Not exercised against a live API-key session. Every link is a unit test plus the chain in the issue comment, not an observation.

body:
Chỉ **tài liệu**, không đổi một dòng code nào. `docs/*` và `*.md` nằm trong `is_no_container_path()` của deployer, nên release này deploy với `services=none` - không container nào bị tạo lại.

## Việc này bổ sung gì

PR #9 đã đưa ADR-046 lên production nhưng để trống phần số đo ("đo được, xem báo cáo kiểm thử tải"). PR này điền con số thật vào đó và lưu bằng chứng thành tài liệu.

## Kết quả đo trên production

Release `61a28a9`, provider thật `opencode.ai`/`deepseek-v4.1-flash`, qua đúng đường công khai Worker → Tunnel → nginx → FastAPI:

| | 60 người @ concurrency 1 | 60 người @ concurrency 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Hàng đợi rút trong | 526,1 s | **136,0 s** (3,87×) |
| Nộp thành công | 60/60 `201` | 60/60 `201` |
| `peak_overlap` | 1 | **4** |
| p50 / p95 review | 7557 / 13898 ms | 7355 / 13954 ms |
| Lỗi AI | 0 | 0 |

Cổng go/no-go đạt hết: 0 lỗi 429, RAM khả dụng đáy 6565 MiB, RSS worker đỉnh 51 MiB, load đỉnh 3,67, 0 restart, health `200` suốt.

## Đính chính ADR-046

Lý lẽ lúc ra quyết định là *"đây là trần provider, không phải trần CPU"*. Số đo cho thấy **ngược lại**: thứ chạm trần trước là **CPU 2 lõi** (load đỉnh 3,67 trên cổng `<4`, còn ~9% biên), trong khi provider không hề bị bóp. Decision giữ nguyên, thêm mục **Đính chính** vào Consequences để người đọc sau không suy "provider còn chịu được" thành "nâng được nữa".

## Hai chỗ lệch, ghi rõ chứ không giấu

1. **Lượt 60@4 đầu tiên phát từ máy dev bị hỏng** - Cloudflare bóp theo IP trên route `*.workers.dev` (21/60 login, 12/39 submit `SSL: UNEXPECTED_EOF_WHILE_READING`; cùng URL đó từ VPS 20/20 OK). Phải phát lại từ VPS, vẫn qua đúng đường công khai.
2. **Tổng token chưa gom được** - harness không cộng dồn `usage`, và dòng `ai_reviews` đã bị xoá cùng cuộc thi test lúc dọn. Chi phí thật của một đợt 60 người vẫn chưa có con số; đây là việc của lần đo sau.

Báo cáo cũng ghi 2/111 lượt hỏng vì đầu ra model ở concurrency 4 so với 0/61 ở concurrency 1 (Fisher exact **p = 0,540** - không do concurrency; nhưng vì hai mã lỗi non-retryable nên mỗi lượt hỏng là một job `FAILED` vĩnh viễn).

## Dọn dẹp

8 cuộc thi test xoá qua API cascade, 232 account test vô hiệu hoá qua API, `ai_review_jobs`/`ai_reviews`/`competition_content_revisions` = **0**, bucket chỉ còn 2 object của cuộc thi thật, không ciphertext khoá provider nào sót lại. `vku-deploy.timer` đã bật lại, lượt chạy đầu báo *"Không có gì mới"*.

## File

- `docs/AI_REVIEW_LOAD_TEST_PROD_2026-09-23.md` - mới, báo cáo 11 mục
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` - 1 dòng: số đo + mục đính chính trong ADR-046
- `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md` - mốc checkpoint 2026-09-23, sửa 3 chỗ đã lỗi thời

author: dallman2
body:
> **Stacked on #1**, which is the base branch here. #1 fixes CI by committing the lockfile. Merge #1 first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

## Why

In a growing `Docs/` tree, a new doc gets linked from one place and not from the others. The index doesn't list it, or the sprint plan doesn't point at its retrospective. After that, the only way to find it is to already know the path.

`generate-index.mjs` covers the epic → phase → sprint skeleton, but it writes derived HTML to disk (which goes stale and conflicts across branches), and it only knows the epic tree. It can't tell that an audit or a retrospective belongs somewhere. Asking every author, human or agent, to remember to update every relevant index is exactly the kind of bookkeeping that gets forgotten.

## What

Navigation is **derived at read time** from a link graph, and nothing is written to disk.

| Piece | Does |
|---|---|
| `Docs/scripts/docs-graph.mjs` | Builds the graph: each doc's title and `data-*` metadata, plus its outbound doc links. Incremental: a file is re-parsed only when its mtime changes. `--stats` counts unlisted and unreached docs. |
| `Docs/scripts/serve.mjs` | Serves the graph live at `/_derived/docs-graph.json`. Injects `css/docs-links.js` into every HTML page, so **existing docs need no edits**. Serves a generated listing for a directory with no `index.html`. 301s directory URLs to the trailing-slash form so relative links resolve. |
| `Docs/css/docs-links.js` | Renders under the page's `<article>`: **Also in this directory** on an index (docs and subdirectories the index doesn't link); **Linked from** on any page; **Same sprint, not linked above** on a sprint doc (same `data-epic`, `data-phase` and `data-sprint`). |

Under a plain static server the script finds no graph and renders nothing.

Documented in `AGENTS.md` and the `spiderweb` and `spiderweb-serve` skills. `bootstrap.sh` copies the new script.

### Worth a look in review

- **`serve.mjs` now depends on `linkedom`** (through `docs-graph.mjs`). It was zero-dependency before. linkedom is already a `Docs/scripts` dependency and bootstrap installs it; the serve skill now says so.
- **Stricter path check:** it now requires a path separator after the docs root, so a sibling directory such as `/Docs-other/` can no longer pass the prefix test.
- **Behaviour change:** a directory URL without a trailing slash now redirects to the slash form. Before, the page was served at the slash-less URL, where its relative links broke.
- **Relationship to `generate-index.mjs`:** the two coexist. Its generated pages get the same panels, which show anything the generator didn't list. Whether to eventually replace committed index generation with this is a separate question.

## Tests

100 pass: the 88 from #1 plus 12 new.
- `docs-graph`: href resolution, metadata, templates skipped, backlinks, unlisted children, incremental cache.
- `serve`, against the real server: the graph endpoint, exactly one script injection, the generated listing, the redirect, and a traversal attempt.
- `docs-links.js`, run under linkedom against a real graph.

Two mutation checks: disabling injection, and inverting the sprint-mate match. Each fails a test.

**End to end:** I bootstrapped a fresh repo from this branch, added a retro no index lists, and loaded pages in headless Chrome. The sprint plan showed *Linked from* (its phase index) and *Same sprint* (the retro). The phase page showed *Also in this directory* with the sprint directory its index doesn't link.

author: mominbinshahid
body:
Momin's idea, and his argument for the shape: writing every definition into the sentence that uses it makes the screens verbose — *"if we started doing inline for everything, then it will be so verbose"* — so the sentence stays short and the explanation sits behind the word.

```
Check ketones now. If ketones are present…
      ˙˙˙˙˙˙˙                                ← tap
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ ketones                              │
   │ When there is not enough insulin,     │
   │ the body burns fat for energy…        │
   └──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

`[[key]]` inside a copy string becomes the tappable word. The marker lives in the **copy**, not the markup, for the reason `mgdl` and `timestamp` do: a component cannot reach the translation, and Urdu marks «اسٹیکنگ» where English marks "stacking" only because somebody wrote both.

### Which makes the pairing checkable
That is the part worth having — a component that *guessed* which words to underline could not be tested at all. Three tests hold it:
- both languages mark the same keys in the same places
- every marked key has an entry to open
- **no Urdu entry is short enough to be a bare transliteration** — «اسٹیکنگ» and «کریکشن» are English words in Urdu letters, pronounceable and empty to exactly the reader the entry is for

### Seven entries, and the first two are why this exists
An audit found **`ketones` used at three points in the dose flow with no definition anywhere, in either language** — and `docs/URDU.md` conceding the reader may not know the word. **`ketoacidosis`** shipped as a bare transliteration against an unresolved glossary question. Both are now explained, one tap from where they appear.

The other five: stacking, correction, carbohydrate, diabetes, background insulin. The last two already had *inline* glosses in the Urdu — the right instinct — so those sentences can now shorten rather than every sentence growing.

### The underline was measured before it was chosen
Nastaliq has **zero ink below the baseline** — it climbs rather than descends, which is why it needs 2.3 line-height — so a dotted underline collides with nothing in any of the four faces. `--ink-2` and not the accent, because teal already means "this is the number you came for".

The panel sits **over** the screen rather than replacing it: the reader is mid-task and the result they are reading expires, so a screen change would cost them their place for a definition.

Verified end to end in Urdu. `check-plan.py` clean · smoke clean · **910 tests**.

body:
## What & why

PR #1444 ("Fleet Studio") was squash-merged into `feature/free-tier-fleet` (commit `6df5c515`), then **orphaned** when the branch was rebased onto `main` and force-pushed — the merged code ended up on no branch (`6df5c515` dangling; the signature files were absent from both `origin/feature/free-tier-fleet` and `origin/main`). #1444 is `MERGED` and GitHub will not reopen a merged PR, so this PR **re-lands** the work.

This is a faithful cherry-pick of the exact reviewed + CI-green squash `6df5c515` onto the current main-rebased tip (`ef8cf3cf`). The only non-mechanical change: `packages/app-bundle/manifest.json` was regenerated from the overlay tree via `refresh_manifest.mjs`, so it reflects the merged file set instead of either side's stale copy.

## Provenance

- **Re-lands:** #1444 (merged, then orphaned by a post-merge force-push)
- **Parent PRD:** #1436 — slices #1438, #1439, #1440, #1441, #1442 (all still open)
- Recovery sources anchored locally so they can't be GC'd: squash `6df5c515` (branch `recovered-1444-merge`) and PR head `57caa541` (branch `opencode/fleet-studio-1436`)

## Verification (this branch)

- **Fast suite:** 270 files / 4372 passed / 0 failed — **+96 tests** vs the bare base branch (the recovered fleet-studio suites, present and passing)
- **Drift gate:** PASS — manifest in sync with the overlay (845 files)
- **Engine typecheck:** clean — only the three #1229-allowlisted base-drift errors, no new ones
- No conflict markers anywhere; both ADRs (0031 Fleet Studio, 0032 peer-trust credential) and all 13 fleet-studio source files present

## ⚠️ Known gap — not yet wired into the runtime (follow-up)

This restores #1444 **exactly as it was merged**, including its unfinished wiring. The following slices are implemented and unit-tested but **not connected to the live dispatch/render path**, so the unified UI does not yet render or function:

- **Slice 3** — `session_multiplexer.ts` has no non-test caller; live dispatch still uses the single attachment pointer.

author: airiness
body:
## Summary

Upgrade GGLab's directional shadow system from a single shadow map to a stable, diagnosable cascaded shadow implementation.

This PR completes the first **Shadow 2.0** milestone and uses the Coastal Atrium rendering baseline as the primary validation scene.

## Highlights

* Add up to four directional shadow cascades
* Add practical cascade splitting with configurable uniform/logarithmic blending
* Add cascade overlap and smooth transition blending
* Add shadow-distance fade
* Add stable-sphere cascade fitting
* Add texel snapping for improved temporal stability
* Replace the legacy raw rasterizer-bias policy with cascade-aware receiver-side bias
* Add receiver-plane depth correction for PCF sampling
* Store cascades in a `Texture2DArray`
* Add per-cascade shadow-map preview and visualization overlays
* Add replayable temporal diagnostics based on `CAM_ShadowStairs`
* Add per-cascade GPU timing and projection diagnostics

## Shadow frame contract

Introduce `DirectionalShadowFramePlan` as the resolved per-frame directional shadow contract.

Each cascade owns its resolved:

* render view
* render queue
* main-camera split range
* blend region
* projection information
* world-units-per-texel
* receiver bias

Cascade views are flattened into the frame view buffer as a contiguous range rather than consuming fixed `RenderViewID` slots.

All shadow consumers use the same resolved frame state for rendering, GPU upload and diagnostics.

## Bias and filtering

The previous raw rasterizer bias controls have been retired.

Directional shadows now resolve receiver bias from the cascade's actual texel footprint:

`shadow texels → world-space offset → normalized receiver depth`

The shadow producer therefore runs with zero rasterizer depth and slope bias.

PCF filtering additionally evaluates the receiver-plane depth gradient so individual filter taps follow the receiving surface instead of relying on increasingly large constant bias.

The current filtering kernel remains 3×3 PCF.

## RenderGraph

CSM introduced the first real requirement for multiple passes to write independent array slices of the same RenderGraph texture.

The RenderGraph compiler now tracks texture producers per:

* mip
* array slice
* aspect

Partial writes replace only their declared subresources while preserving dependencies for untouched contents. Overlapping WAR/WAW ordering and exported texture dependencies are handled at the same granularity.

Contract tests cover both single-cascade and four-cascade shadow graphs.

## Diagnostics

The Shadow Inspector now exposes:

* cascade split ranges
* transition regions
* stable/tight fitting mode
* texel-snapping state
* projection extent
* world units per texel
* snapped and unsnapped light-space centers
* resolved receiver bias
* per-cascade draw statistics
* selected array-layer preview
* per-cascade GPU timing

Optional overlays visualize:

* blue / green / orange / purple — cascade regions
* yellow — cascade transition regions
* pink — shadow-distance fade

A deterministic `CAM_ShadowStairs` replay path records adjacent-frame projection movement, texel-scale changes and texel-grid alignment for temporal stability analysis.

author: mtibbits
body:
## Summary

Today the only guard on the six auto-exec commands (`analyze`, `branch`, `cleanup`,
`commit`, `mergetoall`, `sync`) is a header comment in
`tests/skills-no-bang-exec.bats`. Nothing asserts it, so a command silently
converted off the auto-exec path, or a stray bang-exec line landing in a seventh
command, would both go green. This PR adds the positive counterpart to #550's
negative canary, in the same file, reusing `_bang_exec_re`:

- **@test 7** pins the exact carrier set. It is the only test that catches a
  seventh carrier.
- **@test 8** pins exactly one bang-exec line per command.
- **@test 9** pins the column-0 convention.
- **@test 10** is an anti-vacuity fixture covering column-0, indented,
  markdown-image and clean inputs, a missing subject, and the value of the
  column-0 regex.

`_bang_exec_re` is indent-tolerant. That is safe for #550's offender hunt but
fail-open for a positive pin, so @test 9 uses a column-0 form. That form is
*derived* from `_bang_exec_re` rather than spelled out again, so a later grammar
change carries through. @test 9 is framed as a convention pin: it makes no claim
about whether the harness would expand an indented or fenced `!` line. The
header now names those shapes, and commands in subdirectories of `commands/`
(the scan is one level deep), as unpinned. The six expected names live in one
`_auto_exec_cmds` literal that @test 7, 8 and 9 all assert against.

One deviation from the plan came out of quality review: the new per-command
counter and #550's `_bang_offenders` shared a copy of the #337 rc-precise
`grep -c` loop. They now go through one `_bang_counts` / `_bang_carriers` pair,
and `_bang_offenders` is a one-line wrapper, so #550's tests are unchanged.
The review and red-team minors were applied in two follow-up commits,
`test: address review minors …` and `test: address red-team minors …`.

**Suggested squash title:** `test(596): positive pin on the six bang-exec commands`.
The first commit's body is only a devdoc pointer, so please use this PR's summary
as the squash body.

## Related issues

Closes #596
Related: #550 (the negative canary this complements; its grammar-broadening and
`agents/*.md` deferrals stay open)

## Testing

- `bats tests/skills-no-bang-exec.bats`: 10/10 (was 6).
- **Mutation matrix.** AC2 names 3 mutations; this PR ran 5. It ran in a scratch
  copy, never the live plugin tree. The red/green vector over @test 7-10 for
  each row, at the final file content:

  | Row | Mutation | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
  |-----|----------|---|---|---|----|
  | M1 | delete `sync.md`'s bang line | RED | RED | RED | green |
  | M2 | duplicate `analyze.md`'s bang line at column 0 | green | RED | RED | green |
  | M2b | add an *indented* duplicate to `analyze.md` | green | **RED** | green | green |
  | M3 | append an inert `` !`true` `` to `draft.md` | **RED** | green | green | green |
  | M4 | indent `branch.md`'s bang line | green | green | **RED** | green |

  M2b, M3 and M4 each isolate a single leg. @test 1-6 stayed green in every row.
- **#550 regression controls through the refactored helper:**
  - A bang line planted in a `core-*` SKILL.md reddens @test 5 only.
  - A missing or unreadable SKILL.md makes `_bang_offenders` return rc 2.
- **shellcheck.** There are no SC2314 hits across `tests/*.bats`. Diff-scoped
  analyze: 0 new findings. The one warning in the file, SC2120 on the unchanged
  `_user_invocable_skills`, predates this PR.
- **Cost.** This file's run time went from 0.55s to 0.86s.

body:
## Summary

Finds and renames every production `helpers.rs`/`utils.rs` module still on `main` (plus `examples/adaptive_beamforming_refactored.rs`) to a name that states its actual concern, derived from current content — not blindly copied from the stale `codex/kwavers-aequitas-sequencer` branch's proposal where that branch's content has since diverged from `main`.

- **kwavers-physics**: `analytical/utils` → `validation`, `fusion/algorithms/utils` → `registration`, `monte_carlo/utils` → `scatter`
- **kwavers-python**: every per-binding `helpers.rs` (mems, breast_fwi, simulation_py, source_py, theranostic_bindings) → `py_convert.rs` — one consistent name for the private binding-layer parsing/conversion role each submodule already plays
- **kwavers-solver**: `conservation/helpers` → `energy`, `elastography/helpers` → `analytical`, `volume_operator/helpers` → `geometry`, `gradient/utils` → `norm`, `photoacoustic/utils` → `reconstruction_ops`, `time_reversal/utils` → `focus`, `numerical_accuracy/helpers` → `laplacian`
- **kwavers-therapy**: `abdominal3d/helpers` → `coord_convert`, `cavitation/helpers` → `grid_ops`, `waveform/utils` → `indexing`
- **kwavers-transducer**: `focused/utils` → `factory`
- **kwavers**: `examples/adaptive_beamforming_refactored.rs` → `examples/adaptive_beamforming.rs` (`_refactored` is a naming-prohibited quality/history marker; no `adaptive_beamforming.rs` existed to collide with). Consolidates the duplicate book chapter — keeps the fuller `adaptive_beamforming.md`, deletes the thinner duplicate, repoints `SUMMARY.md` and `examples/README.md`.

Scope: matches from `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -E "(helpers|utils)\.rs$|_refactored\.rs$"`, excluding test-directory and `#[cfg(test)]`-gated helper modules (out of scope per the source branch's own stated intent — "production modules") and directory-form `utils/`/`helpers/` modules that don't match the `*.rs` file suffix (e.g. `pstd/utils/`, `simulation_py/run/helpers/` — different, untouched entities).

Every `mod`/`use` site is updated in the same commit; `git grep` for each old module path returns nothing. No re-export shims.

Source: `codex/kwavers-aequitas-sequencer` (tip `a141b90fde`) proposed most of this in `7427c28896` and `0f5d711913`, but never merged. Names are re-derived where that branch's content has since diverged from `main` (e.g. `photoacoustic/utils` → `reconstruction_ops` here rather than the branch's `shared_ops`, matching what the module actually computes: distance/back-projection-weight/forward-model construction for reconstruction).

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — clean on `kwavers-python`, `kwavers-solver`, `kwavers-transducer`. `kwavers-physics`, `kwavers-therapy`, and `kwavers` carry pre-existing `-D warnings` violations (mostly `println!` in unrelated test/example files) in files this PR does not touch — confirmed by diffing the flagged files against this branch's changed-file list. This matches CI's own `Code Quality` job, which runs the general clippy pass as `|| true` for exactly this reason.
- `cargo clippy -p kwavers-solver --features pinn --all-targets -- -D unused` — clean (CI's PINN-specific clippy gate)
- `cargo nextest run --locked` across all six affected packages — 3486 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --doc --locked` — passed on every package that supports doctests (`kwavers-python` is a `cdylib`, doctests not applicable)
- `python3 scripts/lockfile.py --check` — clean (`Cargo.lock` untouched; this PR is pure Rust renames)

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p <pkg> --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` for each affected package (pre-existing unrelated debt noted above)
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p <pkg> --locked` for each affected package
- [x] `cargo test --doc -p <pkg> --locked` for each affected package
- [x] `scripts/lockfile.py --check`

This PR performs a systematic refactoring that renames all `helpers.rs` and `utils.rs` modules across the codebase to names that better reflect their actual concerns. For example, `helpers.rs` modules become `py_convert.rs` in Python bindings (to indicate their conversion role), `utils` in physics becomes `validation` or `scatter` (matching their domain), and solver helper modules are renamed to `energy`, `analytical`, `geometry`, `norm`, `reconstruction_ops`, etc. The PR also consolidates a duplicate `adaptive_beamforming` example by removing the `_refactored` suffix. Every import site is updated in the same commits with no behavioral changes, re-export shims, or test modifications—this is purely a naming/organization refactor.

author: kriscoleman
body:
## Why

Con-voyage's model story was a single hardcoded `provider = "opus"` on all 16 reviewer agents — which silently required every consuming city to define an `opus` provider, put review compute on the most expensive claude tier, and had no answer for two provider-side failure modes that bead-level watchdogs can't see: **claude usage/rate limits** (a capped session looks alive but produces nothing) and **context auto-compaction** landing mid-task.

## What

### Three-tier model architecture

All work is ranked by task complexity into **small / medium / large**, with a fixed claude ↔ opencode equivalency:

| Tier | Kind of work | claude | opencode (pack default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| small | rudimentary | haiku | `minimax-m3` |
| medium | standard | sonnet | `glm-5p3-flash` |
| large | critical / intensive | opus | `kimi-k3` |

- `pack.toml` now **ships three tier provider presets** (`cv-review-light` / `cv-review-standard` / `cv-review-intensive`) on `builtin:opencode`, so the pack is self-contained — casting it into any city yields working reviewers.
- The 16 `cv-*` lenses move onto the tier matching their reasoning depth: **6 intensive** (security, code, Go/Frontend PE, data/db, api-platform), **6 standard** (QA, SRE, compliance, product-owner, founder-cto, dev-ex), **4 light** (janitor, docs, marketing, design-ux).
- The claude side of the split (opus mayor, sonnet workers) stays where it belongs: **city config**, since those role agents are providerless and inherit city defaults.
- **Everything is a default and overridable**: a city redeclares the same provider name in `city.toml` (city loads before packs, city wins) or moves a single lens with `[[patches.agent]]`.

### `con-voyage-lookout` — rate-limit circuit breaker + compact handoffs

New city-scoped monitor order (5m cooldown) that peeks every active claude-backed session:

- **Compact approaching** (pane advertises ≤15% context left) → proactive `gc handoff --target`: the worker restarts fresh with its own handoff mail waiting, *ahead* of the reactive PreCompact hook path.
- **Limit signature observed** → **circuit breaker opens**: fleet-wide handoff (context preserved for when limits clear) + throttled escalation mail to the mayor naming the all-opencode fallback pools per tier, with the fleet's trailing-hour `usage.jsonl` burn attached. Auto-closes with an all-clear mail after a limit-free reset window.
- All knobs (`CV_LOOKOUT_*`: claude provider names, thresholds, cooldowns, reset/remind windows, fallback pool names) are env-overridable via `[[orders.overrides]]`.
- The mayor orchestration fragment gains the **all-opencode fallback runbook** (re-sling to fallback pools, durable city.toml switch, all-clear return) plus two new red flags.

### gc 1.4.2 compatibility note

The installed gc predates open provider options (`flag_template`): its builtin opencode model catalog is a closed list, and unknown `option_defaults` values hard-fail config load. Each tier therefore re-declares the `model` option with an explicit choice carrying `flag_args` (`options_schema_merge = "by_key"`). Verified against the real binary: `gc config explain/show` load clean, all 16 cv-* agents resolve to their tiers, and implicit per-rig fallback pools (`<rig>/kimi-k3`, `<rig>/glm-5p3-flash`, `<rig>/minimax-m3`) materialize.

## Testing

- `tests/con-voyage-lookout.test.sh` — 11 hermetic cases against a stubbed gc: healthy no-op, compact handoff + cooldown, breaker trip (fleet handoff + escalation content), remind throttling, reset-window all-clear, opencode sessions ignored, closed sessions skipped, env coercion, usage-summary attachment, handoff-failure fail-safe, preflight failure.
- `tests/model-tiers.test.sh` — pins the tier contract: every reviewer binds a declared tier, exact lens↔tier membership, pack provider defaults (base/model/`flag_args` choice), lookout order wiring + city scope.
- Full mold suite, `ailloy temper`, `ailloy assay`, shellcheck, md-links all green; `ailloy cast` smoke-tested.

Companion city-side PR (fallback pools + recast): kriscoleman/repl_city (feat/model-tiers-lookout).

author: crispstrobe
body:
`i18n.svelte` merges the bundle as `{ ...terms, ...messages }`, so
`messages` wins where both carry a key. Fifty-nine keys are in both;
fifty-seven agree. The two that did not had been recorded as undecided,
and they are not the same kind of problem.

`limewater` was one English word doing two jobs — the substance, and the
test for it. `terms` said Kalkwasser, `messages` said Kalkwasserprobe, and
`messages` won, so a bottle on the shelf carried the name of a test.
`data/kids/experiments-v1.json` lists `limewater` as an INGREDIENT of the
breath test, so that name was reaching a materials list; you do not pour a
test into a beaker. No German could have been right, because the English
was ambiguous — so the fix is not a choice between two translations but a
source-text change: the test has its own English now, through
`gasTests.ts`, and `limewater` goes back to being the substance.

That map also settles a second drift nobody had noticed. Two vocabularies
reached `t()` for the same four tests — the Inspector's command words
(`splint`, `litmus`) and the engine's tokens (`glowing_splint`,
`damp_litmus`) — and both components now read one map, so they cannot
name the same test two ways.

`invisible ink boundary` was the other kind: one meaning with two German
renderings, and the winner dropped the word the lesson is named for. Its
five sibling boundary lessons all read "Grenze …", so the `terms` entry
was right and the duplicate was deleted.

The guard generalises it without enumerating the 248 `t()` call sites that
take a variable — too many to be useful, and the dangerous ones all leave
the same trace. The two sections mean different things, and that is what
makes it decidable: `terms` is the ENGINE's vocabulary, keyed by its own
identifiers, so `ethyl_acetate` and `naked_egg` belong there; `messages`
is the INTERFACE's own English. A snake_case key in `messages` is a wire
token that reached `t()` and got translated instead of being given a name.

It found five: `glowing_splint` and `damp_litmus`, the gas-test tokens
behind the collision, and `naked_egg`, `cut_apple` and `fatty_soap`, which
are registry canonical_keys filed in the wrong section. The
recorded-collisions list in `locale-collision-lint.py` is empty for the
first time, and an empty list is the claim rather than the absence of one.

author: iluzdaf
body:
## Summary

- The application read the wall clock three ways: `glfwGetTime` for the frame, a chrono helper of its own for the profiled sections, and `timePhase` in `timing/frame_profile` read chrono directly. A `Stopwatch` in `timing` now does all of it. It starts when built, reports the seconds since, and a lap restarts it, so read once per frame it is the frame's time. The frame lap is read straight into the profile and the fixed step takes the value from there.
- Six readers subtracted an optional stamp from the world's simulation time by hand, each first checking the stamp was set. `World::secondsSince` does that once: nothing without a stamp, the age otherwise, and a stamp ahead of the clock is rejected as it already is when an actor or exit is added. The readers now only compare the age to their window. One behaviour change: the NPC hearing check used to ignore a future shot stamp and now throws like the rest of the world's stamp validation.
- The two timing tests that spun the clock share one `spinFor` helper under `tests/support`.

- [x] Debug build with warnings as errors

author: oddurs
body:
Closes cairn 0091.

- **The five border sets** as eleven named slots each (`horizontal`, `tee-down`, `cross`…), keyed to the junction table the engine uses. A theme names one as `current` and keeps the rest available.
- **Marks, blocks, the eight-step bar, the ten braille spinner frames** — the characters a UI makes when colour alone will not do.
- **Attributes:** bold is a weight, dim is a colour (not an opacity), underline is a thickness and offset. Reverse has no value: it is a swap.
- **Every glyph is one cell**, asserted with the engine's own `wcwidth` rather than by eye.
- **Type pairings are monospace now** — `system`, `jetbrains`, `ibm-plex`, `berkeley`. They still named Inter and Figtree, which cannot hold a grid, and `ch` in a proportional face means nothing. The metric-matched Inter fallback goes too: the system mono stack is already there.
- **`borderSet`** joins the theme inputs; the workbench renders in JetBrains Mono.

body:
## What you'll see
- **A CRM phone app** (new `mobile/` folder). It opens the normal CRM, so every CRM update reaches the app with no app-store update needed.
- In the app, once someone is **clocked in**, location keeps being shared **with the phone locked or in a pocket**. Arrivals at jobs are logged, and the Team Map stays live.
- On Android, an **"On the clock"** notification shows while sharing. Sharing still stops the moment they clock out or start a break.
- If location is blocked for the app, the "On the clock" pill turns orange and offers **Open settings**.
- In a normal phone browser, nothing changes: location is shared only while the CRM is on screen.

## Try it on Android now (no Google account needed)
1. On this PR, open the **"Android App (test build)"** check, then **Summary**, then **Artifacts**, and download **ai-build-pros-crm-android**.
2. Unzip it and send `app-debug.apk` to an Android phone. Open it and allow "install unknown apps" when asked.
3. Sign in, go to **Time Clock**, and tap **Clock in**. When asked, allow location **"All the time"** and notifications.
4. Lock the phone and drive to an appointment address. The office's Team Map should keep updating.

## Still needed from you (for the app stores)
- **Apple Developer account** ($99/year) and **a Mac with Xcode** to build and ship the iPhone app.
- **Google Play developer account** ($25 once) to publish on Android.
- The app uses the default Capacitor icon for now.

## How it works
- The app loads crm.aibuildpros.com inside a Capacitor 7 shell, with the free `@capacitor-community/background-geolocation` plugin.
- The existing location sharer detects the app. It takes fixes from the plugin and posts them through the phone's native connection, because Android slows down web requests in the background. It still posts to `/api/location`, and the database still refuses location from anyone who isn't clocked in.
- **SQL to run: no.**

## Proofs
- The new rule for when a fix gets sent was tested first (`send-policy.test.ts`).
- `npm test` passes (927), `npm run lint` shows only the one baseline warning, and the type check passes.
- The **Android build is proven by this PR's "Android App (test build)" check**: this sandbox can't download Android's build tools. I haven't tested the app on a real phone, and the iPhone build has never been compiled.

author: vladroja
body:
## Resumen

Corrige un bug detectado en pruebas de Contact Center donde un mismo caso podía terminar con dos citas `SCHEDULED` activas.

### Backend
- `create_appointment()` bloquea el caso con `FOR UPDATE`.
- Antes de insertar revisa si ya existe una cita `SCHEDULED` para el caso.
- Si existe, responde validación y obliga a usar **Reagendar**.
- No requiere migración.

### Frontend
- La ficha detecta la cita programada vigente.
- Cuando existe, deja de mostrar el formulario **Agendar cita**.
- En su lugar muestra la cita activa y botón **Gestionar cita**.
- `scheduleAppointment()` también tiene una defensa local para no intentar crear otra.

### Pruebas
- Contrato backend para una sola cita activa por caso.
- Contrato frontend para ocultar el alta cuando ya existe una cita `SCHEDULED`.

### Dato de prueba existente
Las dos citas que ya se crearon en producción durante la prueba no se modifican automáticamente. Después de desplegar esta corrección se puede cancelar la cita de prueba anterior y conservar la vigente.

author: sherintg
body:
A dfs_obj_t caches a single (parent_oid, name) pair. For a hardlinked inode that pair is only one of the names the inode is reachable by, and it can be removed or renamed while the inode stays alive through another link. dfuse keeps one dfs_obj_t per inode and shares it across every name, so once the cached name was dropped, metadata operations on the handle failed with ENOENT even though the file still exists.

The authoritative metadata of a hardlinked inode already lives in the GIT object keyed by OID; only the callers had not been updated. Three paths resolved the object through obj->parent_oid/obj->name before consulting the hardlink bit:

  - entry_stat() fetched the parent dentry first, which made both dfs_ostat() and dfs_osetattr() depend on the cached name.
  - dfs_ostat() and dfs_osetattr() opened the parent object unconditionally.
  - dfs_link() re-read the source dentry under the transaction.

Route all three through GIT by OID when the handle carries the hardlink bit, so no parent handle is opened and no dentry is consulted. The parent handle is now opened only on the dentry path and closed conditionally. Behaviour for objects without the hardlink bit is unchanged.

Also propagate the hardlink bit in dfs_obj_copy_attr(). dfuse calls it during lookup to salvage state from a freshly resolved object into the retained inode object before discarding the former; without this, a handle that predates a conversion performed by another client keeps a stale mode and falls back to the dentry path. The bit is only ever set, never cleared, matching the design in which the last surviving link keeps its hardlink bit and its GIT record.

set_chunk_size() still resolves by name, so
dfs_file_update_chunk_size() on a hardlinked file writes the chunk size to the dentry instead of GIT. open_file() reads it back from the same dentry, so the two remain consistent. Both will be fixed together as part of DAOS-19527.

Test: DFS_UNIT_TEST35 opens a file, hardlinks it, removes the name the handle was opened by, and verifies that stat (sync and async), read, write, all four xattr operations, dfs_osetattr for mode/uid/gid, mtime and size, and dfs_link all keep working through the now nameless handle, with every change observable through the surviving link. It repeats the checks for a handle whose name was renamed away rather than removed, and confirms that every operation returns ENOENT once the last link is gone.

Allow-unstable-test: true

author: vincentkoc
body:
Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156203

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tool registration and resolution repeatedly rebuild or scan the same declared-name membership. Large tool sets pay this work for each registration and each resolved tool.

## User Impact

Reduces repeated work for large plugin tool sets without changing tool availability, declaration validation, factory freshness, or returned order. This is a scaling repair, not a universal CPU or memory improvement: the common 35-tool batch case uses more warm CPU, and the 512-tool individual-registration case has higher phase RSS.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one lazy, detached, trim-only and case-sensitive declaration Set per PluginRecord. Share it across that record's registrations, attaching it after PluginInstance wraps callable fields. Prepare raw media-name membership lazily once per plugin resolution. Keep the host array helper, produced-name arrays, unnamed-registration fallback, conflict short-circuit, and current factory/lifecycle behavior.

The declaration Set remains live with its registrations. The raw media Set is rebuilt per resolution; unnamed registrations materialize an availability array. These allocations have costs. The measured RSS differences do not identify retained objects or prove a leak, and this change makes no allocation-only or net-memory claim.

## Evidence

[Retained native baseline/candidate proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35819884239) used the real PluginInstance registration API and prepared-runtime tool resolution on Node 24.19.0 / Linux x64. Before the subsequent test-only corrections, candidate passed all 261 leaves across six files; baseline passed 258 and failed the three intended regression assertions. Both arms have the same leaf inventory, including duplicate-title multiplicity. Three baseline fixture emission bindings adapt only the original private array representation; assertion/input order is unchanged. Eight functional commands and twelve measurement workers completed, with matched source/dependency endpoints and complete owned-process/provider closeout. A preceding timed-out attempt contributes no functional or measurement credit.

Independent review of the production change found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The measured production logic remains unchanged. Later changes are formatter line wrapping, an explicit return type for a deliberately throwing test getter, and a verbatim extraction of the optional-tool registry fixture into a sibling test helper. The fixture extraction preserves every test body, assertion and hook order. The Gateway persistence test now waits for main's canonical exact-claim settlement notification, asserts no persistence warnings, and verifies the stored failure receipt before checking the clear-requested owner state. It retains the blocked-writer assertion and original case order; the superseded persistence spy is removed. The retained functional proof predates these test corrections; fresh scoped reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

[Historical CI for PR head `128fbd9250a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35823690163) and native hosted preparation passed. The CI checkout was merge `2958af493ef20c107a5d6eb6e7ba25cba17ef753` (PR head `128fbd9250a745293737d81bb2d14ca02ac82be3` with base `80bab7e23ce05a0cf68f4f54d38f8702d0238d35`), using Node 24.19.0 / Linux x64 and Vitest 5.0.0. Actual shard plans and test output confirm the [full persistence file: 9/9 cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35823690163/job/107061159183), [persistence-owner sibling: 13/13](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35823690163/job/107061156883), and [run-failure sibling: 23/23](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35823690163/job/107061156848) passed. The persistence file ran in its original case order, including the blocked-writer and repaired settled-failure case; the repaired block is unchanged in that merge checkout. The required combined `openclaw/ci-gate` status and native merge verification subsequently passed for that head. A later conflict with main's settlement-notification repair was resolved by integrating pinned main `2e9a2eceb11bd937a64dc01fb7894ff23eb80ef7`, retaining its canonical notification and the failure-receipt assertion. Signed integration head `9ddc44ce6165069cc127c8b0236cab764fe014ef` preserves the original PR ancestry. Its [core type-check job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35829115452/job/107077648933) then failed on a UI route-loader type error. The failing file is byte-identical in the pinned main, CI base, PR head and CI merge. The canonical [main fix `813a10e7deb`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/813a10e7deb628a71d11c883636e9281a7911ac3) is integrated in signed head `0916cdf9d29f32e12c662fd647017bda6100c66b`. All 11 PR files and the main-relative PR diff remain byte-identical; the existing scoped source review applies. Final-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35830437785) and native hosted preparation passed for `0916cdf9d29f32e12c662fd647017bda6100c66b`. A separate [native focused run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35836696601) passed the complete persistence file, 9/9 cases in original order, including blocked-writer, queued end/cancellation/settled-failure and native cancellation cases. Exact head/tree/file, frozen installation, Node 24.19.0 / Linux x64, pnpm 12.4.0 and Vitest 5.0.0 were verified, with stable source endpoints and complete provider/process/source/install closeout. Current CI also proves the [persistence-owner sibling: 13/13](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35830437785/job/107081839658). The earlier 45-case results, including run-failure 23/23, remain historical evidence for their stated merge checkout.

Untimed delegated-work counts are separate from timing. At 512 tools, 100 warm resolutions replace 26,214,400 declaration-array entries with 51,200 Set membership calls. Individual registration reads the declaration source 512 times on baseline and once on candidate (262,144 versus 512 entries). Raw media checks replace 51,200 Array.includes calls with one Set construction per resolution reading 51,200 source entries; native includes comparison counts were not measured.

Timing uses five same-ordinal serial AB/BA pairs, each worker running all eight rows in the same order. Individual means separate registrations; batch means one factory registration producing the tool set. After 25 warmups, each warm interval contains 100 resolutions. The table reports the median of the five paired percentage changes (candidate versus baseline), not a ratio of arm medians.

| Tools | Registration shape | Warm wall | Warm CPU |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | Individual | +6.99% | +6.46% |
| 0 | Batch | -0.55% | -0.32% |
| 1 | Individual | +2.61% | -6.21% |
| 1 | Batch | +2.69% | +5.27% |
| 35 | Individual | -23.01% | -3.07% |
| 35 | Batch | -2.81% | +5.43% |
| 512 | Individual | -49.71% | -42.92% |
| 512 | Batch | -51.41% | -46.29% |

Both 512-tool shapes improve warm wall and CPU in all five pairs. Tiny rows have mixed signs. The 35-tool batch warm CPU is higher in every pair (+2.56% to +77.97%); its paired median increase is 8.524 ms per 100 resolutions.

Registration, first resolution, warmup, imports and fixture/setup are distinct phases. The 512-tool batch registration total (first plus remaining registration intervals) rises by paired medians of 1.568 ms wall and 8.051 ms CPU, higher in all five pairs. Its first resolution improves by paired medians of 12.730 ms wall and 22.140 ms CPU. These phase medians are not summed into a net estimate.

Memory is mixed. After the 512-tool individual row's warm phase, paired current RSS rises by a median 142.45 MiB (137.71–182.63); after joined owner/cache disposal it remains higher by 138.94 MiB (129.06–174.90), in all five pairs. Whole-worker peak RSS

## What

Issue #150 asks for 100 percent line coverage of `provenance_map.py`, with tests that document the chosen behaviour for ambiguous raw values inline.

The issue was closed as addressed (commit 41b6408, covering the mapping tables in `tests/test_phase1.py`), but the derived helpers added to that module *after* the close -- `origin_rank`, `clamp_derived_origin`, `provenance_for_run` -- had no callers and no tests, and the string-source and absent-source arms of `derived_provenance_for_events` were never hit. The module sat at 86 percent, so the acceptance criterion was not actually met.

## Change

Adds `tests/test_provenance_map.py` (22 tests) pinning each uncovered helper and recording the chosen behaviour inline:

- an unparsable or missing event source degrades to `EXTERNAL_AGENT`, never to verified
- absent trust information reports `UNKNOWN` rather than being coerced to unverified
- `provenance_for_run` folds archived and live events in sequence order, so an archived agent fact cannot be laundered into `DETERMINISTIC`
- an unreadable archive or live log degrades instead of raising

`provenance_map.py` now reports **100 percent line and branch coverage**.

The 22 new tests move the collected total from 2501 to 2532, so the documented figure is resynced across the ten files the docs guard reads.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_provenance_map.py` -- 22 passed
- `provenance_map.py` coverage 86 percent -> 100 percent (term-missing shows no missing lines or branches)
- `ruff check src/ tests/ examples/`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src/continuum` -- all clean

- types.ts: banking/social_media widened from Record<string, never> to their real confirmed fields (all optional nullable strings; social_media uses facebook/instagram/youtube/twitter exactly, no _url suffix). New ApiIntegrationsUpdate type structurally excludes `configured` (response-only) so sending it is a compile error, not just discipline.

- ApiIntegrationsPanel — the one with real design weight: api_key/ client_secret come back masked from GET and are NEVER seeded into their inputs (both always start empty), so the mask can never be sent back. Each gets its own `edited` flag (separate from the existing blur-based validation `touched`) that flips true on any onChange regardless of resulting value, since "never touched" and "typed then deleted" both look like "" otherwise:
    - not edited        -> field omitted from the PATCH (unchanged)
    - edited, non-empty -> send the new plaintext value
    - edited, empty     -> send null (explicit clear)
  The masked current value shows as static read-only context text next to
  each input, never bound to the field. sms_sender_name/client_id are
  plain optional strings, no special handling.
- page.tsx: 3 panels wired in; Banking's and Social Media's read-view cards
  restored to show real fields (were a stale "coming soon" placeholder from

body:
## Summary

A dead-owner `brain.rvf.lock` made `RvfDualWriter.initialize()` misclassify a healthy RVF store as corrupt: native `open()` returned `LockHeld`, native `create()` returned `FsyncFailed` because the path existed, and the writer quarantined the valid store before rebuilding it empty. This fixes the production failure reported in #574 by reclaiming only a lock with a known dead owner, retrying open, and requiring a known structural open error before any quarantine. The shared and pattern-store recovery paths use the same guard; a failed embedding-space manifest check now closes its opened native handle.

## Verification

- Test-first reproduction on current `main`: the populated-store test failed because `totalVectors` fell from 1 to 0 and the original store was moved to `.corrupt-*`; the manifest-mismatch test failed because `brain.rvf.lock` remained.
- Native RVF integration coverage verifies populated-store preservation, live-owner contention, lock-release/permission races, true corruption behind a stale lock, and native-handle cleanup. The pattern-store fallback has its own dead-owner regression.
- `npx vitest run` on the six focused RVF suites: **91 passed / 91 total**.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` (TypeScript, CLI, MCP), focused ESLint, and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Failure modes

- A live owner or an ambiguous/malformed lock degrades RVF to SQLite rather than moving a potentially healthy store; covered by live-owner and lock-error tests.
- A known structurally corrupt store remains recoverable and its bytes are preserved in quarantine; covered by the existing corruption suite and the new stale-lock corruption test.
- A manifest mismatch disables the dual writer and releases its lock; covered by the new native test.
- The original report is on Windows; this branch was verified against the available macOS native binding. Windows-specific confirmation remains tracked in #574.

Part of FF-25 (backgrounds). A reviewer asked for this change on opf-pptx#66.

The pattern-background examples used `diagStripe`. That id exists only in the preview and has no DrawingML name. opf-pptx#66 exports it as the closest DrawingML preset, `wdUpDiag`, so a PPTX round trip turned `diagStripe` into `wdUpDiag`.

This PR switches the examples to `wdUpDiag` so the name survives the round trip:
- `spec/schemas/opf.schema.json`: the `PatternBackground.pattern.preset` example now reads `["pct5", "ltHorz", "wdUpDiag"]`. The description now says:

## English

### Reason

A rejected DNS zone deletion left its confirmation open, but rendered the failure in the danger card behind the modal. The user therefore saw no explanation in the active workflow and could not confidently decide whether to retry.

### Scope

- Move DNS zone deletion failures into the existing confirmation dialog.
- Preserve the zone name and destructive-action context after rejection.
- Keep the confirmation open and allow an immediate retry.
- Reset a stale deletion error when the confirmation is cancelled or reopened.
- Keep the existing transaction preflight, pending-state protections, task tracking, API request, and post-success navigation unchanged.
- Add desktop and mobile Playwright regression coverage for a rejected deletion followed by a successful retry.

### Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` — passed.
- Tailwind token lint — passed.
- Banned-pattern lint — passed.
- i18n audit — passed.
- CSP audit — passed.
- Production Vite build — passed.
- Focused Playwright, Chromium + mobile Chrome — 2/2 passed.

### Risks and follow-up

- The change affects only error placement and reset behavior; DNS deletion semantics and authorization are unchanged.
- Successful deletion still returns to the DNS zone list and remains tracked through the existing task workflow.
- No server, database, or deployment changes are included.

### Deployment status

Not deployed. This pull request requires human review and merge before any deployment.

## Česky

### Důvod

Zamítnuté smazání DNS zóny ponechalo potvrzení otevřené, chybu ale vykreslilo v danger kartě schované za modálním oknem. Uživatel proto v aktivním workflow neviděl vysvětlení a nemohl spolehlivě rozhodnout, zda má akci zopakovat.

### Rozsah

- Chyba smazání DNS zóny se přesouvá přímo do stávajícího potvrzovacího dialogu.
- Po zamítnutí zůstane zachovaný název zóny i kontext nebezpečné operace.
- Potvrzení zůstane otevřené a akci lze okamžitě zopakovat.
- Zastaralá chyba smazání se vyčistí při zrušení nebo novém otevření potvrzení.
- Stávající kontrola probíhajících transakcí, ochrana pending stavu, sledování úloh, API požadavek i navigace po úspěchu zůstávají beze změny.
- Doplněn je regresní Playwright test pro desktop i mobil, který ověřuje zamítnuté smazání a následné úspěšné opakování.

### Ověření

- `tsc --noEmit` — prošel.
- Kontrola Tailwind tokenů — prošla.
- Kontrola zakázaných vzorů — prošla.
- i18n audit — prošel.
- CSP audit — prošel.
- Produkční Vite build — prošel.
- Cílený Playwright, Chromium + mobilní Chrome — 2/2 prošly.

### Rizika a návaznosti

- Změna upravuje pouze umístění a reset chyby; význam smazání DNS zóny ani autorizace se nemění.
- Úspěšné smazání dál vrací uživatele na seznam DNS zón a používá stávající sledování úloh.
- PR neobsahuje změny serveru, databáze ani nasazení.

Nenasazeno. Pull request vyžaduje lidskou kontrolu a sloučení před jakýmkoli nasazením.

author: cyptopimpinainteazy
body:
## **User description** Three components hash Bitcoin headers and walk merkle proofs: this pallet's `btc_gateway`, `crates/x3-bitcoin-vault`, and `crates/x3-crosschain-intent`. The matrix called the duplication "a standing drift risk". A test that feeds **one real block to all three** says it was worse than a risk: ## The vault was verifying a different tree `x3-bitcoin-vault::verify_merkle_proof` had no transaction index and instead put whichever of `(node, sibling)` compared **numerically smaller** first. Bitcoin's tree concatenates by *position* — the left child first, read from the low bits of the index — so this is a different tree. It accepted the leftmost transaction whenever the leaf happened to be the smaller of the two (the only case its tests covered) and **rejected valid proofs for every other position**. It is the same defect `x3-settlement-engine` fixed as C-009, still live in a second implementation because nothing had ever shown the two the same block. Found by running the agreement test rather than by reading either implementation: the pallet reconstructed the real root from a real regtest block's proof, and the vault called the same proof invalid. - `verify_merkle_proof(txid, tx_index, merkle_root, proof)` reads the direction from the position, exactly as the pallet does. - `verify_deposit_spv` takes the position as a parameter — it is part of the proof, not an optimisation. - `merkle_proof_is_position_aware_not_value_sorted` is the regression: a two-leaf tree whose left leaf is numerically *larger* than its sibling, verified at index 0, at index 1, and refused at the wrong position. - `the_three_bitcoin_header_implementations_agree` pins all three to the same 32 bytes for that block, and the pallet's and vault's walks to the same verdict. The byte-order convention is asserted in **both** directions, because the intent crate's doc comment claimed display order while returning wire order — also fixed. `x3-bitcoin-vault` becomes a dev-dependency of the pallet, which is what lets one test compare them; the lockfile edge moved with it. ## Verification `cargo test -p pallet-x3-settlement-engine` = 158 + 23; `cargo test -p x3-bitcoin-vault` = 24; clippy and `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `feature_matrix.py check` and `check-readiness-consistency.sh` pass. Runtime re-attested: two srtool builds of `7ea1819169` agree, and the hashes are **identical to the previous revision's** — the vault is a dev-dependency and the intent change is a comment, so nothing the runtime instantiates moved. That is the second revision in a row where only `recorded_revision` changed. Matrix blocker updated: the three implementations are now tested against each other, which is how the divergence was found; consolidating them into one would remove the risk rather than detect it. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `x3-bitcoin-vault`'s merkle proof verification, which was validating against a different tree and rejecting valid proofs for every transaction position except the leftmost. - `verify_merkle_proof` now takes `tx_index` and reads the concatenation direction from the position's low bits, matching the pallet's walk. - Adds `merkle_proof_is_position_aware_not_value_sorted` as a regression test for a tree whose left leaf is numerically larger than its sibling. - Adds `the_three_bitcoin_header_implementations_agree` pinning the pallet, `x3-bitcoin-vault`, and `x3-crosschain-intent` to the same bytes and merkle verdict for one real regtest block; `x3-bitcoin-vault` becomes a dev-dependency of the pallet to enable this. - Fixes the intent crate's doc comment, which claimed display byte order while the code returns wire order. Runtime hashes re-attested at `7ea1819169` and are identical to the previous revision's, since only dev-dependencies and a comment changed. Written for commit 350c5c050019d061e14771a6d13c873bab21ec0a. Summary will update on new commits. ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Verify Bitcoin SPV proofs using transaction position and consistent hash bytes ### What Changed - Merkle proofs now use the transaction’s position to determine child order, accepting valid proofs at any position and rejecting proofs supplied for the wrong position - Bitcoin deposit verification now requires the transaction index instead of inferring order from hash values - Header hashing documentation now correctly identifies the returned bytes as Bitcoin wire order - Tests compare header hashes and merkle verification across all three Bitcoin implementations using a real regtest block ### Impact `✅ Fewer valid Bitcoin deposits rejected` `✅ Wrong-position proofs rejected` `✅ Consistent Bitcoin proof verification across components`

## High-level PR Summary This PR fixes a critical bug in the Bitcoin merkle proof verification within `x3-bitcoin-vault` where it was constructing an incorrect merkle tree by sorting node pairs numerically instead of by position. author: niteeshkanna-sh
body:
**395px wide instead of 505, and 383 tall instead of 450.** Four columns of twelve rather than five, tighter padding, smaller labels, a shorter button. The banner came down with it — 678px to 610.

What the width bought back went two places: the heading now sets *"and across Kanyakumari district"* on one line instead of two, and the photograph has more of itself visible between the text and the card.

### Two things stopped it going smaller

**The date boxes have to sit on one line.** Stacked, the card is *taller* than the one it replaces — the opposite of the point.

**At exactly 1024px**, where the two columns first appear, four of twelve leaves those boxes 113px each: enough to fit, not enough to read a date in. So it is five columns from 1024 and four from 1280.

### Measured

| | card | dates |
|---|---|---|
| 1400px | 395×383 | 171px each, one row |
| 1280px | 363×383 | 155px each, one row |
| 1024px | 359×383 | 153px each, one row |
| 768px | 704×383 | 326px each, one row |
| 390px | 350×375 | 153px each, one row |
| 360px | 320×392 | 138px each, one row |

Nothing clipped, nothing overflowing, at any of them.

The text contrast was re-measured against the photograph afterwards, because a wider text column sits over a different part of it. Everything still clears — the closest is the heading at 5.88:1 against a needed 3, and the intro at 6.01:1 against 4.5.

### Tested

58 checks on the banner, now including that the two date boxes stay on one row and that no label is cut off mid-word — the two things that would make "smaller" into "broken". Plus 35 on the picture addresses and the existing suites (51 reminders, 64 bell, 18 unread, 52 admin, 19 enquiry, 29 ERP, 28 fleet, 46 money).

### One thing on your side

The database password is still in this repository's git history and has not been rotated. Change it in hPanel → Databases, then put the new one in `nitesha-config/config.php` above the document root. Nothing in the panel will work between the two steps, so do them together.
