author: romaincouturier
body:
## Ce qui change

### Mode démo
- **Fenêtres de participant d'une formation** : toutes contrôlées.
  - « Modifier le participant » : champs identifiants floutés (participant, commanditaire, adresse, montant, coupon, URL du financeur, notes). Le nom du financeur et les fichiers joints sont masqués.
  - « Ajouter un participant de la même entreprise » (formulaire pré-rempli) : champs identifiants floutés, financeur masqué.
  - « Recueil des besoins » :
    - nom, prénom, email et société masqués ;
    - réponses libres floutées, dont les besoins d'accessibilité ;
    - le PDF exporté garde le vrai nom (il recevait le nom masqué en mode démo).
  - Toast « Participant ajouté » : email masqué.
  - Repositionner, Dupliquer vers une autre formation, Documents, Traçabilité : vérifiés, rien d'identifiant non masqué.
- **Page d'édition d'une formation** : client, commanditaire, responsable administratif et financeur floutés (trouvé par le contrôle [068]).
- **Missions** :
  - contenu d'une page, résumé IA et résultats de sondage floutés ;
  - titres de pages masqués dans l'arborescence ;
  - titre de mission masqué dans le dialogue de facture.
- **Noms de documents** (`maskFileName`) :
  - dans le gestionnaire de documents partagé (missions, formations, AO), l'analyse des pièces d'AO, les livrables de mission, les pièces jointes d'email du CRM, la Médiathèque et le sélecteur de médiathèque du Book ;
  - y compris dans les confirmations et les notifications.
- **Cartes du module contenu** : les noms de clients cités dans le titre, la description ou les tags sont masqués. La liste de noms vient de :
  - CRM, missions et contacts, formations et sociétés des participants, devis, témoignages, lus avec pagination ;
  - le réglage admin « Autres noms à masquer » (`app_settings.demo_masked_names`).

  Tant que la liste n'est pas chargée, ou si son chargement échoue, le texte reste flouté.
- **Statistiques des tableaux** : montants masqués dans le flux cumulé de valeur.

### Pennylane
- **Nouveau** : « Générer une facture » dans une mission crée un **brouillon** de facture dans Pennylane (edge function `create-mission-invoice`).
  - Une ligne par activité, échéance à J+30, TVA au choix (20 % par défaut).
  - La fiche client est reprise de la carte CRM liée à la mission, sinon de la mission et de son contact, et reste modifiable dans le dialogue.
  - Pennylane retrouve le client par email ou crée sa fiche ; une fiche existante n'est jamais modifiée.
  - Les activités sont marquées facturées.
  - La saisie manuelle reste disponible dans l'onglet « Facture existante ».
- **Isolation** : lectures et écritures sous la RLS de l'utilisateur ; seul le token Pennylane est lu en service role.
- **Logique commune** : `_shared/pennylane-invoices.ts` reprend la résolution client et le format de lignes des devis.
- **`useEdgeFunction`** affiche maintenant le message d'erreur renvoyé par la fonction au lieu de « non-2xx status code ». Ce comportement change pour tous les appelants : le message affiché est plus précis, rien d'autre ne change.

### CRM et statistiques
- « AO à qualifier » (`/crm/marches-publics`) devient un sous-module du CRM dans la barre latérale, avec les droits du module CRM.
- Carte de contrôle : la moyenne, l'UCL et la LCL affichent leur valeur au survol.

### Correctifs
- **Cron jobs (spinner infini)** — migration `20260923100000` :
  - `get_cron_status()` lit l'historique en un seul parcours sur 14 jours, au lieu de deux lectures complètes par job ;
  - un job quotidien purge l'historique au-delà de 14 jours, et la migration purge le stock existant ;
  - l'onglet affiche l'erreur avec un bouton « Réessayer ».
- **Médiathèque, erreurs de preview** : les images des buckets privés (`book-productions`, `crm-attachments`) ne sont plus demandées avec l'URL publique avant leur signature, et la signature est réutilisée 50 min.
- **Book** :
  - aperçu des vidéos dans le sélecteur de médiathèque et sur les vignettes d'album ;
  - une vidéo ajoutée depuis la médiathèque n'utilise plus son propre fichier comme image de vignette.
- **Archives** : défilement vertical de la liste et des filtres.

### Règles
- [068] Formulaire d'édition interne : champs identifiants floutés en mode démo.
- [069] Bucket privé : jamais d'URL publique rendue avant signature.

Les deux contrôles ont été mis en échec volontairement avant d'être retenus (règle [043]).

## Vérifications
- **Typecheck, build** : OK.
- **`check-rules.sh`** : 89/89. Ratchet [065] à 0.
- **vitest** : 2161 tests passent (145 fichiers).
- **Lint** : aucune erreur ajoutée (1161 erreurs, comme `main`).
- **`verif-rebase.sh`** : aucune anomalie. Pas de collision de numéro de règle.
- **Couverture** :

  | Fichier | Couverture |
  |---|---|
  | `_shared/pennylane-invoices.ts` | 100 % (lignes, branches, fonctions) |
  | `useDemoClientNames.ts` | 100 % des lignes |
  | `useEdgeFunction.ts` | 100 % des lignes |
  | `useResolvedStorageUrl.ts` | 96 % des lignes |

- **Revue de sécurité** : aucune vulnérabilité introduite.

## Non couvert ou à faire
- **Migration à appliquer** : sans elle, le spinner des cron jobs reste.
- **Brouillon Pennylane jamais appelé en réel** : le format de la facture suit celui des devis, déjà en service. Il faut vérifier que le token Pennylane a le scope `customer_invoices:all` ; en cas de refus, le dialogue affiche le message de Pennylane.
- **`create-mission-invoice/index.ts`** : non couvert par les tests, `Deno.serve` démarre à l'import. La logique est dans `_shared`.
- **À planifier** : `GenerateInvoiceDialog.tsx` dépasse 400 lignes et appelle encore Supabase en direct pour l'upload manuel (existant).
- **Sécurité, antérieur à cette PR** :
  - `pennylane-proxy` n'exige qu'une session valide, sans contrôle staff. Avec l'inscription ouverte, n'importe quel compte peut lire et écrire les factures et clients Pennylane. À corriger dans une PR dédiée.
  - `get_cron_status()` est lisible par tout compte connecté.
- **Mode démo, non couvert** : titres des productions du Book, objet prérempli du dialogue d'envoi des livrables.

body: A Ready Claude / Codex / Cursor rail now lists **that account's real models**, asked of the vendor's official CLI. The hard-coded placeholder rows are gone: `default_models` (Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, "Codex default model", Cursor "Auto"). Nothing reads another app's credential files or keychain. Traycer's passive lane is not adopted; its MIT client logic is reused and cited where it helped. ## Per vendor (official CLI only) | Rail | Probe | Read | |---|---|---| | Claude | `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config` plus the `initialize` control request, which is what the Agent SDK's `supportedModels()` / `accountInfo()` read | `models[]` (`value`, `displayName`), `account` (`email`, `subscriptionType`) | | Codex | `codex app-server`: `initialize`, `initialized`, `account/read` (never `refreshToken`), `model/list` (paged) | `data[]` (`model` slug as in Traycer `codex-adapter.ts`, `displayName`, `isDefault`, `hidden` skipped), `account` (`email`, `planType`); `account: null` counts as not signed in | | Cursor | `cursor-agent models` | text ` - (current, default)` between `Available models` and `Tip:`; "Authentication required/failed" counts as not signed in | - Wire formats are pinned against the real CLIs installed with their official installers (Claude Code 2.1.280, Codex 0.156.1, Cursor Agent 2026.09.18-9a7762b), the SDK's documented `ModelInfo`/`AccountInfo` types, `codex app-server generate-json-schema`, and the listing code in the Cursor CLI bundle. - The Claude documented `--model` aliases are a last resort, used only when a CLI build does not answer the handshake. They are labelled `opus (alias)` and so on, flagged `documented_aliases`, and never cached. ## States a Ready rail can show (no invented rows) - **Loading:** "Loading models…" until the CLI answers, when nothing is cached. - **Listed:** the CLI's list, in its order, default first. `cached` marks the last good list from `$WORKSHOP_HOME/catalog-cache/-models.json` (0600). - **Failed:** "Couldn't load models — press Ctrl+R to retry", when the probe failed and nothing is cached. The picker's refresh key is Ctrl+R; a plain `r` types into the filter. - A "not signed in" answer, or `auth status` reporting logged out, drops the cache. ## Safety rules (Traycer's sign-out lessons, `ephemeral-probe.ts` / `auth-probes/claude.ts`) - **One child per vendor at a time.** A process-wide `VendorSlot` covers every child detection starts (`--version`, status, model probes). A caller whose budget runs out while waiting spawns nothing. - **Claude kill grace.** A `claude` child past its budget is never SIGKILLed at the deadline. A reaper gives it `claude_kill_grace` (30 s, Traycer's `OAUTH_REFRESH_SAFE_TEARDOWN_GRACE_MS`) and keeps the slot until it exits. Model probes close stdin to end the CLI cleanly. ## API (for the `/model` layout work, bc-1b9089ff) Module `crates/workshop-detect/src/models/` (`workshop_detect::models`, re-exported at the crate root): - `subscription_models(rail, bin, &cfg) -> Result`: the live probe. `SubscriptionModels { rail, models: Vec, account: Option, documented_aliases, fetched_at_secs }`. `ModelsError` is one of `NotLoggedIn`, `TimedOut`, `Busy`, `Failed`. - `cached_subscription_models(rail, &ModelsCache)`: the cached variant, starts no children. - `rail_models` / `rails_models` / `picker_rails(&cfg, &cache, Refresh::CacheOnly | Refresh::Live { max_age })`. - `RailState.subscription: RailModels` is one of `NotReady`, `Loading`, `Listed { list, cached, error }`, `Failed { reason }`. `RailState.models` holds the rows. - Pager wiring: - Picker loads are `CacheOnly`. - `/model` refresh and Ctrl+R are `Live` (60 s freshness; forced means always ask). - A load that leaves a rail `Loading` (`/auth`, after sign-in) queues the new `WorkshopRefreshRailModels`, which asks the CLIs; Workshop itself makes no request. - `workshop login` asks the CLIs before printing its one-shot picker. - Full note: `internal/subscription-models-api.md` in the project store. ## Tests - **Unit, against the captured real outputs:** Claude signed-out `initialize` (5 models), Codex `model/list` (7 models, one default) and `account/read` shapes, the Cursor listing format and its signed-out error. - **`models_fakes.rs` (11 tests, fake CLIs in the documented protocols):** - signed in: models, plan and email per vendor, exactly one probe each, no `refreshToken` - cache-only shows Loading and runs no probe; the cache is reused while fresh - sign-out drops the cache - a CLI that says "not signed in" gives Failed and drops the cache - a failure keeps the last good list; with none cached it shows one Failed row, never placeholders - Claude without the handshake gives labelled, uncached aliases - a Claude probe past its budget returns at the deadline while its child runs to completion, and the next probe waits for it - a wedged Claude child is killed only after the grace - Codex and Cursor timeouts are bounded - concurrent probes never overlap (a pid-checked lock inside the fakes) - probe children run in `$HOME` with the credential-free env - **Pager dispatch:** a load that leaves a rail Loading queues exactly one rail-models refresh; a queued `/model` refresh covers it; Listed and Failed rails queue nothing. - **gate:no-theft:** - new `workshop-detect/tests/no_theft.rs`: no credential path, keychain tool or crate in `src/`, and file access only in `models/cache.rs` - `THEFT_MARKERS` and `no-xai-scan.sh` add `.claude/.credentials` and `find-generic-password` - `scripts/no-theft-fs-audit.sh` phase 2 runs every model probe under strace against signed-in fakes, decoy credentials and a fake `security` tool (CI builds the `probe` example first). Its negative control (a planted read of `~/.claude/.credentials.json`) fails the audit as it should. - **PTY gate** `live_tui_turns rails_ready…`: the rail waits for the listed models, asserts no placeholder rows, and the composer reads `Claude · Default…`. - **Real CLIs, signed out (no accounts):** `real_cli_models.rs` (ignored by default) gives Claude 5 models in about 0.2 s, Codex "not signed in" in about 0.1 s (its `model/list` still parses 7 models), and Cursor "Authentication required" in about 0.4 s. - **Local replay of `ci.yml`:** all 20 steps green. That covers fmt, check, clippy, shellcheck, the source scan, the patches check, the gates, overlay and upstream unit tests, the pager lib suite (10,153 tests), the binary scan, the no-egress smoke, the no-theft audit, and every PTY gate.

author: boby478
body: The `createUser` function was vulnerable to ID overrides and accepting arbitrary fields. This PR adds validation for required fields (name, email), restricts roles to public ones, and ensures only allowed fields are used when creating a user object, thereby keeping the server-generated ID authoritative.

author: aimoonprojekt-oss
body:
## Was ändert sich

Admins können die Agenten einer Firma jetzt **in deren Workspace** testen, auch wenn die Firma kein Abo hat:

- Einstieg: **Verwaltung → Kunden → Firma → „<Agent> testen“**.
- Der Chat öffnet sich mit dem gelben Hinweis „Testmodus · läuft im Workspace von …“.
- Der Lauf nutzt die Kopie des Agenten im Workspace der Firma, deren Speicher und deren Markenwissen, also denselben Weg wie ein echter Kunde.

Dazu kommt `scripts/kurztest.mjs`, ein Rauchtest je Firma. Er prüft den Schlüssel aus dem Vault, Agent und Umgebung im Ziel-Workspace und ob eine Antwort kommt. `docs/testlauf.md` beschreibt das Testen jetzt in vier Stufen.

**Regeln im Testmodus** (`testFreigabe` in `lib/runs/starten.ts`):
- Nur Admins (`ADMIN_USER_IDS`). Das wird serverseitig in `laufVorbereiten()` geprüft, nicht nur in der Oberfläche.
- Der Tarif ist immer `intern-test`. Nur Agenten aus diesem Paket lassen sich testen.
- Tages-, Monats- und Budgetgrenze sowie die Sperre für gleichzeitige Läufe gelten nicht. Mengenbegrenzung und **Kostendeckel bleiben**.
- Der Lauf wird mit `zaehlt_kontingent = false` und `test_organization_id` gespeichert. In `/admin/laeufe` erscheint er als „Test bei <Firma>“.

## Warum

Sins 'n Lashes hat noch kein Abo. Ihre Agenten-Kopien und ihr Wissen liegen aber in ihrem Workspace, und dort müssen sie getestet werden. Bisher ging das nur mit einem Umweg: Man musste sich in ihre Firma eintragen und dafür aus KANA AI austreten.

## Wie geprüft

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` ohne Fehler
- [x] `npm run build` ohne Fehler, mit den Platzhalterwerten aus der CI
- [x] Check „Mandantentrennung“ lokal nachgestellt: kein direkter Zugriff auf `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` außerhalb von `lib/anthropic/`
- [x] Migration `0026` (additiv) ist in Supabase eingespielt. Der Code schreibt die Spalte ohnehin nur im Testmodus.
- [x] Der Schlüssel von Sins 'n Lashes ist über `workspace_schluessel()` abrufbar (nur die Länge geprüft, der Schlüssel selbst wurde nicht ausgelesen)
- [ ] Echter Testlauf im Workspace von Sins 'n Lashes, nach dem Deploy

## Checkliste (aus dem Playbook, Abschnitt 4)

- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` ergänzt
- [x] Keine Secrets im Code
- [x] Migrationen nur ergänzt (`0026`)
- [x] `agents/` nicht berührt

## Risiko

Gering. Der normale Kundenweg ändert sich nicht: `testFirma` wird nur gelesen, wenn es gesendet wird, und nur für Admins angenommen. `anthropicFuerNutzer` ruft jetzt die neue Funktion `mandantFuerFirma` auf, die Logik darin ist unverändert.

**Bekannte Grenzen:**
- Dateien, die der Agent erzeugt, erscheinen als Link im Chat. Öffnet man die Sitzung später über „Verlauf“ neu, fehlen sie, weil sie im Ordner der Kundenfirma liegen.
- Die Kosten von Testläufen zählen zum Monatsbudget des KANA-Pakets `intern-test`.
- Analysen und Markenwissen aus einem Testlauf landen bei der getesteten Firma. Das ist gewollt, es ist ihr Wissen.

author: hermes-gadget
body:
## Summary

This batch closes the two medium findings that remained after the merged security, Wave 3, CI, and Wave 5 work. Firmware responses now stream from the Python server under signed device-size limits, and the browser rejects missing or mismatched lengths while reading only the signed image size. The UI now derives connection, channel, and flash labels/status from current state after connection, flash, and monitor transitions.

No deployment was performed.

## Per-issue mapping

| Issue | Assessment | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #4 — full erase can hit the wrong ESP | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #23](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/23) gates writes on the ROM-reported ESP32-S3 and requires the T-Deck erase phrase. |
| #5 — SHA-256 does not authenticate firmware | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #23](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/23) adds the Ed25519-signed manifest and pinned browser verification key. |
| #6 — Python server exposes repository files | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #23](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/23) replaces fall-through static serving with an exact allowlist and path checks. |
| #7 — flash offsets inferred from filenames | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #23](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/23) binds offsets, sizes, partitions, and image digests in the signed manifest and validates images before writes. |
| #8 — Update Only uses the wrong hash | ALREADY-FIXED | The signed update mode binds `firmware.bin`, its `0x10000` offset, size, and digest; regression coverage landed with [PR #24](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/24). |
| #9 — failed downloads are promoted as complete | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #23](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/23) uses bounded temporary downloads and signed size/digest checks; [PR #24](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/24) adds preservation/retry regression coverage. |
| #10 — lexicographic versions select stale releases | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #24](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/24) selects aliases in GitHub API order and tests the `0.1.10` versus `0.1.9` case. |
| #11 — Docker deployment cannot serve firmware | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #24](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/24) adds the Python backend, nginx proxy routes, and a least-privileged sync profile. Vault provisioning and scheduling stay deployment-owned. |
| #12 — nginx drops security headers on cached locations | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #24](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/24) includes the complete header set in each cached location and tests the config. |
| #13 — write success lacks flash readback | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #24](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/24) supplies esptool-js MD5 readback verification before reset/success. |
| #14 — flash console inserts untrusted text as HTML | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #24](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/24) switches console output to text nodes and whitelisted classes. |
| #15 — stopping monitor leaves WebSerial open | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #24](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/24) cancels and drains the reader before releasing the lock and closing the port. |
| #16 — firmware response memory is unbounded | FIXED-ON-BRANCH | `server.py` caps signed firmware at the 16 MiB device flash size and streams in 64 KiB chunks. Browser reads require exact `Content-Length` and fill a signed-size buffer incrementally; source ArrayBuffers are dropped before flashing. Sync downloads already use bounded temporary files and signed digests. Added server and browser regression tests. |
| #17 — connection/flash controls become stale | FIXED-ON-BRANCH | `refreshUiState()` derives button labels, enablement, selected channel, and step status from current connection/flash/monitor state. Tests cover auto-selected channel → connect → flash and post-flash disconnect state. |
| #18 — debug report privacy guarantee is unsafe | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #26](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/26) adds the sensitive-data warning and review/redaction gate. |
| #19 — download UI has stale/dead hooks | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #26](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/26) gives controls unique IDs, renders release links from metadata, and removes or wires dead hooks. |
| #20 — archive responses use mutable cache policy | ALREADY-FIXED | Main normalizes the vault-relative archive path and recognizes `archive/` before applying immutable caching; this was part of the baseline carried into [PR #26](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/26). |
| #21 — vault publication is not atomic | ALREADY-FIXED | Main writes JSON and unique temporary symlinks, then uses `os.replace()`; [PR #26](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/26) records this finding as already fixed on its baseline. |
| #22 — missing CI and dependency provenance | ALREADY-FIXED | [PR #25](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/25) adds CI; [PR #26](https://github.com/hermes-gadget/SigurdOS-Webflasher/pull/26) adds the lockfile, vendored bundle provenance, pinned Docker digests, and CI lockfile enforcement. |

## Verification

- CI workflow commands: asset `node --check`, `npm test` (21 passing), `python3 -m py_compile server.py`, and Python unittest discovery (13 passing).
- Explicit Python suites: `python3 -m unittest -v tests/test_server.py tests/test_firmware_manifest.py` (13 passing).
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Leftover local branch audit

The leftover branches contain no unique work needed for this batch. `fix/add-ci`, `fix/w3-mediums`, `fix/sigweb-highs`, and `fix/w5-lows` match work merged through PRs #25, #24, #23, and #26 respectively; `verify-sigweb` and `w3-verify` duplicate the corresponding high/medium branch tips. `fix/security-hardening` is superseded by the signed-manifest work in PR #23. `fix/nginx-eol-cves` is superseded by the mainline nginx update and the later digest-pinned base in PR #26. These unused local refs could be removed after review; `fix/w5-lows` is currently checked out in `/home/ben/SigurdOS-Webflasher` and should remain until that worktree moves. No branch was deleted, and no remote branch was deleted.

author: mixvlad
body:
Five public-domain decks from Wikimedia Commons (mostly BnF / Gallica scans), each with `full/`, `720px/`, three GIF previews and a per-card `metadata.json` (licence verified via the Commons API).

| Deck | Folder | Cards | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grand Etteilla (H. Pussey, c.1880–1890) | `tarot/etteilla/` | 75 of 78 | ~1600×2800 |
| Tarot de Viéville (Paris, c.1650) | `tarot/vieville/` | 78 + back | ~1706×3040 |
| Visconti-Sforza (Milan, c.1450–1470) | `tarot/visconti-sforza/` | 73 of 78 | 512×1024 |
| Oswald Wirth (1889) | `tarot/oswald-wirth/` | 22 major arcana | ~910×1536 |
| Tarot Nouveau (Grimaud, 1898) | `tarot/tarot-nouveau/` | 78 + back | ~1500×2655 |

Notes
- **Etteilla**: own 1–78 numbering, `NN_<Title>.jpg`. 49, 63 and 78 are not on Commons; 16 and 17 come from a lower-resolution copy of the same edition.
- **Viéville**: file numbers follow the numerals printed on the cards (VII Justice, VIII Chariot, IX Force, XI Hermit).
- **Visconti-Sforza**: scans of an AGMüller facsimile by David Madore (2003); four cards are lost from the original and the King of Cups is missing from this scan set.
- Card backs are stored as `Cover.jpg` and skipped by the GIF script.
- `download_commons_deck.py`: maps for all five decks, and retry with backoff on Wikimedia HTTP 429.
- README, SOURCES.md, CLAUDE.md and `decks_config.json` updated; SOURCES.md now states the real Marseille resolution (~813×1536, not ~200×351).

Adds ~294 MB of images.

author: danielromanmartinez
body:
## Summary
`StripeAbstractComposeView` now gives its inner compose view a view-scoped `ViewModelStoreOwner` and `SavedStateRegistryOwner` (`ViewScopedOwner`) instead of the Activity's, and clears that `ViewModelStore` in `handleOnDropViewInstance`. Both owners are always assigned; only `setParentCompositionContext` still depends on `composeCompatView`.

## Motivation
Fixes #2678.

With the Activity's owners, every mounted `EmbeddedPaymentElement` leaked its `EmbeddedPaymentElementViewModel` (a new random key per mount). All of their `SavedStateHandle`s were written into the Activity's saved state on each `onStop`. After a few mounts this crashes with `TransactionTooLargeException` in `activityStopped`, usually when Link opens `LinkForegroundActivity`. Screenshots and the full logcat are in the issue.

The view's registry is never attached to the Activity's, so this doesn't depend on how a given androidx version stores the handles. Trade-off: if the process is killed while the element is on screen, its internal state is not restored. The element is recreated from scratch anyway, since the random instance key doesn't survive.

`PaymentMethodMessagingElementView` also extends this class. It creates its element with the Application and doesn't use ViewModels, so the only change for it is that its compose tree gets the view-scoped owners.

## Testing
- [x] I tested this manually
- [ ] I added automated tests

I tested through flutter_stripe, which ships a byte-identical copy of this file (flutter-stripe/flutter_stripe#2474), on a Pixel 6 emulator with Android 16:
- Before: mount/unmount the element 7 times, then select Link and confirm → `TransactionTooLargeException` (894 KB), process dies.
- After: same steps, no crash, same PID. Back from Link returns to the app.
- After: full card flow works (form sheet → element shows the card → confirm → setup succeeds).
- The file compiles against Stripe Android 23.19.0 (the version pinned here), and `./gradlew detekt` passes. I didn't build the React Native example app.

## Documentation

Select one: 
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation for my changes.
- [x] This PR does not result in any developer-facing changes.

author: rubicon
body:
Closes #496

Phase 3 of #38, stacked on #500 (phase 2's harness). Review #500 first — this PR's base is `dev/495-bulk-write-harness`, and GitHub will retarget it to `main` when #500 merges.

## What it adds

`bulk_find_replace` — the write payload that actually touches `post_content`, on the harness phase 2 proved with a payload that could not.

**Literal strings only, never a pattern.** Your decision, and the reason holds up: a regex the caller cannot fully predict, applied to 25 pages under one approval, is a different risk class from the one the dry-run plan exists to let a human judge.

**Per-opener splice, never a block-tree round trip.** One opener's attribute JSON is decoded, the replacement runs on the decoded tree so only string leaves change, and the result is re-encoded through `serialize_block_attrs_canonical()` and required to decode cleanly before it is spliced back. That avoids both hazards a `parse_blocks()`/`serialize_blocks()` round trip carries here: the #11 `divi/global-layout` materialisation, and the byte loss phase 0 measured on 17% of real pages.

Openers are rewritten last to first, because a replacement almost always changes length.

## The two things worth your attention

**1. A real production bug, found by chasing a surviving mutant.** Invalid UTF-8 in `search` or `replace` does not fail gracefully — it *fatals*, inside WordPress core. `serialize_block_attributes()` passes `wp_json_encode()`'s return straight into `strtr()` without checking it, and `wp_json_encode()` returns `false` on invalid UTF-8. Reaching the encoder with those bytes is a `TypeError` mid-run, after however many earlier targets in the same run had already been written. It is now refused up front, before any target is read.

**2. A find/replace can detach a global layout, and this is not theoretical.** `globalModule` is stored as a *string*, so an ordinary site-wide sweep of a numeric token — a post id, an order number, a SKU — rewrites a wrapper's layout reference like any other string leaf, and the page silently points at a different layout or at none. The guarded write now runs with global-layout drift checking on; that target fails as `bulk.global_layout_drift` and is left byte-identical, while the rest of the run proceeds.

## Testing

`tests/test-bulk-find-replace.php`, 83 assertions, sections named for the corruption each one prevents. Full suite: 6394 passing, plus the local-site drift gate, which wants a staging deploy.

A 17-mutant matrix kills 13. The four survivors are recorded in the test file with their reasons rather than left looking covered: three are guards unreachable through the public API and kept as defence in depth, and the fourth is an equivalent mutant — swapping the canonical encoder for a plain `wp_json_encode()` produces byte-identical stored content, measured, because the tail canonicalisation is the load-bearing step. That last one is worth knowing rather than covering: a change that removed *it* would not be caught by anything in this file.

## Not in this PR

Bulk module-attribute edits ("change every button's border radius"). Phase 3's per-opener primitive is exactly what that needs, so it is now a viable phase 4 — proposed on #38 rather than smuggled in here.

author: moukrea
body:
One menu switches the update channel of every connected element at once (JAU-99).

- **Settings → Update channel → Switch everything** opens a menu listing `main`, each channel published in `<page>/ch/index.json` (with its PR number and title), and **Other…** for a hand-typed name. The name is still validated by each surface against `ch/<name>/config.json` before any install.
- Targets are this app (desktop or Android), the desktop's local host and every directly connected host whose updates are managed by the public installer; offline or unmanaged hosts are listed as skipped.
- Hosts switch first, through the existing `updates.configure {channel}`; the app switches itself only once every chosen host has accepted, because the desktop closes to install. A browser never switches itself (PWA selector, JAU-87).
- Reading the list: a browser fetches it from its own Page; the desktop CSP and the Android WebView forbid that fetch, so the desktop gets a `channels` update action and Android an `app.channels` bridge action, both reading the official Page. `web/js/channels.mjs` validates the list (official page/repository, publishable names only).
- Tests: `tests/js.test.mjs` (list validation against the shared fixtures), `tests/desktop_updates.test.cjs` (native list fetch), `UpdateChannelsTest` (index URL), and `tests/client_update_e2e.py` now performs the channel switch through the grouped menu from a published `ch/index.json`, saving `test-results/channel-menu.png` in the `browser-evidence` artifact.

author: shichao-wang
body:
PR #5 那次「重试两分钟」没能救回来：`v2026.09.23-022592` 的发布后校验把 24 次重试跑满（09:44:38 → 09:46:19），下载始终是空的。**两个 release 本身都好的**——六个资产都在，校验和与本地算出来的逐字符一致：

```
86c1c7023d…  cpa_2026.09.23-022592_darwin_amd64.tar.gz
5ab1bb9a82…  cpa_2026.09.23-022592_darwin_arm64.tar.gz
1346576096…  cpa_2026.09.23-022592_linux_amd64.tar.gz
765db7b31c…  cpa_2026.09.23-022592_linux_arm64.tar.gz
```

我在这两个 release 上各跑了一次真实升级：`v2026.09.23-ed88bb -> v2026.09.23-022592`，`checksum ok`，装完报 `cpa v2026.09.23-022592`。整条链路是通的，红的只是校验。

## 结论：这道校验不该存在

发布后那几分钟里，下载 URL 和 releases API 都会按「这个 release 是空的」作答，实测窗口两三分钟且不稳定（ed88bb8 那次两分钟内就好了，022592 这次超过两分钟）。所以：

- 预算调小 → 假红，就是现在这样，已经连着两次；
- 预算调大 → 覆盖窗口，等于**每次**发版都在这儿白等两三分钟；
- 而它自诞生起一个真问题都没抓到过——它要防的「`gh release create` 静默不挂资产」，出处是那个已被证伪的 v0.2.1 判断。

上传真失败时这一步本来就会失败（`gh release create` 非零退出）。所以这个 PR 把回读整段删掉，注释里留下实测到的传播窗口和补救手段（`gh release upload <tag> --clobber …`，是重传而不是重跑）。

顺带删掉只服务于这段校验的 `REPO` 环境变量。

## 验证

假 gh/git 跑了 3 个场景：正常发布（打 tag + create，且**不再有任何 curl**）、tag 已存在（只发布不重打 tag）、release 已存在（直接跳过）。YAML 解析正常，release 任务步骤仍是 `Work out the version / Build archives / Tag and publish`。这次没动 Go 代码。

合并这个 PR 会再切一个 release：那次的 run 应该是绿的（这次没东西可红了）。

## Submission type

## Submission status and current guidance

author: cydoentis
body:
Snipux had no way to tell anyone a release had happened. Someone who installed 1.0.0 would keep running it until they next visited the repo — and 1.0.1 fixed a copy that silently lost its image on Wayland, which those users would never learn.

## What it does

A tray item — **"Check for updates"**, directly above Quit — and nothing else. No check at startup, no timer, no traffic of any kind until someone picks it. A screenshot tool that phones home unasked is one people stop trusting, and checking automatically buys nothing but hearing about a release a few days sooner.

The message matches the build that's running, the same split `run_update` already makes:

| Build | Told to |
|---|---|
| pip / pipx | run `snipux --update` |
| exe, AppImage, `.deb` | download from the Releases page (pip can't upgrade any of them) |
| already current | "Snipux 1.0.1 is the newest version." |
| check failed | "Could not check for updates. Try again when you are online." |

## Design notes

- **Off the UI thread.** One GET, reported back through a signal, so a proxy that never answers can't hang the tray menu.
- **Every failure is an answer, not an exception** — no network, a rate limit, a JSON shape that changed. Not knowing is a normal outcome of asking.
- **`urllib`, not a fourth dependency.** One request to a public API isn't worth one.
- The check object is held in an attribute: `AppController` isn't a `QObject`, so there's no Qt parent to own it, and a `QObject` collected mid-emit is a crash rather than a missed message.

## Also

`--update`'s help still said it fetched "from GitHub" — it has fetched from PyPI since 0.6.0.

## Verification

3299 passed, 20 skipped. 28 new tests, none of which touch the network: every one injects its own opener, so the suite answers the same on a machine with no connection and on the day a release is cut.

author: tamnd
body:
Part of #943, and the tcc half of #425. tcc's `bitfield_test` has `long long f1 : 45` and prints it with `printf("%lld", st2.f1)`. rucc refused the function with "no rule lowers a `trunc` producing a `i45`".

The field's type is right. A bit-field wider than `int` promotes to an integer as wide as the field, which is what gcc calls `long int:45`. What was missing is the call. No call has a register for a 45 bit integer, and gcc passes one past a prototype at the type the field was declared with, so `va_arg (ap, long long)` on the other side reads the value sign extended to 64 bits. The default argument promotions now do the same when the argument is a bit-field of an ordinary integer type whose promotion came out as one of these. A real `_BitInt(N)` argument is left alone, since its calling convention is the rest of #425.

Checked on server2: a repro with tcc's struct prints `4886718345 4026531841 120` and `8913250186` from gcc 16 and rucc at O0, O1, O2, O3 and Os. `cargo xtask ci` is clean. The golden case in `tests/golden/bitfields.c` shows the conversion to `long long` in the checked tree.

tcc at O0 is down to 11 refusals, all of them templates (#349).

author: imoriana3
body:
**Cuatro veces en una semana** se quedó atrás el número de una tarjeta — v1.63, v1.64, v1.68 y el salto de v1.70 a v1.76 — y las cuatro lo destapó `tests/test_versiones_app.mjs` **después**, no antes.

Esa es la cuenta que obliga a mirar el mecanismo en vez de la última vez: **un número copiado a mano sólo puede envejecer**, y un careo acorta la ventana pero no la cierra. Peor, la ventana caía siempre en el mismo sitio — entre el merge de la app y el siguiente que tocara el Panel — que es justo cuando alguien mira la captura para saber sobre qué versión está diagnosticando.

```diff
-    version: "v1.76.0",
+    verEnApp: true,      // el número vive en la app, no en la tarjeta
```

## El mecanismo ya existía en la casa

No se ha inventado otro. Las tarjetas con `release:` (la TCU Toolbox) leen su versión de la API de GitHub desde hace tiempo, pisan el valor escrito, cachean 6 h y caen al literal si falla. Esto es lo mismo, leyendo el fichero de la app en vez de la API.

## El Panel lee Pages y el arnés lee `main`

Parece incoherente y no lo es: son preguntas distintas.

| | lee | por qué |
|---|---|---|
| el Panel | **Pages** | el número describe la app que el usuario va a **abrir al pulsar**, o sea la publicada. Si Pages va retrasada, lo honesto es decir la versión retrasada |
| el arnés | **`main`** | Pages va unos minutos por detrás tras cada merge; exigírselo pondría el check en rojo **justo al publicar**, por un retardo que no es un defecto |

## Lo medido, no supuesto

| | |
|---|---|
| mismo origen | `imoriana3.github.io` las dos → **no hay CORS** |
| coste | 588.485 + 299.483 = **887.968 B**, con caché de 6 h |
| rango HTTP | **descartado**: `const VER` está en el byte 47.073 de una y el 145.363 de la otra, y ese desplazamiento se mueve con cada edición; y **no está medido** si Pages sirve `206` |

## Y si no se puede leer, no se inventa

Las tarjetas con `release:` guardan el literal como respaldo **a propósito**; aquí no, porque el literal es justo lo que se está quitando. El respaldo es la **última lectura de ese navegador**, marcada, y si no hay ninguna la tarjeta dice «versión no leída».

Ese tercer estado **antes no podía ocurrir**: con el número escrito siempre había algo que pintar, aunque fuera falso.

## Una sola definición de la regla, y es la del Panel

La expresión que busca `VER` se **extrae** de `index.html`; no se copia al arnés. Copiarla habría repetido el mismo defecto dentro del fichero que existe para impedirlo: el día que cambie el formato de la declaración, el arnés seguiría verde leyendo con la regla vieja mientras el Panel se queda a oscuras.

## El arnés cambia de pregunta

De «¿son iguales estos dos números?» a «¿sigue resolviendo el puntero?» (13 → **18** comprobaciones). Lo que queda por vigilar **es menos, y se dice**: que la app deje de declarar `VER` donde la regla lo busca, que la url deje de servir ese fichero, o que alguien vuelva a escribir `version:` al lado del puntero.

Los cuatro casos, **vistos en rojo con mutantes**. Y el pintado se prueba en navegador (`test_index.js` 18 → **28**): los tres estados con la app simulada, con el control de que el número de la prueba —`v9.9.9`— **no está escrito en `index.html`**, verificado leyendo el fichero.

## Un mutante mío salió verde por estar mal hecho

Y casi lo leo como «el arnés no lo caza». Lo escribí **por número de línea** y una regla de CSS que añadí más arriba lo había desplazado uno, así que el `sed` no tocó nada. Es el mismo vicio del puntero por línea que acababa de arreglar en el otro repo, cometido aquí diez minutos después. Rehecho por contenido: rojo.

## Dos afirmaciones que nadie puede comprobar

Encontradas al medir la cobertura y **no arregladas aquí** porque no son de esta línea: `sim-viento.html` no contiene la cadena `1.26` en ninguna parte y `comparador-estructuras.html` no contiene `1.58`. Sus tarjetas declaran una versión que la app no dice en ningún sitio. Quedan nombradas en el arnés y en `tests/README.md`.

## Hueco declarado

`imoriana3.github.io` está **bloqueado por el proxy de salida** de la máquina donde se escribió esto, así que la lectura contra Pages **real** no se ha podido ejercitar — sólo con la app simulada. En CI sí es alcanzable, y el arnés imprime lo que ve.

## Bancos

Suite completa: **43 arneses verdes · 2408 comprobaciones leídas**, de una tirada entera y limpia.

El recuento del README decía «40 · 2296» y estaba **dos arneses viejo**. No se equivocó nadie al ponerlo: envejeció, que es lo que le pasa a un número copiado — el mismo defecto que este PR quita del Panel. Se actualiza declarando que sale de una tirada **local, no de CI**, que es peor procedencia; sigue valiendo «manda CI».

Y la tirada anterior a ésta dio 42 verdes con `test_viento_sitio.js` en rojo por un `waitForSelector: Timeout 5000ms`. **No era el arnés ni el cambio**: había otro Chromium con WebGL corriendo en paralelo en otro repo — lo lancé yo — y el control a solas dio 52/52.

author: khushalsonawat
body:
## Summary

`evaluations/catalog/system_evals.yaml` is the only place a built-in eval's tags come from, and after TH-8044 it is also the only list of built-in evals simulation may offer. Six conversation evals the harness already uses exist only as legacy YAML under `model_hub/system_evals/agent/`, so without this change they would drop out of that offer. This PR adds them to the catalog with their text copied byte-for-byte from the legacy files, and bumps the seeder version so the next operator-run seed copies the new tags onto the stored templates.

## Linked issues

Closes #
Linear: Closes TH-8043

## AI use

AI use: Claude Code implemented this change from a reviewed plan and contract; tests were written first as static files and run at the end; one cold review round on the full diff.

## Type of change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] 📖 Documentation only
- [ ] 🧹 Chore / refactor (no user-visible change)
- [ ] 🚀 Performance improvement
- [ ] 🧪 Test-only change

## E2E coverage

E2E: exempt (backend-internal — catalog data and seeder tests, no UI)

---

## 1) What changes were done

**A. Six conversation evals added to the catalog**

- `advice_authority_boundary`, `claim_intake_accuracy`, `lead_qualification_completeness`, `no_misselling`, `intake_field_accuracy` and `customer_agent_task_completion` added to `futureagi/evaluations/catalog/system_evals.yaml`.
- Each entry carries `eval_type`, `output`, `required_keys`, `description`, `tags` and `rule_prompt`.
- `description` and `rule_prompt` are copied verbatim from the legacy YAML, so the six score exactly as they do today; only their tag data is new.
- The entries use inline lists for `required_keys`/`tags`, like the rest of the file.

**B. Seeder version bump**

- `SYSTEM_EVALS_VERSION` in `futureagi/model_hub/management/commands/seed_system_evals.py` moves from 16 to 17, so an operator-run seed picks up the new tags instead of being skipped as already-current.

**C. New test file**

- `futureagi/model_hub/tests/test_seed_system_evals_catalog_tags.py` pins the six entries, the prompt parity, the file's list style and the seeder's tag copy.

---

## 2) Why the changes were done

- **Product/UX:** once simulation reads only the catalog (TH-8044), a built-in eval missing from it stops being offered, and these six are already used by the harness.
- **Technical:** copying the prompt and description text byte-for-byte instead of rewriting it keeps scoring unchanged, and a test pins that parity so the two copies cannot drift.
- **Architecture:** the catalog stays the single source of an eval's tags; the seeder is the only writer of those tags onto stored templates, and only on a version bump.

---

## 3) Tests written + scenarios each covers

**`test_seed_system_evals_catalog_tags.py`** — 11 tests: the six entries and their tags, byte-for-byte prompt/description parity with the legacy YAML, no orphaned catalog key, `required_keys` declared everywhere, the seeder copying catalog tags onto stored templates, the version gate reopening, an unlisted legacy eval keeping its own tags, an empty `tags` list being ignored, the section header, and inline list style.

```
19 passed in 107.44s (0:01:47)
```

---

## 4) How to run / test

### Backend tests

```bash
cd futureagi
uv venv --python 3.11 && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -r requirements-test.txt
bin/test model_hub/tests/test_seed_system_evals_catalog_tags.py model_hub/tests/test_seed_system_evals_modality_tags.py -v
```

### Frontend tests (if applicable)

Not applicable — no frontend change.

### Contract verification (if API surface changed)

Not applicable — no API surface changed.

### UI steps (manual)

Not applicable — no UI change.

---

## 5) Screenshots / recordings

### Test output

No screenshots; the pytest summary in section 3 is the run (19 passed).

### UI testing

Not applicable — no UI change.

---

## 6) Edge cases & considerations

- Prompts use `|-` block scalars: the legacy prompts end without a newline, and the parity test compares without stripping.
- Data only — nothing takes effect until the seeder runs: `SERVICE_TYPE=bootstrap STARTUP_DB_MUTATION_MODE=operator NO_STARTUP_DB_MUTATIONS=false python manage.py seed_system_evals`; until then stored tags stay as they are.
- The seed re-applies catalog tags to all 72 listed templates (65 differ from their legacy tags today); the visible effect is the evals-library filter chips.
- Simulation offers keep using the JSON name list until TH-8044 lands.
- The pinned 21-voice / 22-chat offer lists land with the offer rule in TH-8044, not here.
- First in the chain: #3008 (TH-8045), #3013 (TH-8044), #3015 (TH-8046) and #3021 (TH-8055) sit on top of it.

---

## 7) Pre-existing issues (NOT introduced by this PR)

## 8) Architectural / important decisions

- **Byte-for-byte prompt copy:** the six entries' `rule_prompt` and `description` were copied from the legacy YAML rather than rewritten, and a test pins the match, so this PR changes what tags exist and not how any of the six score.

body:
## Description `POST /configuration/hosts` now accepts `alias`, `snmp_version` and `snmp_community`. `alias` is trimmed and bounded at 200 characters measured after trimming, as `NewHost` does, so a blank value reads as "not provided" and lands as `NULL` where legacy stores `''` — config generation skips both alike. `snmp_version` takes `1`, `2c` or `3`, the values legacy stores in `host.host_snmp_version`. `snmp_community` is write-only: with a vault configured it is stored under `monitoring/hosts` / `_HOSTSNMPCOMMUNITY` and only the `secret::` reference reaches the column, so the response never carries it, as in legacy. It mints a standalone vault entry, and legacy reuses that entry's UUID for password macros — whoever migrates macros must thread it through rather than mint a second one. That reference shares the column with the plaintext, hence the new `WhenVault` constraint, on the model of `WhenPlatform`: the 255-character bound applies only when no vault is configured. With one, legacy measures the substituted path rather than the plaintext, so a longer secret is accepted there and here. The bound itself lives on `SnmpCommunity`, built from whatever the column will actually hold. **Fixes** # [MON-208991](https://centreon.atlassian.net/browse/MON-208991) ## Type of change - [ ] Patch fixing an issue (non-breaking change) - [x] New functionality (non-breaking change) - [ ] Breaking change (patch or feature) that might cause side effects breaking part of the Software ## Target serie - [ ] 24.04.x - [ ] 24.10.x - [ ] 25.10.x - [x] master

body:
## Summary

- replace the historical componentwise comparator surface with a compact, Mathlib-native formulation using Euclidean `ℝ³ × ℝ` coordinates
- package an explicit global spatial weak derivative in `NSEData`, fixed-box bounds in `HasEnergyRegularityOn`, and the PDE and local-energy clauses as separate predicates
- use the parabolic metric only for Hölder regularity and Hausdorff measure, with ordinary product coordinates for the Navier–Stokes equations
- prove the cleaned Theorems A, B, and C by exact coordinate, measure, weak-derivative, Hölder, limsup, and Hausdorff-measure transport to the existing CKN library
- update the comparator checker and documentation to verify the shared public definition layer, exact theorem types, clean Solution elaboration, and permitted axioms

The global weak-derivative hypothesis is formally stronger than the previous boxwise presentation, but it is the standard global formulation and is equivalent in the intended Euclidean open-domain setting by countable exhaustion and Fubini. The Solution only needs—and proves—the direct global-to-local restriction.

## Validation

- `python3 scripts/check_comparators.py`
  - source comparison passes for the 229-line Challenge
  - the Challenge has exactly the three intended proof placeholders
  - the Solution elaborates warning-free

author: lmriccardo
body:
## Summary

Fixes #96

`AssetManager::GetImage(virtualPath)` is cached by path, but `AssetManager::CreateTexture(renderer, image)` allocates a brand-new GPU texture on every call. Any caller that wants "the texture for this path" and doesn't carefully cache the result itself leaks one texture per call — one per frame, for an immediate-mode UI that runs every tick.

## Changes

- `src/ASGE/Game/Assets/AssetManager.hpp` / `.cpp` — adds `Result<video::ITexture*> GetTexture(str::StringCRef inVirtualPath, video::IRenderer& inRenderer)`, cached by virtual path like `GetImage`: first call resolves the image and creates the texture, later calls for the same path return the same pointer. A failed resolve/decode or texture creation is returned as-is and nothing is cached, matching `AssetPool::GetOrLoad`'s existing retry-on-failure behaviour — surfaces the underlying `VfsError`/`ImageError` from `GetImage`, or a new `RenderError::TextureCreationFailed` if the renderer itself fails.
- `src/ASGE/Game/Assets/AssetResolver.cpp` / `.hpp` — `Resolver<Sprite>` now routes through `GetTexture` instead of calling `GetImage` + `CreateTexture` directly, so two `Sprite`s sharing a texture path now share one GPU texture instead of each allocating their own.
- **`AssetManager::CreateTexture` (the uncached one-shot method) is removed.** It turned out to have no production caller left once `Resolver<Sprite>` moved to `GetTexture` — and font atlas textures never went through it either; every caller (`text_demo`, the render tests) creates and owns those directly via `IRenderer::CreateTexture`. Removing it collapses the storage model: `m_TextureCache` is now the *sole* owner of every texture `AssetManager` creates (`unordered_map<str::String, unique_ptr<ITexture>>` instead of a non-owning raw pointer into a separate vector).
- That collapse makes eviction trivial, so this also adds `AssetManager::UnloadTexture(virtualPath)` — a plain map erase, no scan for a matching raw pointer required. No-op if nothing is cached for that path.
- `tests/unit/Assets/AssetManagerTests.cpp` — `GetTextureTest` covers creation, same-path caching, different-path independence, unresolvable-path/renderer-failure both surfacing the right error without being cached, and the two new `UnloadTexture` behaviors; a `ResolveAssetsTest` case asserts two sprites with the same virtual path end up sharing one texture. The old `CreateTextureTest` suite is gone along with the method it tested.

Out of scope: the issue also asks to drop the level editor's hand-rolled `g_CachedPath`/`g_CachedTexture` preview cache (`editor/AssetInspector.cpp`) in favour of this. That code lives on the still-unmerged `feat/level_editor` branch, which doesn't exist on `main` — so that part will need to happen there once this lands.

## Testing

- `cmake --build --preset linux --target ASGE_AssetsTests` then ran it directly — all 46 tests in the Assets suite pass.
- `ctest --preset linux` — full suite, 995/995 passed.

author: alex-kopylov
body:
## Why

After `yolo-push` merges a PR, the head branch (local and remote) and its worktree stay behind. Deleting them by hand is where data gets lost: `git worktree remove` silently deletes ignored files such as `.env`, `git branch -d` rejects squash merges so people reach for `-D`, and a plain remote delete drops commits pushed after the merge.

## Changes

- `yolo-push` Workflow gains cleanup Steps 9–12, run after CD reaches a terminal state; the report moves to Step 13:
  9. Resolve PR facts (`gh pr view`), move to the main worktree, and skip cleanup unless the PR is `MERGED` and the branch is not the default one (GitHub branch protection blocks deleting protected branches).
  10. Check for irreversible losses, read-only: worktree files including ignored ones, local commits missing from the PR, remote commits pushed after the merge, and open PRs based on the branch.
  11. Ask the user one question with two options: delete the merged branch locally, on the remote, and its worktree, or keep everything.
  12. On delete, run the guarded deletions: `git worktree remove` without `--force`, `git branch -D` only when the branch is an ancestor of the PR head, and a remote delete with `--force-with-lease=<PR head>` that is skipped when open PRs target the branch.
- Codex parity: `agents/openai.yaml` sets `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`, matching `disable-model-invocation: true`; the unused "Use when…" trigger sentence is removed from the description.
- Reporting gains a `Cleanup:` line with the restore command.
- `tests/test_yolo_push_skill.py` extracts the skill's bash blocks and runs them against a sandbox repo with a stubbed `gh`. It checks that the checks delete nothing and report the findings, that the question has both options, and that the delete path removes only what the merged PR contains.
- `dev-workflow` 0.10.3 → 0.11.0; README catalog line updated.

## Validation

- [x] `uv run --python 3.12 pytest tests` (58 passed, 7 skipped)
- [x] Mutation check: removing the ancestor guard and the lease makes the `unmerged-work` test fail
- [x] `jq empty` on marketplace and plugin manifests
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [ ] Run `/yolo-push` end to end on a real PR and answer both options

## 背景

A8 `satisfies` 批次三仓之一。本仓已有先例 `src/config.ts:148`、`src/http/routes.ts:53` 用 `as const satisfies`，另有三张表仍以注解声明形状。

## 改动（3 处，纯类型层，+6 −6）

| 位置 | 原形态 | 新形态 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/config.ts:205` `THRESHOLD_PAIRS` | `readonly ThresholdPair[]` 注解 | `as const satisfies readonly ThresholdPair[]` |
| `src/client/settings/use-config-form.ts:124` 同名双胞胎 | 同上 | 同上 |
| `src/client/settings/BalanceSettingsCard.tsx:67` `GROUP_FIELDS` | `Readonly<Record<GroupKey, readonly string[]>>` | `as const satisfies Record<GroupKey, readonly string[]>` |

## 逐处收益与核对（消费方写入已全仓 grep 逐处读）

- **宿主表**：除「表不可再被 push」外有真实精度增益 —— `warn/critical` 由 `keyof Config`（11 键并集）收窄成具体键，`value[pair.warn]` 不再拿并集类型。写阈值的一行 `numeric[pair.warn] = pair.defaultWarn`（`resolveThresholdPairs`）写的是 **config 的数值视图**，不写表 ✓。消费方 `config.ts:235/:258`、`index.ts:112` 全是 `for..of` ✓。
- **客户端双胞胎**：`warn: string`（本半体刻意不用 `keyof Config`）→ 无 keyof 增益，只有不可追加 + 字面量；消费方 `:512 .some`、`:624 .find`、`Card:120 .some`、`Card:204 .find`、`test/threshold-pairs.test.ts` 的 `for..of`/`.find` ✓ 无写入。两份表之间的「抄写对账」仍由 `test/threshold-pairs.test.ts` 钉着，本刀不碰。
- **GROUP_FIELDS**：只读性由 `as const` 保住（不是减弱）；键穷尽性交给 `Record<GroupKey, …>`，联合键索引 `GROUP_FIELDS[key].some(...)`（`key: GroupKey`）实测合法（穷尽 Record + satisfies 不打断）；唯一消费方 `:118` 只读 ✓。

## 为什么不用单用 `satisfies`

编译器实测（探针落在系统临时目录，未进仓库）：单用 `satisfies` 时宽 `string` 字段被放宽、表仍可 `push` → 对这三张表零增益。`as const satisfies` 才给「外层只读 + 逐元素字面量」。**同时实测到一条边界**：`as const satisfies` 后，若目标字段声明为可变 `string[]`，内层数组会被拉回可变 → 不会打断把内层传给 `string[]` 形参的消费方（同批在 AI-tool-calling 那边验证）。

## 验证

- `npm run typecheck` rc=0（三段：宿主 / 客户端 / 测试）
- `npm test` rc=0：先 build 再 **30 文件 / 355 用例全绿**
- `git diff --check` 干净；三文件行尾保持 LF，无翻转；工作区无残留产物（`lib/` 被忽略）
- 未改文档：本仓 AGENTS 规定测试数字一律不抄进文档，无同步点；文件名/导出名未变，子目录 README 索引不受影响

## 一处环境说明

推送时 `github.com` 的 HTTPS git 通道不可达（`api.github.com` 与 SSH:22 正常），故该分支经 SSH 传输推上去——**同一提交 `08843dd`，未改任何 remote 配置**。

关联 A8 批次（AI-analytics 已合并 `40a73e9`；AI-tool-calling 随后，无 CI 需人工批）。

body:
Six of the eight open npm dependabot updates, applied together and verified once.

All eight touch `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so merging them individually forces a rebase and a full CI run on every other open one — seven round trips through `verify`, `integration`, four `design-system` shards and `visual regression`. This is the same set of upgrades in a single pass.

## Taken

| PR | Package | From | To |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #47 | jsdom | 26.1.0 | 30.1.1 |
| #46 | testcontainers | 11.14.0 | 12.1.0 |
| #45 | pino | 9.14.0 | 10.3.1 |
| #43 | graphql-yoga | 5.21.2 | 5.24.1 |
| #42 | @opentelemetry/sdk-node | 0.217.0 | 0.222.0 |
| #39 | wgc | 0.80.1 | 0.131.1 |

Close those six once this merges.

## Held back — and why

These two do not work. Finding that out is what this branch was for.

**#41, `@vitejs/plugin-react@6`.** It imports `vite/internal` and declares a peer of `vite@^8`. On Vite 7 the design system's test run dies at startup:

```
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './internal' is not defined
by "exports" in .../vite/package.json
imported from .../@vitejs/plugin-react/dist/index.js
```

This is a Vite 8 upgrade wearing a plugin bump, and Storybook 9, `apps/docs` and `apps/storybook` all come with it. It needs its own piece of work.

**#44, `@apollo/subgraph@2.15`.** It no longer exports `EntityType` from `dist/types`, which `@pothos/plugin-federation` imports — the plugin this repo already carries a patch for:

```
SyntaxError: The requested module '@apollo/subgraph/dist/types.js'
does not provide an export named 'EntityType'
  at tools/codegen/src/subgraph.ts
```

Subgraph codegen fails outright, which takes `just supergraph` and every module's schema with it.

**One extra change because of that second one.** The declared range was `^2.11.0`, which *allows* 2.15 — so the install picked it up regardless, and reverting the bump changed nothing. It is now pinned to `~2.14.3`, which is what actually holds. Lifting the pin means updating `patches/@pothos__plugin-federation@4.5.0.patch` first.

Leave #41 and #44 open; they are real work, not noise.

## Verified

`lint`, `check`, `check-strict`, `test` and `test-all` all exit 0 — including the integration suites, which matters here because testcontainers went up a major.

author: johnitvn
body:
## Description

Closes #29 — two fixes in one contract, because they are one mechanism:

**Store-scoped transactions.** The transaction context key was a package-scoped empty struct, so any `postgres.Store`'s `WithinTx` joined whatever transaction the context carried: with two stores over two pools, a nested `storeB.WithinTx` inside `storeA.WithinTx` silently wrote into store A's unit of work instead of beginning its own. The key now carries the pool that opened the transaction (`txKey{db *sql.DB}`), so a scope can only ever find a unit of work opened on its own pool — same pool joins, another pool begins and commits its own, deterministically. The nested-join rule in the port's `WithinTx` documentation now states exactly that.

**The transaction-bound query contract.** The port said repositories must "resolve the transaction from the context, never from the pool" but provided no mechanism. The port gains `Querier` — `ExecContext`/`QueryContext`/`QueryRowContext`, the small common ground of `*sql.DB` and `*sql.Tx`, no begin, no commit, no pool handle — and `Store.Querier(ctx)`, which resolves to the unit's transaction inside the scope and to the pool outside it. The join decision in `WithinTx` and the query resolution are the same lookup, so they cannot disagree; a repository holding only a `Querier` cannot reach around the transaction it belongs to. No private key, no `*sql.Tx`, no `*sql.DB` crosses the port.

The old carried-transaction test read the private key directly and proved nothing a repository could observe; it is replaced by driver-level proofs (the fake driver grew an `ExecerContext` so an exec's connection is observable): an exec inside the unit lands on the connection the transaction holds (exactly one connect), an exec outside it runs on the pool, and the cross-store tests pin per-driver begin/commit streams.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change fixing an issue)
- [ ] New capability in the gateway API
- [ ] Console (web) change
- [ ] OpenAPI contract change
- [ ] Breaking change (a consumer must edit configuration or code to upgrade)
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Build, CI, or repository tooling

## Contract impact

- [x] No API surface changes

The storage port's Go API grows (`Querier`, `Store.Querier`), but the HTTP/OpenAPI contract is untouched — the service serves the same three endpoints as before.

## How this was verified

**Steps:**

1. `cd apps/api && go test ./internal/storage/... -count=1` — 13 tests green, including the three new cross-store/leak tests and the two Querier-resolution tests.
2. Red-proof: with only the key lookup/insert mutated back to the legacy global-key semantics (`txKey{}` on both sides), exactly the three new tests fail — `TestNestedWithinTxOnADifferentStoreRunsItsOwnIndependentUnit`, `TestNestedWithinTxFailureOnADifferentStoreLeavesTheOuterVerdictToItsOwner`, `TestAStoreNeverHandsOutAnotherPoolsTransaction` — and the restored fix is green again.
3. `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` over the whole module — green.

- [x] Tests added or updated for behavioural changes, and I watched the new one fail before it passed
- [x] `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` all pass locally

body:
Stacked on #418: this PR changes the header/footer helper #418 adds, so it targets #418's branch. Retarget it to `gravitypdf` once #418 merges.

## Cause

With `forcePortraitHeaders`, `_puthtmlheaders()` turns a landscape page's header and footer a quarter turn, and turns their links with them. The link's `x` came out right, but its `y` was measured down the page from the wrong edge. On an A4 landscape page, a link in a rotated header sat about 110 mm away from its text: at y 184–237 while the text was drawn at y 500–553.

## Fix

The header is drawn with `0 -1 1 0 0 w cm`. That maps a point `X, Y`, measured up from the header's foot, to `Y, w - X` on the page. In `placeHtmlHeaderLinksAndAnnots()`, a link's rect is now turned with that same transform: its foot becomes its left edge, its left end becomes its top, and its width and height swap. That replaces the old six-step calculation. The comment describing the transform moves above both loops, since links and annotations now share it.

## How it was verified

A header and a footer, each holding a link and a note, were rendered on an A4 landscape page with `forcePortraitHeaders`. Each `/Rect` was compared with the text's position in the content stream, taken through the rotation `cm`, and the page was rasterised with Ghostscript. The link now spans y 500–553, matching the text, and the note sits at the end of it.

## Tests

In `tests/Mpdf/HtmlHeaderAnnotationTest.php`:
- `testALinkTurnsWithARotatedHeader` (header and footer): the link lands in the strip the margin leaves and starts at the side margin.
- `testAnAnnotationTurnsWithARotatedHeader` (header and footer): now also checks that the note is on the link's line and follows it. #418 checks the note against the page instead, since the link was misplaced there.

Against #418's branch, all 4 of these cases fail, and all 13 tests in the file pass with this change.

No snapshot fixture has a rotated header link, so none changed.

## Gates

This branch's tree is identical to #418's before it was split, where they passed:
- `composer test`: 3426 tests, 5 skipped
- `composer cs`: clean
- PHPStan: no errors
- PHP 5.6 lint of both changed files: clean

Form fields in a rotated header are still not turned. That is left for another change.

author: noah80
body:
Closes bead **hisim-cyc.3** (P2, mvp), which implements the owner decision of 2026-09-20: SEAI's solar PV grant is paid pro rata.

## Problem

SEAI pays **700 € per kWp up to 2 kWp, then 200 € per further kWp up to 4 kWp, at most 1,800 €**, pro rata. None of the engine's benefit kinds can express a capped amount per unit that changes by band. So `IE.json` approximated the grant with four `LUMP_SUM` steps on `measure.technical_attributes.peak_power_in_kwp`:

- they were exact only at 1, 2, 3 and 4 kWp;
- they were too low in between: 2.5 kWp, the page's own example, got 1,400 € instead of 1,500 €;
- they paid nothing below 1 kWp.

## What changes

- **New benefit kind `TIERED_PER_UNIT`** (`hisim/economics/subsidies/catalog.py`):
  - Its payload `TieredPerUnitBenefit` holds `tiers`, an ascending list of `{up_to, amount_per_unit}` in which only the last tier may be open (`up_to: null`), and an optional `cap_in_euro`.
  - Each tier pays its rate on the part of the size that falls inside it. The sum is then capped.
  - **The load refuses, naming the scheme:**
    - an empty or unsorted tier list;
    - an open tier before the last one;
    - a negative amount or a negative cap;
    - a cap below the first tier's full value, since no later tier could then ever pay;
    - a tier object with a missing or unknown key.
- **Solver** (`solver.py`): values the kind like `PER_UNIT`, on `ComponentCostFacts.size`, exact in every uncertainty slot, and clamped to the eligible-cost basis. `value_estimate` uses the same arithmetic.
- **The size is the right quantity for PV.** The adapter builds it from `PVSystem.power_in_watt` in kW, which is the same number the `peak_power_in_kwp` attribute published. Every array has it, so an array sized as a share of the roof is now priced too. Such an array has no attribute, and the old steps left it `undetermined`.
- **`IE.json`:**
  - The four `IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV_*` schemes become one `IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV`, with tiers `[{up_to: 2, amount_per_unit: 700}, {up_to: 4, amount_per_unit: 200}]` and `cap_in_euro: 1800`.
  - It keeps the same applicant and construction-year conditions and drops the peak-power condition.
  - `IE_SEAI_WARMER_HOMES` now excludes the new id instead of the four old ones. `python -m hisim.economics validate` flagged those.
- **Docs:** `README_IE.md` and the SEAI PV source note describe the tiered encoding. The comment on RenoVisor's `peak_power_in_kwp` attribute says that no shipped scheme reads it any more; the attribute stays, as a generic hook for conditions on array size.

## Behaviour change

The Irish PV grant goes up wherever the size falls between the old steps, for example 2.5 kWp now gets 1,500 € instead of 1,400 €. Arrays under 1 kWp now receive their pro-rata share. Arrays sized as a share of the roof are priced instead of coming out `undetermined`. The catalogue now has 45 schemes instead of 48.

## Tests

- `tests/economics/test_ie_catalog.py`:
  - 1 → 700, 2 → 1,400, 2.5 → 1,500, 3 → 1,600, 4 → 1,800 and 6 → 1,800.
  - 0.5 kWp → 350.
  - A 900 € array is clamped to its 990 € eligible basis.
- `tests/test_economics_subsidies.py::TestTieredPerUnitBenefit`: tier sums, an open last tier, parsing, every refusal, and that the shipped catalogue carries the single scheme.

What I ran locally:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python -m hisim.economics validate` | 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `tests/economics`, `tests/renovisor`, `tests/test_economics_*.py`, `tests/test_worked_examples.py` (`-m base`) | 1821 passed, 1 failed (below) |
| `tests/renovisor/test_staged_economics.py`, `test_run.py` (system_setups) | 34 passed |
| prospector on the changed files | 0 messages |
| pylint (`pylintrc-critical-only`) | 10.00/10 |
| mypy | no errors in the changed files |

The one failure is `test_contract.py::…::test_every_locally_vendored_file_equals_the_shared_one`, the known mockup mismatch against the contract checkout. It fails the same way on `main`, and #795 fixes it.

Once this is merged, contract todo H16 can be ticked.

body:
Closes #571

Depends on #570 (this PR's base).

## Summary
- `runner.Freezer` — an optional `Runner` capability, `FreezeSandbox`/`ThawSandbox` — pauses/resumes the **agent container only**; the proxy sidecar is never paused (it keeps renewing its token and answering egress decisions while the agent is frozen). Both are idempotent on a missing sandbox or a redundant call.
- Docker driver implements it via `ContainerPause`/`ContainerUnpause`.
- `runner.Capabilities.Freeze` / `substrate.ClassSupport.Freeze` report support **per confinement class**: `CC1` (runc) is `true` — the only runtime this is verified against (runc 1.4.3, cgroup v2, per the long-holds design doc §3.1); `runsc`/Kata-backed classes report `false` (unverified — RL-0). An operator CC1 pin away from runc also reports `false`.
- Kubernetes does not implement `Freezer` (no primitive; unsupported per the design). The orchestrator answers `ErrFreezeUnsupported` for a substrate that doesn't implement it.
- Orchestrator routes `FreezeSandbox`/`ThawSandbox` to the owning substrate and merges each substrate's per-class `Freeze` map into its aggregated `Capabilities` (same first-claim-wins rule as `Resolved`).

No caller decides *when* to pause a run yet — that's RL-7 (pause and resume), which this PR's capability primitive is scoped to unblock.

## Design
`/home/cjohn/wardyn-archive/mock-08/long-holds-design.md` rev 4, §3.1 ("Per runtime") and §8 (issue table, RL-6 = LH-5).

body:
## What

E5's acceptance line: *a parent files a leave request, the class teacher approves it, both are notified … rejected requests state a reason; CSV export.* The staff half is `hr.mjs`; the family half had HTTP tests and no walk, and the E-track plan said so.

`scripts/smoke/requests.mjs`, three logins: the parent files a request about their child and sees it pending with the child's name; the class teacher and the office are told in their notification centres; the office sees who asked and about whom, is refused a rejection with no reason, rejects with one, and the card shows the decision with its date and reason; the parent sees the rejection and is told; files a second; the office approves it; the parent sees it approved and is told; the CSV carries both. `SmokeMarkerSeeder::requestsCycle()`; `RequestsCycleSmokeResetTest`. Thirty-fifth walk.

## Five defects, all on the family's side of the one screen

1. **The wrong types.** Every type was offered to everyone, defaulting to *teacher leave*; a parent was refused with "a staff profile is required". The index now offers the two leave types only to a teacher/staff profile, and the staff fields only for staff leave.
2. **No child.** `regarding` was null for every family request. Families now choose *Regarding* from their own children; `BuildSchoolRequestPayloadAction` refuses any other pupil's id (People's `ListGuardianChildrenAction`, by Action — rule 3).
3. **Nobody told.** Filing told no one. `NotifyRequestSubmittedAction` tells everyone with `requests.review` and the class teacher of every class the pupil is active in, never the requester. Trilingual strings under `notifications.request`.
4. **An empty rejection.** `ReviewSchoolRequestAction` now refuses a rejection with no reason, and says so.
5. **A card with no answer.** `ListSchoolRequestsAction` adds who asked (to reviewers), about whom, when, and the decision with its date and reason. The CSV grows `regarding_*`, `submitted_at`, `reviewed_by`, `review_notes`.

## Owner decision

Who approves a family's request. The acceptance line says the class teacher; today teachers and parents hold `requests.submit` only and the office holds `requests.review`. A global teacher review permission would let them decide staff leave too, so the right shape is the plan's per-type approver rule — recorded as plan owner decision 9. Until then the class teacher is told and the office decides, which is what the walk asserts.

## Verified

`requests.mjs` 23/23 twice on a re-seeded database; `hr.mjs`, `sweep.mjs`, `family.mjs` green on the reshaped form; `RequestFamilyHalfTest` (4); full suite 2087 passed. Built assets committed. STATUS §5fw, §2 S2.10 row, `docs/EDUPAGE_FEATURES_PLAN.md`.

## Summary

Expose Objective-C Foundation classes under the Swift names used by OpenCombineFoundation and OpenSwiftUICore: `NotificationCenter`, `OperationQueue`, `Operation`, `BlockOperation`, `URLResponse`, `URLSessionDataTask`, and `Bundle`.

Mark `NSURLRequest` as bridging to the Swift `URLRequest` value type so Swift callers can pass a request to Objective-C APIs such as `URLSession.dataTask(with:completionHandler:)`. This depends on the real Swift `URLRequest` overlay in [darling-swift PR #52](https://github.com/VibeDarling/darling-swift/pull/52). Mark `NSBundle.mainBundle` nonoptional in the header so Swift imports `Bundle.main` as a usable value. The Swift overlay's internal adoption of `Bundle` is in [darling-swift PR #54](https://github.com/VibeDarling/darling-swift/pull/54).

These API notes affect the Clang/Swift importer. They do not change Objective-C class identity or runtime behavior. Closes VibeDarling/darling#826 and advances VibeDarling/darling#819.

## Verification

- A Swift 6.3.3 arm64 macOS typecheck probe fails to resolve the original six class names without the API notes and passes with them.
- With the adapted open source `URLRequest` overlay module, `URLSession.dataTask(with: URLRequest)` fails before the `SwiftBridge` note and typechecks after it.
- A focused `Bundle.main`/localization Swift probe typechecks with the new API note. The complete arm64 Foundation overlay builds and links with the dependent Swift PR #54; its Bundle guest test exits 0 in the combined Darling prefix.
- All 5,088 prior arm64 Foundation overlay exports remain after the Bundle rebuild. The target-aware OpenSwiftUI build no longer reports missing `Bundle` type errors, but `OpenSwiftUICore` still has other API gaps.

This PR does not claim a working SwiftUI.framework or AppZapper runtime.

author: razvan-danit-tq
body:
Internal patched build of Apache Jena, published as `6.2.0-tq-2`. Cumulative on top of `6.2.0-tq-1`: it carries the journal write-back fix from #5 as well as this one.

`BPTreeNodeMgr.formatBPTreeNode` decoded a node with relative `position()`, `limit()`, `slice()` and `rewind()` calls on `block.getByteBuffer()`. That returns the block's single buffer instance, and the same `Block` is shared across transactions: after a writer commits while readers are active, later transactions are stacked on its `BlockMgrJournal`, whose `getRead` hands out its `writeBlocks` entries directly (`BlockMgrCache.getRead` shares cached blocks the same way in direct file mode).

When the next writer takes such a block for writing, `BlockMgrJournal._promote` copies it via `Block.replicate`, which moves the shared buffer's position and limit without holding the block monitor. A reader decoding the same block at that moment slices the wrong byte range and reads a garbage child pointer. It surfaces as `BlockException: BlockAccessBase: Bounds exception` on `node2id.dat`, from `find()` in a read transaction with no journal replay involved.

The fix uses absolute `slice(index, length)`, so decoding neither reads nor changes the shared buffer's position. Six lines in, twelve out, and no lock.

Tracked as DEV-1347. This is the second race described in DEV-1230, the one the write-back patch does not address; it has its own ticket because it is a separate Jena bug with its own symptoms. The approach is the one sketched in DEV-1230.

**Validation**

- jena-tdb1 suite on this branch: 1005 tests, 0 failures.
- Reproduction harness from DEV-1230, 10 runs of 300s per build on 4 pinned cores: `6.2.0-tq-1` failed 2 of 10, both `BlockException` on `node2id.dat` with no data loss; `6.2.0-tq-2` failed 0 of 10.
- Independent earlier run at 60s on 12 cores: 5 of 60 versus 0 of 60.

**Not urgent.** Master is on `6.2.0-tq-1` and that build is being observed. This is ready whenever it is wanted; `tq-1` remains published and tagged, so moving between them is a one-line change to `ver.jena`.

(Supersedes #6, which was merged prematurely by mistake and has been undone — `base-jena-6.2.0` is back at the `tq-1` state.)

body:
## Request (owner)
Polish the look of the town, cars and trees so it fits the apocalypse, and send before/after images of the map for comparison.

## What changed
- **Ground, roofs and floors:** asphalt, concrete, lawn, roofs and floors are small tiled pixel-art textures sampled with nearest-neighbour, at 4 world units per texel.
- **Tinting:** roof, car and tree textures are drawn grey and tinted at runtime, so each building, car and tree keeps its own colour.
- **Props:**
  - cars: 4 body styles, each with a broken-into and a burnt version;
  - trees: 3 crown shapes;
  - bins, pumps, rooftop units, manholes, drains, oil stains, cracks, litter and dried blood.
- **Shadows:** soft 9-slice images. The lit roof slope and the kerb and parapet shadows follow the sun, or the survivor's light at night.
- **Renderer** (`shared/engine/renderer.ts`): any pooled sprite can carry an image. The image layer is created once per slot and reused, so draw order is unchanged and nothing is created per frame.
- **Fallback:** each texture falls back on its own to today's flat drawing until it has an asset id (`client/view/worldArt.ts`). Gameplay is untouched: no solid, collision box or generator rule changed. A car's state comes from a hash of its position, so every client draws it the same.
- **Zombie outline (live now, not tied to the upload):** zombie bodies and arms get a near-black outline for LEG-03. A walker's outline used to be almost the lawn colour; its contrast on grass doubles (15 → 30).
- **Tools:**
  - `npm run art:world` generates the textures and `worldArtAssets.ts`;
  - `npm run render:map` renders the town to PNG with the real drawing code;
  - `npm run cloud -- upload-art [--dry-run]` uploads new or changed textures through the Open Cloud Assets API. The key is never printed and a dry run never reads it.
- **Before/after:** `docs/art/before`, `docs/art/after` and `docs/art/compare` (street, downtown, park, school, gas, wreck, street-night, overview).
- **Merge with main:**
  - CLAUDE.md keeps the hud and lobby suites and adds world-art;
  - `main.client.ts` keeps the lobby's netClient import and adds `preloadWorldArt`.

## Cost (dense downtown, 1920×1080)
- Sprites on screen: 167 → 170, of which 137 now show an image.
- Instances in the pool: 283 → 353.
- Property writes while panning: 217 → 272 per frame.
- Still camera: 0 writes. Instances created after warm-up: 0.

## Testing
- New `test:world-art`, also added to CI together with a check that the generated files are up to date:
  - with no asset ids, the drawing matches golden hashes of the flat town from before;
  - with ids, the textures draw at the right size, and each one falls back on its own;
  - no Instance churn over 600 frames;
  - LEG-03 legibility on 7 ground types.
