author: dviejokfs
body:
## Description

Console startup previously awaited every retained log WAL batch, including slow storage writes and database retries. Initialize the log writer without replaying WAL, then recover in the background so console startup can finish immediately.

Log collectors and maintenance wait for successful recovery. Writes, container removal, and purge are gated so replay cannot overwrite new heads or resurrect purged logs. Existing committed logs remain readable.

Recovery classifies errors before retrying. Validation, invalid configuration, not-found, deterministic I/O, and format failures stop with an actionable error. Damaged or deferred WAL keeps the existing 10-minute repair check, allowing recovery to resume after an in-place repair. Both paths retain WAL and keep collection and purge paused. Transient failures use the shared `RetryConfig` exponential backoff, starting at 30 seconds and capped at 10 minutes. Inner persistence retries also stop immediately for permanent failures.

No database migration or new configuration is required.

## Validation

- Full log-aggregator library suite: 300 passed, 2 existing ignored.
- `cargo check --lib -p temps-log-aggregator` and full-workspace `cargo check --lib` passed. Existing workspace profile, debug web-build, and dependency future-compatibility notices remain.
- Mandatory commit hooks passed, including all-targets/all-features Clippy with `-D warnings`.
- Independent correctness and security review approved the retry classification and retained-WAL safety.
- Full application/browser startup was not exercised. The startup regression invokes production plugin initialization with a blocked manifest sink.

## Evidence

```sh
cargo test --lib -p temps-log-aggregator
```

```text
test result: ok. 300 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; finished in 74.50s
```

The new terminal-error regression advances the paused clock by 601 seconds, verifies the recovery task exits, and checks exactly one persistence attempt, retained WAL, and readiness remaining false:

```sh
cargo test --lib -p temps-log-aggregator background_recovery_stops_after_one_permanent_failure_and_retains_wal -- --nocapture
```

```text
1 passed; 0 failed; finished in 0.03s
```

The transient regression uses a typed database connection failure, then restores the dependency and verifies recovery completes without WAL loss:

```sh
cargo test --lib -p temps-log-aggregator background_recovery_retries_failed_pass_without_losing_wal -- --nocapture
```

```text
1 passed; 0 failed; finished in 5.29s
```

Existing regressions cover nonblocking plugin startup, write/purge/removal protection, post-recovery ingestion, retained corrupt WAL, no-WAL startup, and contextual HTTP error mapping.


The recovery group also verifies that repairing a retained `.recovery-wal` generation in place resumes collection on the 600-second repair check, without duplicate manifests:

```sh
cargo test -p temps-log-aggregator background_recovery_ --lib -- --nocapture
```

```text
7 passed; 0 failed; finished in 5.30s
```

author: stevevitali
body:
# S3.4d — the Hosting ABI schemas (`hh-hosting`): `HostedEvent` + I-1..I-5 validators, `proj_ABI`/`lift` over the single `HOSTED_LOWERING` column, `ConformanceRecord`/`AdapterRecord`/`ParticipantRecord` (registry opaque arms + `hosted_entries`), adapter zero, `requires_capabilities`/`requires_mediation` wired to scorecard applicability, and the `MatchSpec` enforceability AC battery (R-2.10.6⁰)

**Spec:** `spec/CANONICAL_SPEC.md` §6.6 (the `hh-hosting/1` Hosting ABI) ·
§6.4 (scorecard applicability) · §2.9 (envelopes)
**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/050_S3.4d__hosting-abi-schemas.md`
**Requirement ids stamped:** **R-2.10.6⁰**
**Base:** `svitali/harnessharness-s3.4c` (stacked) · **Stage:** 3 ·
**Live stage:** offline-only (all checks hermetic)
**ADR:** `docs/adr/ADR-0281-s3.4d-hosting-abi-schema-rulings.md`

## Summary

**The schema half of the Hosting ABI lands; the service does not.**
`hh-hosting` is a new leaf crate carrying `HostedEvent` (the opaque
participant's event envelope) with the I-1..I-5 validators — lifecycle
completeness with `ensure_terminal` synthesis of unobserved terminals,
dense sequence, extension preservation (unknown/`_`-prefixed members
round-trip verbatim, never coerced), the authority ceiling (claims above
`delegate` only on kernel-gated `intercept`/`environment` origins over
closed-schema kinds; `mediated` is inadmissible on participant/adapter
claims), and hosted stamping. Unknown hosted kinds are never dropped —
`lift` maps them to `lifecycle.hosted.native_record` with the raw kind
and payload preserved.

**One class list — the lowering is a column, not a second registry.**
`proj_ABI` reads `HOSTED_LOWERING`, a new column on `hh-ledger`'s class
table (typed kind | passthrough | hint | none), so the lowering policy is
single-sourced (CC7) and exhaustive by construction. `project` takes the
session's declared observability: `model.call.*`/`model.stream.*` —
*including* hint rows, whose `ext.source` embed would otherwise smuggle
model I/O — emit no row when `model_io` is undeclared, declared in the
`LoweringLossReport` (`observability-gated`), never silently absent.

**Records layer through the registry as opaque bodies.**
`RegistryRecord::{Participant, Adapter}` store canonical `Json` behind a
`kind`-tag gate — `hh-hosting` owns the §6.6 schemas, the registry never
re-owns them. The typed exception is `ConformanceReport.hosted_entries`:
`ConformanceRecord` derives its verdict (`drift` iff both sides concrete
and differing; `unknown`/`skipped` never coerce), the codec re-derives
and refuses authored drift, `hosted_entries` is legal only on a
`subject_kind = participant` report pinned to a registered participant,
and a version bump re-derives conformance rather than inheriting it.
`ParticipantRecord.version_identity` is derived, not authored.
**Adapter zero** is the deterministic intercepted fixture over a native
run — AC-R-2.10.6-2 lifts it and asserts `metric_view` byte-parity on
every metric inside its declared observability and `n/a{observability}`
on the rest.

**Applicability gates are now real.** `EvalRun.mediation` populates from
`ResultsRow.coordinates.mediation` (native rows are fully mediated —
the kernel owns every channel; hosted rows carry only their declared
channels); `render_cell` calls `applicability_at`, so
`requires_mediation` (`veto.permission_violation` → `mediated(effects)`),
`requires_capabilities` (`n/a{capability}` when unbound), and
`applies_to_classes` (the seven hosted-only declarations;
`duplicate_effect`/`audit_completeness` native-only) all produce typed
`n/a` — never zero, never a proxy.

**AC-R-2.10.6-6 exercises the landed `MatchSpec` gate:** a matched-cap
dimension with `unenforceable`/`advisory` enforcement refuses
`IncommensurableMatch{Unenforceable}`; interception-derived `enforced`
accepts.

## Also in this change

- `hh-ontology`: `InfraErrorFamily::Participant`, `HostingMechanism`,
  `CapabilityVerdict`, `MediationChannel`/`MediationRequirement`,
  `EnforcementLevel::parse` (additive codecs).
- `check-removability.sh`: new `removability(hosting)` arm —
  `hosting_edges = []`, the tier removes clean.

## Deferred (unchanged)

The handshake, baseline/capability verbs, probes P-01…P-16, quarantine,
hosted launch, `budget_enforcement` derivation, and Adapter A+ stay at
S4.5a; the hosted-metric folds arrive with the service (declarations are
schema now and render honest `n/a`). DF-S1.3-2 keeps OPEN — the
`≤ delegate` mint needs the vouching service.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check` · `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` (150 result
lines, 0 failures — `hh-hosting` 16/16) · `cargo clippy -D warnings` ·
`check-drift` · `check-removability` (incl. the hosting edge-free arm) ·
build-memory check — all green. Offline-only throughout.

body:
Adds **Pavilion event concierge** under Amos Bar-Joseph: a skill an attendee runs in Claude (or any agent) to turn the Pavilion GTM2026 Summit program into a personal agenda as a living HTML app. Pavilion will share this with their attendees.

## What ships

- `SKILL.md` as used in production (only the frontmatter was extended with `title` and `category`, and the description reworded to the marketplace's "Use this skill when" form; the procedure is untouched).
- The complete session database for GTM2026 (`references/events/gtm2026/`: event file, venue and logistics, four day files, every session card).
- The Swan x Pavilion plan template (`references/plan-template.html`), the two helper scripts, the raw CSV exports the build script rebuilds from, and the logo files.

The files are shipped **as-is** on purpose: Claude Desktop and other hosts need the template and the database exactly where the skill expects them. This is the version that was run end to end and reproduced the reference asset.

## Validator change

`tools/validate.mjs` now allows `.html` and `.webp` alongside the existing extensions. A skill that ships a runnable template and brand assets could not be submitted otherwise.

## Checklist

body:
**1 of 7** in the semester planning backend (P-WEB-8). Based on `main` (the schema from #296 is merged). This PR adds groundwork only: no public functions yet.

## What's in it
- **`semesterPlanning/rules.ts`** (pure)
  - `TRANSITIONS` / `canTransition`: the allowed status changes. A confirmed application can only be withdrawn; to move it, the editor withdraws, reopens and sends a new offer.
  - `isValidOrgNumber` (9 digits, MOD11), `normalizeOrgNumber`, `toCompanyOrgNumber` (company profiles store it as a number)
  - `STUDENT_CAP` per event type, `STATUS_LABELS`, `FORM_VERSION`, `CONSENT_VERSION`
- **`semesterPlanning/helper.ts`**
  - `transitionStatus`: the only code that writes `status`. It refuses forbidden changes with a Norwegian error and always writes a `status_changed` history row.
  - `logActivity`, `findLiveApplicationOnDate` (the double-booking check), `supersedePendingOffers`
- **`lib/tokens.ts`**: `generateToken` (256-bit, base64url) and `hashToken` (SHA-256). `feedback/tokens.ts` now re-exports `hashToken` as `hashFeedbackToken`, so there's one implementation.
- **`@workspace/shared/semester/time`**: `osloToday`, `osloDateTimeToEpoch`, `tuesdaysAndThursdays`, `nextTermAfter`, `isIsoDate`. The helpers never invent semester dates or deadlines; a human sets those in Bifrost.
- **Test fixtures**: `insertSemester`, `insertApplication`, `applicationById`, `activityFor`

## Tests
- Every allowed and forbidden status pair (table-driven)
- Org number check digits
- Tuesdays and Thursdays across Easter and daylight saving
- The Oslo day around midnight, and Oslo time in winter and summer
- Token uniqueness and hashing
- `transitionStatus` writes exactly one history row, and nothing when it refuses
- The double-booking lookup ignores withdrawn applications and other semesters

Updated for the renamed schema fields (`type`/`actor` on activity rows, `wantsToUseEscape`, `foodPurchasedBy`). Also fixes the two SonarCloud findings in `lib/tokens.ts`: `fromCodePoint` instead of `fromCharCode`, and no backtracking regex.

`pnpm --filter @workspace/backend check-types` and `test` pass (304 tests on current `main`).



## Review fixes

- `semester/time.ts` now uses date-fns (`parse`, `format`, `eachDayOfInterval`, `isTuesday`/`isThursday`) in the Oslo time zone instead of hand-written ISO parsing and UTC day arithmetic. Parsing is strict, and a time in the spring-forward gap is now refused.
- Removed the `hashFeedbackToken` re-export (`feedback/tokens.ts`). Feedback imports `hashToken` from `lib/tokens`, so there is one name and one implementation. `api.d.ts` is regenerated for the removed module.
- The activity `Actor` and details types are derived from the schema, and the fixtures use `FORM_VERSION`/`CONSENT_VERSION`.
- Simplified the org number check-digit comparison.

author: sunilpawar-git
body:
## Summary
Two follow-ups from the Google sign-in investigation (#84, #85).

### 1. Workspace list load can no longer hang forever
`useWorkspaceLoading` waited on Firestore and IndexedDB with no timeout. On Safari, a stuck local cache left the sidebar showing only "Untitled Workspace" and the canvas stuck on "Loading…", with **no error logged**.

- **15 s budget.** On timeout the app shows the **cached workspace list** from IndexedDB metadata, plus a warning toast with **Retry**.
- **A late fresh list still wins.** If the real load finishes after the timeout, it replaces the cached list.
- **Retry** re-runs the load. Results that arrive after unmount are ignored.
- **Split into helpers.** The 85-line `load()` now meets the 50-line function limit. Normal-path behaviour is unchanged, and the existing auto-select regression tests pass.

### 2. Turnstile "Cannot find Widget" warning
`useTurnstile` removed the widget's container on unmount but never called `turnstile.remove()`, so Turnstile's timers logged warnings after sign-in. The widget is now removed before its container.

## Test plan
- [x] New `useWorkspaceLoading.timeout.test.ts` (6 tests): in-time load, hung list load, hung IndexedDB, late success, Retry, unmount
- [x] `useTurnstile.lifecycle.test.ts`: widget removed on unmount, and no `remove` call when no widget was rendered
- [x] `npm run check`: 659 files / 17,821 tests; `lint:strict` clean
- [ ] After deploy: no "Cannot find Widget" warning after sign-in in Chrome

body:
This PR improves the map screen’s user-location navigation and makes returning to a previous property view more reliable. Tapping the user-location button now centers the user’s location marker consistently, while preserving the exact previous map position for a quick return.

## Correctif

Avec ccache (ou sccache) dans le `PATH`, toute compilation GCC/Clang échouait :

```
ccache: unknown option -- g
```

`_DetectCompilerCache` **remplaçait** `ccPath`/`cxxPath` par `ccache` seul ; la commande devenait `ccache -c -o x.o -g ... x.cpp` (sans `g++`) et ccache lisait les drapeaux comme les siens. `CCACHE_CC`/`CCACHE_CXX` n'existent pas dans ccache.

Désormais la toolchain garde le vrai compilateur et `Builder._WithCompilerLauncher` place le cache en tête des seules commandes de compilation (Linux, macOS, MinGW, clang Windows hors clang-cl). Édition de liens et MSVC inchangés.

author: askalf
body:
GitHub keeps at most **one pending run per concurrency group** and cancels the older pending one when another arrives, whatever `cancel-in-progress` says. The groups added in the Actions-audit PR were keyed on `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` for every event. So with a main-branch run A in progress and B queued, a third push C cancelled B, and a scheduled CodeQL run could be replaced the same way. The comment promised default-branch results were never dropped; a queued one could be. (Found by the second-opinion review.)

Now the group is `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.ref || github.run_id }}`:
- PR runs share one group per branch, and `cancel-in-progress` (still true for PRs only) cancels the superseded run.
- Every push and schedule run gets its own group (its run id), so none is ever replaced or cancelled.

Validated: every workflow in the repo parses, and actionlint 1.7.7 is clean.

author: chidirnweke
body:
## Why

Note publication checked an unlocked revision, recorded its snapshot, then reread and updated the whole note. A concurrent edit could change which revision was published or be overwritten. Archived notes could also be published.

## What changed

Notes locks the authoritative note before checking the ETag and preparing publication. It records that exact snapshot and persists only resolved publication fields in one transaction. The repository retains actor, expected-revision and active-note guards. Archived publication now fails explicitly.

The catalog and shared fakes receive resolved publication values. Existing history retention, attachment snapshots and repeated-publication timestamp behavior remain intact. This depends on #184 and needs no migration. Public commands and responses are unchanged.

## Evidence

The archived-note regression failed before the fix because publication succeeded. Unit tests cover rejection and snapshot rollback. PostgreSQL contracts hold an edit or archive open while publication waits, then verify that the peer's state survives and no snapshot is added. A third contract rejects the publication update after snapshot creation and verifies transaction rollback.

## Validation

- Focused regressions: 33 files, 291 tests passed.
- Type checks passed.
- PostgreSQL contracts run in CI because the local Docker socket is unresponsive.
- Lint, architecture audits and documentation checks passed; docs report one existing hint.
- Full local unit suite: 429 files, 4,028 tests passed.
- [All required CI checks passed](https://github.com/ChidiRnweke/FollowThrough.ai/actions/runs/35884778949), including PostgreSQL contracts, full browser tests and PWA sync.

author: fbhadha
body:
The first live test on GitHub Copilot felt like the default agent: no view of its own, no pushback, no grill, no tickets, nothing explained. There were two causes.

1. **On Copilot the agent mostly didn't run.** A scripted run of Copilot CLI 1.0.88 found three problems:
   - The README's `copilot --agent python-dev` fails, because the real id is `python-dev:python-dev`.
   - Plugin hooks ran in the plugin's install folder instead of the repo, so the main-branch guard, the shaping guard and the stop gate never fired.
   - The session-start line never reached the model.
2. **Where it did run, the persona held back.** It was written to:
   - say one sentence per step and give way after two objections;
   - hand the whole flow to Matt Pocock's `to-spec` and `to-tickets`, which only a person can start and which leave file paths and code out of specs and tickets by design.

Design decisions 47 to 52 and ADR 0007 record what changed.

## What changes

**A senior engineer's loop, on every message** (`agents/python-dev.md`)
- The first line says what kind of message it is: new idea, revision, ticket, bug, question or upkeep.
- No ticket, no code. A one-line fix gets a one-line ticket.
- It gives its view before asking anything: whether to build it at all, what to build and what to leave out, the alternatives it rejected, risks, one-way doors and size.
- It explains every decision and plan in full, shows the exact plan before any code, and asks in rounds of at most five questions, each with its recommended answer, the reason and the cost.
- Pushback comes in three tiers: whether to build it at all, the design, and process.
- The first reply opens with a status line, so you can tell it apart from the default agent.
- How much it explains is set in `mode.md`: `explain: decisions | teach | brief`.

**python-dev runs the flow itself** (`py-shape`, `py-build`, ADR 0007)
- `py-shape` does all of this in one session:
  - reads the code;
  - gives its view and grills you;
  - writes the spec (`references/spec.md`: the design at the level of modules, types and interfaces, plus the order of work);
  - shows a breakdown table for your yes;
  - writes the tickets (`references/ticket.md`).
- Every ticket's plan names the files, the signatures, the tests in the order they get written (with where each expected value comes from), and the commands.
- New route for revisions: a change to something already decided is grilled again and the spec and tickets are updated before any code.
- New route for quick tickets: a small, clear change gets a short ticket and goes straight to build.
- `py-build` checks the plan against the code, shows it and asks "Go?", then builds one slice at a time.
- `py-design` gains `references/planning.md` (the order of work) and `references/boundaries.md` (timeouts, retries, parsing, errors, config, logs, contract tests).
- `upstream.json` drops `grill-with-docs`, `grilling`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `implement`, `handoff` and `writing-for-agents`.

**The hooks** (`scripts/hooks/`)
- Every hook runs inside the project named in the payload's `cwd`.
- Session start emits JSON in both harnesses' shapes and names the plugin's scripts folder.
- Each hook command exits 0 when its script or `python3` is missing. VS Code never fills in the plugin-root path for this plugin, and on its Local target a hook exiting 2 denied every tool call.
- New `guard_edit.py`: in a repo intake has set up, the harness asks before an edit to `src/`, `tests/` or any `.py` outside `prototypes/` unless the branch is a ticket, prototype or intake branch.

**Every agent in the repo works ticket-first.** The `AGENTS.md` template gains `## How work happens here`. Copilot's default agent reads it too, and intake proposes it for repos set up earlier.

**The data-engineering pack is populated.**
- Four how-tos: add a source, a transform, a sink, a pipeline.
- An example package that intake copies into the repo: a CSV export loaded incrementally into SQLite.
  - 44 tests, including one contract suite per port.
  - 97% line and branch coverage; three deliberate bugs each fail the suite.
  - Green under the baseline's pytest, ruff and `mypy --strict`.
- Ten design rules and eight more faults.
- Orchestrators, dbt and Spark are named as not yet covered.

**Docs**
- The README covers the correct Copilot CLI and VS Code setup.
- New `docs/smoke-test.md` is the release gate: a fixed first-session script run by hand on each harness with a real model.
- The persona's size limit rises from 10,000 to 14,000 characters (it is about 12,000), about 700 more tokens per turn. CI also checks that the version in its status line matches the manifests.

## Checks

- `render_agents.py --check`, `check_plugin.py`: pass.
- `test_hooks.py`: 76 checks pass. The new ones fail on the 0.10.0 hooks.
- `check_pack_examples.py`: pass on Python 3.12, ruff 0.16.8 and mypy 1.19.1.
- `check_upstream_skills.py`, `check_template_deps.py`: pass.
- `claude plugin validate --strict .`: pass.

## Not yet done

- The smoke test with a real model on Copilot CLI, VS Code and Claude Code. The Copilot run covered install, the agent id and hooks with a scripted model only.
- VS Code behaviour was read from its source, not run.

author: xzzz
body:
## Summary

`i_am_webservice()` returns true for `USAGE_MODE_JSON` and `USAGE_MODE_REST` but not for `USAGE_MODE_MOJO_REST`, so all call sites treat native Mojo REST requests as browser requests.

Split out of bug [2072313](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2072313) at review request: the change flips behaviour for every `USAGE_MODE_MOJO_REST` endpoint at once rather than for the single endpoint being migrated, so it does not belong inside a migration PR. This PR stands on its own and does not depend on any other open PR.

## Changes

- `Bugzilla/Util.pm`: add `USAGE_MODE_MOJO_REST` to `i_am_webservice()`
- `qa/t/rest_components.t`: assert the exact `auth_failure` message on an unprivileged `POST /rest/component/Firefox`. At 110 characters it is long enough that an exact match fails while the 72-column wrap is applied
- `qa/t/rest_github_push_comment.t`: set `restrict_comments` on a bug, fire a push event against it, and assert a user outside `restrict_comments_group` still cannot react to the resulting comment

## Behaviour changes

Three call sites change observably for native REST endpoints:

- `Bugzilla/Template.pm:866`: the `error_message` filter no longer wraps at 72 columns, so error messages over that length stop coming back with embedded `\n`s. This is the motivating fix, but it is a response-shape change for already-shipped endpoints
- `extensions/RestrictComments/Extension.pm:58`: `object_end_of_set_all` stops force-clearing `restrict_comments` on bug updates made through `Bugzilla/API/V1/Github.pm:364` and `extensions/PhabBugz/lib/API/V1/PhabBugz.pm:235`. Both run as users granted every group, so `_can_restrict_comments()` is always true there, and `Bugzilla->input_params` is never populated on the native Mojo path -- meaning the field is currently cleared on every touched bug. Covered by the new test
- `Bugzilla.pm:593`: `log_user_request` starts logging native REST requests when `log_user_requests` is enabled, which will increase the volume written to that log

The MFA and password-reset branches (`Bugzilla.pm:265`, `:285`, `:305`, `Bugzilla/Auth.pm:91`) and the Quicksearch shortcuts (`Bugzilla/Search/Quicksearch.pm:342`, `:367`) are corrected in the same pass. The `Bugzilla::Auth::Login::*` and `Bugzilla::Auth::Verify::DB` call sites are unreachable under `USAGE_MODE_MOJO_REST`, since native REST authenticates through `Bugzilla/App/Plugin/Login.pm`.

## Test plan

- `POST /rest/component/Firefox` as a user without `editcomponents`, expect 401 and a `message` with no embedded newline
- Set `restrict_comments` on a bug, send a `push` webhook naming it, confirm the restriction survives the automation update

author: builtbybasit
body:
Until now the server spent money through the real providers and recorded none of it, and the budget a person set on a book was stored but held nothing back. This closes both of those items on the "what is not done yet" list.

**Metering.** A provider reports each request it put on the wire through `sent` on its input (`server/providers/sent.ts`). It reports whether the request was answered or refused, with the attempts `call` made, whether any was a 429, and the usage the provider gave. The job settles each report into `requests` (`server/usage/ledger.ts`) using `src/lib/pricing.ts` as it is, at the rates on the stored card when the request completed. What counts follows what a provider bills:
- An answer refused after a 200 (cut off at the length limit, a failed fidelity check) is priced from its usage.
- A chat request that failed on the wire costs nothing.
- A failed speech request is charged for what it sent on per-character, per-byte and per-request endpoints, and nothing on per-minute ones.
- A request refused before sending, or cancelled mid-flight, has no row.

Each part of a split line gets its own row, as does each chunk of a chapter. The fakes report too, marked `simulated`, so budgets can be tested and demoed without a key.

**Budgets.** `server/usage/budget.ts` asks one question: does this fit within what has been spent plus what unfinished jobs hold, priced at the undiscounted worst case? It asks at two points:
- **Before anything is queued.** It checks the whole run, including retakes. A paused book refuses everything, scripting must also fit the script budget, and a run that doesn't fit gets a 409 with a sentence the toast shows, and nothing is queued.
- **Before every request a running job sends.** The job's own hold is left out of the total. The job stops, keeping what it already paid for, when the cap was lowered, the book was paused, or a request cost more than it held.

Jobs hold their reservation in `jobs.reserved` (now written with the row) and give it back as chunks and lines settle.

**Reading it.** `GET /api/books/:id/spend` and `GET /api/endpoints/requests?kind&id&range`. In backend mode the jobs store's `spent`/`reserved`/`scriptSpent`/`scriptReserved` answer from the server (`useBookSpend`, `useLibrarySpend`), and the Endpoints page's Activity list and charts read the ledger (`useEndpointHistory`). Demo mode is unchanged. The narration worst case moved to `src/lib/narrationCost.ts`, shared by the store and the server.

**Still open** (listed in `docs/backend.md`):
- An endpoint's daily `spendLimit` is shown but not enforced, in the demo as on the server.
- Sibling chunks aborted by a failed chunk leave no row.
- `opening_spend` has no writer.

No schema change and no migration. Tests: `tests/server/usage.test.ts` and `tests/server/narrationBudget.test.ts` are new, and `chatScripting`, `endpointSpeech`, `jobs` and `jobsBackend` are extended. Suite: 1039 pass, 10 skipped (live), 0 fail; lint, typecheck, build and fmt are clean. Not checked in a browser.

author: jdegreef
body:
## What

An offline-first **sync indicator** for the Notebook, so readers know their prayers are safe.

**Page-level status** (under the Notebook's date, next to Print):
- Signed out: 📱 **Saved on this device only.** · *Sign in to keep it safe*
- Offline: ⚡ **You're offline — everything is saved on this device.** (or "Offline — N to sync when you're back")
- Waiting: ⏳ **N waiting to sync** · *Sync now*
- Synced: ☁ **All synced**

**Per entry** (signed in only; when signed out the page-level line covers it once): **📱 On this device** until the account has the entry, then a quiet ☁ ("Synced to your account").

**Delivering what is owed.** This builds on the pending map from #3093.
- New `readingSync.flushJournal()` PUTs each owed entry, newest first, one at a time, and stops at the first failure (the connection has gone again).
- It runs:
  - on the window `online` event;
  - after the sign-in merge, for whatever didn't fit the merge's ~1MB share;
  - when the Notebook opens signed in and online;
  - from **Sync now**.
- Owed ids with no entry left on the device are dropped.
- Changes to the owed set fire `ochorus:journal-pending`. A small reactive store, `journalSyncState`, turns that and `online`/`offline` into what the indicator shows.

**Also:** the date, the Print link and the sync line now share one aligned column in the header, which used to wrap unevenly on narrow pages.

## Checks
- `npm run check` has 0 errors and eslint is clean.
- vitest passes all 144 files (1253 tests) when run with a single worker. On this busy machine, parallel runs drop files to worker-start timeouts, and a cover or routing test failed that way before passing on its own; neither is related to this change. New `flushJournal` tests cover newest-first delivery, pruning, stopping at the first failure, and doing nothing when signed out.
- Tested in the browser signed out: the "Saved on this device only." line shows, per-entry marks stay hidden, and the header column aligns. The Sign in link isn't shown locally because auth isn't configured in the dev environment.
- **Not tested in the browser:** the signed-in states (offline, waiting, synced, per-entry marks). That needs a real account session; the unit tests cover the logic.

## For review
- Eleven new strings in nine locales. The **sw, lg, ar, hi and uk** translations are mine and need native review.

author: deblasis
body:
A new terminal on Windows now starts from the environment a fresh logon gives the user, read when the terminal opens: `CreateEnvironmentBlock` over the process token with bInherit FALSE, the same thing a Windows Terminal tab gets with `reloadEnvironmentVariables`. Before, a terminal copied the environment Wintty was launched with. That block is frozen at launch and survives an update restart, so variables and PATH entries installed later were missing, and variables set by the launcher leaked into every terminal.

On top of the fresh block Wintty sets only its own variables (TERM, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR and the rest termio already adds) and the `env` config entries, as before. Two things carry over from the app: the test harness variables (XDG_CONFIG_HOME and WINTTY_*) while WINTTY_TEST_CONFIG is set, and a NO_COLOR the app stripped to turn color on (it marks the strip with WINTTY_NO_COLOR_STRIPPED, so a NO_COLOR merely absent at launch is not treated as one).

The new `reload-env` key (default true) turns this off and gives every terminal Wintty's own environment again. It is documented in Config.zig, and the app reads it from the parsed config (ConfigService.ReloadEnvironment), so an included file or a CLI flag counts.

userenv.dll is loaded at run time from System32 only and resolved once, so a static consumer of libghostty does not have to add userenv.lib to its link.


Tests: `src/os/windows_logon_env.zig` covers the composition rule on canned blocks and reads a real logon block, asserting a variable only this process holds is absent (the test fails if the block is ever built with bInherit TRUE).

body:
## Summary

Adds the frontend setup flow for phishing simulations and completes the final UI/layout polish for the simulation configuration experience.

Administrators can now create or resume a phishing simulation Draft from a Campaign, configure its schedule, sending weekdays/times, permitted providers, and simulation pool context, save changes, and launch the simulation when the Campaign lifecycle allows it.

The setup page also transitions to a read-only configuration view once the simulation is no longer editable.

This PR additionally includes a small shared AppLayout fix to prevent horizontal overflow when the browser has a vertical scrollbar.

## Linked Issue

Closes #598 

## Type of change

- [x] Feature
- [x] Bug Fix
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/Maintenance

## Testing

Verified:

- Frontend typecheck passes
- Focused ESLint passes
- Prettier/format check passes
- `git diff --check` passes
- Focused frontend test suite passes
- 8 test files / 184 tests passed
- Manual browser testing completed for the simulation setup flow

Manual verification included:

- Creating/resuming a simulation Draft
- Saving schedule configuration
- Saving sending weekdays and daily send times
- Provider selection
- Disabled selected-provider handling
- Simulation pool context display
- Dirty-state handling
- Launch confirmation and lifecycle gating
- Read-only state after launch
- Route transition/loading behavior
- Narrow and desktop layouts
- No horizontal document overflow
- Only the intended AppLayout content area scrolls vertically

## Review Notes

### Simulation lifecycle

The frontend follows the existing backend lifecycle rules:

- Campaign `DRAFT`
  - simulation Draft can be created/resumed
  - configuration can be edited and saved
  - Launch is unavailable

- Campaign `ACTIVE`
  - simulation Draft can be created/resumed
  - configuration can be edited and saved
  - Launch is available

- Campaign `PAUSED`, `COMPLETED`, or `ARCHIVED`
  - configuration is read-only
  - no new editable simulation setup is created
  - Launch is unavailable

Only simulations with status `DRAFT` are editable.

### Draft resolution

The singular simulation setup route resolves the newest existing simulation Draft for the Campaign. If none exists, a new Draft is created.

The canonical simulation route is then used for editing and for the post-launch read-only configuration view.

### Provider handling

Active providers are selectable.

If a previously selected provider has since become disabled, it remains visible and checked but cannot be selected again. Unselected disabled providers are not shown.

### UI polish

The final layout pass:

- keeps Start/End together under Schedule;
- groups Send from/Send until with Sending weekdays;
- fixes fieldset heading/border overlap;
- preserves accessible fieldset labelling;
- aligns the Launch card with the rest of the setup UI;
- adds bottom spacing to the setup form;
- removes the duplicate document scrollbar.

### Shared AppLayout fix

The AppLayout outer shell previously used:

`width: 100vw`

which caused horizontal overflow equal to the browser scrollbar width on vertically scrolling pages.

It now uses:

`width: 100%`

so the shell sizes against the available document width instead.

## Checklist

- [x] I tested the change locally
- [x] Accessibility impact was considered if applicable
- [x] No unrelated changes are included
- [x] Relevant tests were added or updated if applicable
- [ ] Documentation was updated if needed
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or sensitive values were committed

author: joshi-chinmay-016
body:
## Overview

This PR improves Curio's adaptive learning behavior by making Teacher Mode persistent and multi-turn, while also fixing custom topic leakage caused by hardcoded fallback logic.

The core principle is:

> Words can trigger entry into Teacher Mode, but only demonstrated understanding can end Teacher Mode.

## Adaptive Teacher Mode

### Teacher Mode Entry

Teacher Mode can now be triggered by genuine learner struggle or explicit help requests such as:

- "I don't know"
- "I'm stuck"
- "I don't understand"
- "Can you teach me?"
- "Explain this"
- "I'm confused"

Semantic equivalents are also handled.

### Multi-Turn Teacher Mode

Teacher Mode now persists across multiple interactions.

The learner can:

- Ask for another explanation
- Ask questions about the learning gap
- Give partial verification answers
- Give incorrect answers
- Express continued confusion

These interactions keep the learner in Teacher Mode until the specific gap is actually resolved.

### Verification

Teacher Mode no longer treats simple acknowledgments as proof of understanding.

Messages such as:

- "Okay"
- "Yes"
- "I understand"
- "Teach me again"

do not automatically complete Teacher Mode.

The learner must demonstrate understanding of the exact gap through a substantive verification response.

### Interrupted Question Restoration

When Teacher Mode starts:

1. The current Student question is snapshotted.
2. The snapshot is preserved across Teacher turns.
3. Teacher verification questions do not overwrite the original question.
4. After successful verification, the original Student question is restored.
5. Teacher intervention state is cleared appropriately.

Max-attempt fallback is also handled using the existing Teacher attempt mechanism.

## Custom Topic Resolution

Fixed custom topic leakage where arbitrary topics could incorrectly produce questions about:

- Binary Search
- FastAPI

Changes include:

- Removed hardcoded Binary Search topic fallback from session state handling.
- Fixed local repository topic heuristics.
- Improved dynamic topic extraction in the mock provider.
- Added coverage for Operating Systems, DBMS, Machine Learning, and arbitrary topics.

## Backend Integration

The existing architecture and AI/backend boundary are preserved:

```text
AIContext
    ↓
CurioEngine.process()
    ↓
AIResult

author: danilofuchs
body:
### Description

Chrome 154 ships [responsive iframes](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/responsive-iframes): an `<iframe>` can size itself to its content when the host sets `frame-sizing: content-height` and the framed document opts in with a `responsive-embedded-sizing` meta tag. This PR adds Metabase's side of that, so hosts can auto-size embeds with CSS alone.

Today auto-height needs iframe-resizer, a non-standard library whose licensing has changed over time. The framed Metabase code also only speaks the iframe-resizer v4 protocol, so hosts that switched to a different parent-side library can't auto-size Metabase embeds.

**Changes**

- `index_template.html` includes `<meta name="responsive-embedded-sizing" content="allow-origins=*">`. It has to be in the server-rendered HTML, because Chrome ignores the tag when it's added dynamically.
- `initializeIframeResizer` is renamed to `initializeFrameSizing`. When the embed URL has `#frame_sizing=content-height` **and** the browser exposes `window.requestResize`, it:
  - drops `EmbedFrame`'s fixed-height scroll container (the same `onReady` path iframe-resizer already uses), so the document can grow;
  - calls `window.requestResize()` from a `ResizeObserver`, because the browser only measures the frame on load.
- iframe-resizer support is unchanged.
- Docs: `static-embedding.md` covers native sizing with an `@supports` fallback, and `static-embedding-parameters.md` lists the new `frame_sizing` hash parameter.

**Why a hash opt-in:** embeds scroll inside a container pinned to the iframe's size, so without the opt-in the document never grows past the frame and there's nothing for the browser to measure. The framed page can't see the host's CSS across origins, so the host has to say it's sizing the iframe. Turning this on automatically whenever `requestResize` exists would change the layout of every existing fixed-height embed on Chrome 154.

**Open questions for reviewers**

- `allow-origins=*` lets any page embedding Metabase read its content height. Content height can leak information across sites (for example, whether an interactive-embedding visitor can see a question). iframe-resizer already sends height to any parent page that asks, and `frame-ancestors` still controls who can frame the app, so this matches current exposure. A stricter option is to render `allow-origins` from the embedding-origins setting. Happy to do that here or in a follow-up.
- I haven't verified how native sizing interacts with iframe-resizer when a host uses both, so the docs present them as alternatives.

### How to verify

Needs Chrome 154 or later. **Not yet tested in a real browser**, which is the main reason this is a draft.

1. Enable static embedding and embed a dashboard with more content than fits in 600px.
2. On a host page, render:
   ```html
   <style>iframe { width: 100%; height: auto; frame-sizing: content-height; }</style>
   <iframe src="{embed-url}#frame_sizing=content-height"></iframe>
   ```
3. The iframe should grow to the dashboard's full height with no inner scrollbar, and resize when tabs or filters change the content.
4. Without the hash parameter, or in a browser without support, the embed should behave exactly as before.

author: tonyisup
body:
Administrators can now schedule announcements that show as banners at the top of every page on the listener site, between a start and end time.

**Each announcement has**
- A message (up to 280 characters)
- A severity: info (blue) or warning (amber). Warnings are listed first.
- Start and end times, entered in the admin's local time zone
- An optional link and label ("Learn more" if no label is given). Links to other sites open in a new tab.
- A dismissible flag. Listeners' dismissals are stored in their browser and reset when the announcement is edited.

**Admin (System → Announcements):** lists announcements as Live / Scheduled / Ended. The editor has a live preview, duration presets and a character count. You can also end an announcement immediately (it's kept for reuse) or delete it.

**Backend:** a new `announcements` table, with audited admin endpoints, at most 20 live or scheduled announcements, and a public `announcements.public.listLive` query. The table is classified as portable backup data.

**Things to know**
- Convex queries shouldn't read the clock, so the site sends `now` rounded to the minute. As a result, anyone calling the API directly can read a scheduled message before it starts. Don't put anything confidential in one.
- New banners can take up to a minute to appear. "End now" removes them right away.
- Deploy the backend before the web app. If the site ships first, an error boundary keeps the banner area empty instead of breaking the page.
- `convex/_generated/api.d.ts` was edited by hand because codegen needs a deployment. `convex dev` should produce the same result.

author: msdataei
body:
A load unit cannot always splat a single element: when its smallest access granularity is wider than the source, the hardware loads the whole granule and splats that, so one element per sub-SIMD group ends up live rather than one for the whole vector.  Give the IR the two things a consumer needs to finish that.

ktdf.read_from_fifo gains an optional `splat` attribute, #ktdf.splat<...>, whose one mode -- first_subsimd_lane_to_all_subsimd_lanes -- names the shuffle that closes the gap.  It names the shuffle rather than asserting that something is owed, so a reader learns what to build and not only that it must build.  It is inherent, not discardable, because it changes what the op means: a read carrying it hands out a value the shuffle has not been applied to yet.  The attribute survives onto a memref-typed re-read of the same slot, since reading a buffer performs no shuffle.

The mode carries no width.  A sub-SIMD group is as wide as the compute unit says, so feature::SIMD gains getSubSimdLanes, mirroring getLanes, over the sub_simd_lanes map device files already declare and nothing read.  Stating the width in a device pattern instead would make two places have to agree about one arch fact.

A trailing-optional attribute has no default in the generated builder, so read_from_fifo also gains the two-argument builder every existing caller uses: a read that owes no shuffle should not have to spell an absent mode.

author: fernandovrgas
body:
## O que muda

Adiciona `ORBIEN_API_URL` e `ORBIEN_WEB_URL` ao `env:` do passo "Publicar
update OTA (Android + iOS, branch preview)" em `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
com os mesmos valores que os profiles `preview`/`preview-ios-simulator` já
usam em `apps/mobile/eas.json`.

## Por que

`eas update` reavalia `apps/mobile/app.config.js` com o ambiente do próprio
job do GitHub Actions — não herda o `env` de nenhum profile de `eas build`
em `eas.json` (isso só vale pra `eas build`). O passo que publica OTA no
branch/channel `preview` só tinha `EXPO_TOKEN` no `env:`, então
`process.env.ORBIEN_API_URL` chegava vazio em `app.config.js:67` e
`extra.apiUrl` caía no default (`http://localhost:3000`, `app.config.js:53`).

Esse job dispara em todo push a `main` que muda JS em `apps/mobile` sem
tocar nada nativo (`app.config.js`, `eas.json`, `package.json`, `assets`) —
não precisa ter relação com login. Qualquer PR de mobile assim mesclado
publicava um update que sobrescrevia `Constants.expoConfig.extra.apiUrl`
pra `localhost:3000` em todo app instalado no channel `preview`.

Foi a causa raiz de um usuário não conseguir logar no app mobile enquanto o
web funcionava: diagnosticamos com um log temporário em
`AuthService.login` (PR #118) e confirmamos que **nenhuma tentativa de
login do app batia no Render** — a requisição nunca saía do device, porque
estava indo pra `localhost` em vez da API de produção.

## Como validar

1. Merge (dispara `mobile-eas-build` no próximo push a `main` que toque
   `apps/mobile`, ou pode ser disparado manualmente publicando um update OTA
   no branch `preview` com o `env` corrigido).
2. No [expo.dev](https://expo.dev/accounts/fernandovargas/projects/orbien/updates),
   conferir que o manifest do update mais recente do branch `preview` traz
   `extra.apiUrl = "https://orbien-api.onrender.com/api"`.
3. Pedir pro usuário abrir o app (channel `preview`) de novo — o
   `expo-updates` baixa o update na próxima abertura — e tentar logar.

## Revisão

Não rodei `/code-review` nem a skill `pr-review` — mudança de 11 linhas só
em `env:` de um workflow, sem lógica nova pra revisar.

## Riscos e pendências

- Não mexe em `render.yaml`, `vercel.json`, `prisma/migrations/` nem em
  nenhuma variável de ambiente configurada manualmente em painel — só
  duplica, no `env:` do passo, valores que já existem em `eas.json`.
- Pendência: os apps já instalados no channel `preview` só pegam a correção
  quando o `expo-updates` baixar o próximo update publicado com este fix —
  não é retroativo ao update quebrado que já foi publicado. Vale confirmar
  no expo.dev se algum update precisa ser republicado manualmente pra forçar
  isso antes do próximo push de mobile.
- Pendência separada (PR #118): reverter o log temporário de diagnóstico em
  `AuthService.login`/`LoginRateLimitService` assim que confirmarmos que o
  login volta a funcionar.

author: nchafy
body:
Closes the last open item in Phase 1 (`docs/phase-1-scope.md` §6 criterion 5), except for
one thing that cannot be automated and is recorded as outstanding rather than ticked.

## What is now gated in CI

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| axe, WCAG 2.2 AA, **all 114** pre-rendered pages | 0 violations |
| Keyboard + accessibility tree, 9 page types | 122 checks, 0 failures |
| Console / CSP, any page | 0 complaints |
| Page weight ≤ 60 KB gzipped | 13.7 KB heaviest |
| All JavaScript ≤ 12 KB gzipped | 6.5 KB |
| Geometry ≤ 300 KB, after first paint | 132 KB |
| Cold load to interactive ≤ 3 s, p95 of 20 runs | 906 ms |

No new dependency, runtime or dev. The browser work goes through a ~160-line stdlib
DevTools-protocol client (`scripts/cdp.py`) rather than Playwright, which would have added
a package that downloads and executes its own browser binaries to a build that pulls
nothing and holds no secrets. axe-core is vendored, checksum-pinned, dev-only.

## The bug

`connect-src` named the geocoder and omitted `'self'`, so under the real policy every
same-origin fetch was refused: `/data/lookup.json`, `/data/districts.geo.json`,
`/manifest.json`.

Local resolution of a ZIP, neighbourhood or district number **is** the privacy feature —
§4.4 promises those never reach the geocoder. With the index unfetchable, every query fell
through to the geocoder, so a policy written to protect the reader's address was causing
more of their input to be sent. Separately the staleness notice, which is what stops an
abandoned site claiming to be fresh, silently never rendered.

The outline's R38 already specified `(self, geosearch.planninglabs.nyc)`. The
implementation diverged by one token and nothing compared the two.

Why nothing caught it: `tests/browser/test_address_box.py` serves from a bare file server
with no CSP, and `scripts/verify.py` fetches the manifest over plain HTTP. Both test the
feature; neither tests it under the policy shipped with it. It surfaced the first time
anything drove the site in a browser behind the real `_headers`.

Now covered from both ends — `tests/unit/test_csp.py` (static, hermetic) and
`scripts/console_check.py` (runtime, real browser, no allowlist) — plus a network-level
test that resolving `35` must fetch the local index, must **not** contact the geocoder, and
must not pull the 132 KB geometry.

## Still open, deliberately

- **A real screen-reader pass.** Reading the accessibility tree is not listening to a
  screen reader. `docs/accessibility-pass.md` §3.2 is the procedure, §4 the record, and it
  says NOT RUN. This is the remaining Phase 1 item.
- `/favicon.ico` 404s. Shipping a mark is an identity decision (§7.3) that is still yours,
  so the console gate names it as an expected browser probe rather than answering it.
- DevTools' Slow 3G preset gives 4.3–5.1 s. Reported, not gated; the reasoning is in
  `perf-budget.json` rather than being a quiet omission.

## Also fixed
§4.5 requires GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs; every action was on a tag. Now pinned
to verified SHAs with the release in a trailing comment.

## Worth a look during review
- `perf-budget.json` — every threshold carries a note saying where its number came from.
- `tests/fixtures/a11y_broken/` — the negative control, because the site passed axe on the
  first run it was ever given and "clean" is indistinguishable from "nothing ran".

body:
Stage 10, third of its PRs: the table system. Two commits.

## What changes

- **Sticky headers where a table fits, a scroll edge where it does not** (`111a1fa`). `fitTables()` measures each table against its box. A table that fits gets `overflow:clip`, which rounds the corners without making a scroll container, so its header row sticks to the top of the window. A table that does not fit keeps scrolling sideways, and the box now draws a soft edge on the side with more columns. That edge is the fix for "the ratings table clips mid-column" on phones. The scrolling state is the default, so without JavaScript a table loses its sticky header, never a column.
- **Headers look like controls only where they sort.** The pointer and hover colour moved from every header to `th[aria-sort]`. The Power Ratings sort headers now take keyboard focus, sort on Enter and Space, and report `aria-sort`; before this, the one sortable table could not be sorted from a keyboard.
- **Borders are `separate`, not collapsed**, because a collapsed border stays behind when a sticky cell moves. The stuck header sits above the Net Rating zero line, which poked through it in the first render.
- **Prose no longer sits in right-aligned number cells.** Model Lab's result column and many of Methodology's table cells, the glossary's definitions among them, wore `td.num` and were set flush right.
- **CLAUDE.md** (`83fd569`) records how the system works and why a sticky header and a sideways scroll cannot both hold on one table.

## Evidence

- `tests/test_table_system.py` checks each premise over the real template and over synthetic input.
- `tests/mutation/cases/table_system.json`, eight cases. Full corpus, `python tests/mutation/runner.py`: 287 cases, all CAUGHT, at `83fd569`.

author: marius-kilocode
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The marketplace can list MCP servers and skills, but an MCP entry cannot reference a skill that explains how to use it. Publishers have no way to ship a remote MCP server together with its companion skill.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Kilo client now installs companion skills when an MCP entry declares them. This adds the authoring and generation side: an MCP entry can list companion skill IDs, and the generator validates them and expands each one into the archive descriptor the client consumes.

Authors add a top-level list to `mcps/<server-id>/MCP.yaml`:

```yaml
skills:
  - example-workflow
```

Generation:

- Rejects malformed lists, duplicates, unsafe or missing IDs, and missing or invalid `SKILL.md` files (name must match the ID, description must be non-empty).
- Validates the MCP ID only when `skills` is present, so existing entries without companions are unchanged.
- Reuses the existing stable skill archive URL construction.
- Preserves `requirements.skills`, which is a separate historical field and does not install skills.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the full remote MCP plus skill example, resource packaging, and the publication order (client release before any client that pins the CLI is updated).

## User Impact

Publishers can ship an MCP server with companion skills in one marketplace entry. Entries without `skills` generate byte-for-byte identical output.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test`: 119 passed, including 32 new generator tests.
- `pnpm run typecheck:mcps` and `pnpm run typecheck:plugins`: passed.
- Real MCP and skill catalog generation: passed; both generated catalogs are byte-for-byte unchanged for existing entries.
- CI workflow now also runs the MCP typecheck.

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Parallel advisor and client tools can fail with HTTP 400
- The client never receives its pending tool calls

How it solves it:

author: chrisrackauckas-claude
body:
> Please ignore until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.

## What changed and why

When every subalgorithm fails, `solve!(::NonlinearSolvePolyAlgorithmCache)` falls back to the subcache with the smallest residual (`findmin_resids`). That comparison included subcaches that were **not attempted in this call**. With retention armed (as the homotopy drivers do on their tracking `reinit!`s), a skipped subcache still holds the residual of an earlier problem, and its `retcode` is still `Default`. So a failed attempt could return that stale subcache's `u` and `ReturnCode.Default`.

Reproducer (NonlinearSolve only). `HomotopySweep` on an S-curve stalls at the first fold, which is expected for natural-parameter continuation, but reports `ReturnCode.Default`:

```julia
using NonlinearSolve
H(u, p, λ) = [u[1]^3 - 3u[1] - (-3 + 6λ)]
sol = solve(HomotopyProblem(H, [-2.1038034027355366]), HomotopySweep(; store_original = Val(true)))
sol.retcode           # ReturnCode.Default (master)
sol.original.u        # [-2.1038034027355366] (the λ = 0 start, i.e. a stale subcache)
```

Instrumenting `findmin_resids` shows the two cheap rungs frozen at the anchor's residual (`u0` is an exact λ = 0 root) on every rejected tracking step:

```
findmin_resids: fus norms = (1.78e-15, 1.78e-15, 2.38e-8, 1.06e-7, 2.38e-8, 2.40e-8) -> idx 1
sweep retcode=Default u=[-1.00016677516083] original.retcode=Default original.u=[-2.1038034027355366]
```

The fix records which subcaches were attempted in the current `solve!` call (in the in-order pass or the retention wrap-around) and gives the fallback only those residuals.

This was found by SciMLBenchmarks `NonlinearProblem/homotopy_continuation`, where `HomotopySweep (default inner)` shows return code `Default` on the S-curve problem.

## Verification

New test `test/Core/homotopy_sweep_tests__item24.jl`, Julia 1.12.7, dev'd `NonlinearSolve` + `NonlinearSolveBase`.

Without the fix:
```
Evaluated: SciMLBase.ReturnCode.Default != SciMLBase.ReturnCode.Default
Evaluated: SciMLBase.ReturnCode.Default != SciMLBase.ReturnCode.Default
Evaluated: [-2.1038034027355366] != [-2.1038034027355366]
sweep stalled at a fold reports the failing corrector, not a stale subcache |    2     3      5
```
With the fix:
```
sweep stalled at a fold reports the failing corrector, not a stale subcache |    5      5
```

I ran every `Core` test file whose name matches homotopy/polyalgorithm (44 `@safetestset`s from `test/runtests.jl`, including the retention, wrap-around, StalledSuccess and HomotopyPolyAlgorithm tests) in a scratch env with the fix: **551 passed**. The one error is `bounds_tests__item4.jl`, which does `using LinearSolve`; my scratch env did not have LinearSolve, so this is not a test failure. Runic `--check` and `typos` are clean on the changed files.

## Not verified

- I did not run the full `Core` group, QA, or the other sublibraries' tests.
- No version bump in `lib/NonlinearSolveBase/Project.toml`.

body: Puts a walkthrough of a real Spotlights report above the fold in the README, between the "point it at a repo and a goal" paragraph and the positioning paragraph — so a reader sees what a ranked, browsable map actually looks like before being asked to take the claim on trust. ## What this changes Two files: | file | | |---|---| | `README.md` | +6 lines — a centered `` and a one-line caption | | `docs/demo.gif` | 9,656,272 bytes, 940×529, 49.6s, loops | Nothing else. No source, no config, no dependency. ## The demo A real run over 8 modules of vLLM (the `examples/vllm_subset` run, whose `result.json` is already in the repo). It walks: the run's output tiles → the 173 ranked candidates → one candidate opened to its write-up and its 11 proposals → the whole run as a radial tree → the findings catalogue, narrowed to papers and then to one module, ending on the paper whose first proposal is the rank-#17 candidate the demo opened earlier. That last beat is the point of the whole thing: it closes the loop from published paper → extracted technique → proposal → ranked candidate in a single frame, rather than asserting the connection in prose. ## How it was made Scripted with Playwright against the real `experiment.html` — not hand-recorded. Every figure in every caption (173, 97, 46, #17, 6 proposals, the module paths) is asserted against the live DOM at record time, so a report change makes the recording *fail* rather than silently ship a demo of a product that no longer exists. The recorder itself is deliberately **not** in this PR. It is a maintainer's tool, and the deliverable is the GIF. It stays on disk locally and can be committed later if it earns its place. ## Sizing 940px / 10fps / 22 colours, chosen by reading real extracted frames rather than by guessing — the catalogue's 8px monospace URLs are the binding constraint on width, and the amber accent is the binding constraint on palette depth. 9.66MB, inside the 10MB budget. ## Review notes - The caption says "8 modules of vLLM", not "vLLM" — the run scoped the repo to 8 modules and the README shouldn't imply otherwise. - `width="940"` is the GIF's native width, so GitHub renders it unscaled. - The `alt` text describes the four stages of the walkthrough. - The branch history contains 20 commits that add and then remove the recorder. **Squash-merging** collapses that to the two-file change this PR actually makes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: strum355
body: ## Summary Implements `check` mode for the action ([TC-5616](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/TC-5616)). Check mode runs DA analysis + license checks on every discovered manifest, writes a detailed report to the workflow **Job Summary**, and sets structured outputs that downstream steps can use for policy gates. Findings never fail the build — a non-zero exit means the action itself failed; enforcement is left to the caller. ## What it does For each discovered manifest, it runs stack analysis against the DA backend, then aggregates: - **Vulnerabilities** by provider/source and severity (critical/high/medium/low), summed across manifests and sources - **Available remediations** (dependencies with a known fix) - **License analysis** — category breakdown and conflicts against the project's own license (best-effort; skipped without failing if license data is unavailable) ### User-visible output - **Job Summary** (`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`): a markdown report with Dependencies Scanned, Vulnerabilities, Available Remediations, and (when data exists) License Analysis sections. - **Structured outputs** for downstream gates: `critical-count`, `high-count`, `medium-count`, `low-count`, `remediation-count`, `license-conflicts`. All are always set (default `0`) so gate expressions never see an empty value. ```yaml - id: da uses: trustification/trustify-da-action@ with: mode: check backend-url: https://exhort.stage.devshift.net - if: steps.da.outputs.critical-count > 0 run: exit 1 ```

author: hiroki23
body:
An inferred empty Hash previously joined `Integer` and `Float` values only when they were written through branches of the same `if` or `case`. A branch writing `2` and another writing `nil` or a String was rejected, although the pinned TypeRB implementation resolves these as nullable or union values.

This change uses the existing checked type join for inferred Hash values and finalizes their representation in MIR. The Hash finalizer inserts Float conversion, nullable wrapping, or union injection at the store after the final value type is known, then remaps block instruction spans. Exact-type stores do not allocate a speculative union value. Explicit Hash annotations, different key types, and assignments in separate statements remain strict.

The shared-language registry adds positive branch-join and negative separate-write cases; both match the pinned Go reference across check, build, execution, and REPL. A managed conformance fixture and forced-GC MIR tests cover scalar and Array-valued unions, three-way case joins, and value lifetime. The source scan checks all 390 reviewed conformance files with zero mismatches. Snapshot-v4, ordinary fixed-point build, focused compiler tests, formatting, coverage/doc checks, and recovery source-closure checks pass. Full local recovery-enabled root and compiler suites pass on the exact source: 111/0 and 567/0 respectively.

This is a partial implementation of #551. Nested untyped empty Array values remain unsupported, so the issue stays open.

author: ehn
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The station pressure sensor measures air pressure (the docs describe it as "the atmospheric pressure at the station level"), but uses the generic `pressure` device class. This PR switches it to `atmospheric_pressure`, which is what `weatherflow_cloud` already uses for its pressure sensors.

With the generic class, core's US customary conversion would turn mbar into psi, so the integration sets `imperial_suggested_unit=inHg` itself. With `atmospheric_pressure`, core converts to inHg on its own, so that override is removed. The same override on the rain per minute sensor is also removed: its `precipitation` device class is already converted to inches by core.

Letting core do the conversion also means the display precision is scaled with the unit. Today the suggested precision is applied to inHg as is, because inHg is the integration's suggested unit. I plan to follow up with a separate PR that sets sensible display precisions (station pressure currently suggests 5 decimals), and this change lets that PR use a single value that works in both mbar and inHg.

Effect on users:

- Existing entities keep the unit stored in the entity registry (mbar for metric users, inHg / in for US customary users, or whatever the user chose).
- New metric installs show station pressure in hPa instead of mbar (numerically identical).
- New US customary installs are unchanged: inHg and in.
- The `device_class` state attribute of the station pressure sensor changes from `pressure` to `atmospheric_pressure` for all users. This only matters to automations or templates that test that attribute.

This also adds the first sensor tests for the integration: a snapshot of all sensor entities, and a check of the units per unit system. The tests replace only the UDP socket and feed it a Tempest's packets, so they go through the library's listener and the integration unchanged.

Question for the code owners: I left vapor pressure on the generic `pressure` device class with its inHg override, since it is a partial pressure rather than the air pressure itself (`sensorpush_cloud` makes the same distinction). Would you prefer `atmospheric_pressure` for it as well?

author: dontblamemedev
body:
A server now seats both wire versions (`reference_server`#58), so a client that mints a room has to choose one. §2's `wire_versions` is the list it chooses from, and this states the rule where that list is read.

- **An unpinned client that can speak `selvage/2` MUST mint `selvage/2`.** A reachable `wire_versions` that holds no version at major 2 it can speak is a **refusal** — local, before a socket is opened, and never a fall back to `selvage/1` — because a room the server can read is the one failure the version gate exists to prevent (the revision's threat model is a server that may be compromised; a list that merely omits `selvage/2` must not be able to talk a client into a plaintext room). The refusal is the client's to word, naming the server and the version it would need.
- **A `/meta` that could not be read is not that answer.** §2 already says an unreachable `/meta` is not a reason to refuse to connect, so the client attempts `selvage/2` and the handshake decides; a server seating only `selvage/1` answers `unsupported_version`, which is loud and not a downgrade.
- **`selvage/1` is what a client mints when it cannot speak `selvage/2`, or when it is pinned there** (a setting, a link, a deployment) — a deliberate choice to host a room the server can read, which is what the pin is for. A pin to a version the server does not seat stays a refusal (§10).
- **A join is not this choice** and is unchanged: it speaks the version its invite names (§5.1, the fragment's two keys or their absence), whatever the list says.

§10's no-downgrade bullet is narrowed from “does not name `selvage/2`” to “names no version at major 2 it can speak”, so a server listing only `selvage/2.1` stays reachable as §10's same-major rule allows. Three informative clauses saying no implementation speaks `selvage/2` yet are dropped, because one does.

**Evidence.** `scripts/ci-local.sh all` — seven steps, all passed (`schemas`, `runner`, `yprotocols`, `peer`, `peer-census`, `recipes`, `workflows`), exit 0. `schema/validate.py`: `result OK`, with `vectors 36 files`, `peer vectors 25 files`, `sealed 48`, `refusals 13`, `session v2 42` — every number identical to before, and `selvage/1` intact (its removal and the corpus re-baseline are the release wave's, gated on the published clients).

The three clients are being changed to do exactly this in the same wave; the VS Code one owns the shared engine helper the other two vendor.

Gates: `specification/scripts/ci-local.sh all`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified that the `selvage/2` protocol descriptions are based on the design, not observed network behavior.
  * Documented version selection for minting: clients use `selvage/1` when they cannot speak `selvage/2` or are pinned to version 1. Clients selecting version 2 do not fall back if `/meta` is readable but offers no compatible version; if `/meta` is unreadable, they attempt version 2 and rely on the handshake.
  * Clarified that joins use the invite’s version, and unsupported version pins are refused without fallback.

author: jcnm
body:
## Ce que corrige ce lot

Recette iOS du 2026-09-23 (staging, `dev` `24ff919659`) : une vue unique **non ouverte** laissait lire son contenu.

1. **Focal** : la légende d'une photo à vue unique (`SECRET-VU-PHOTO`) se lisait en clair sous le voile.
2. **Lecteur d'écran, trois modes** : le libellé d'une vue unique texte jamais ouverte contenait son texte (`Demo, SECRET-VU-DIRECT texte, 16:48, Vue unique`).
3. **Téléchargement** : l'ouverture de la conversation récupérait le fichier d'un sticker à vue unique avant tout geste.

## La cause, et pourquoi le correctif ferme la classe

Le voile était posé PAR-DESSUS un contenu monté. Il protégeait le pixel, pas le reste : le texte restait dans l'arbre d'accessibilité, la légende d'une photo dont seule la PIÈCE portait la vue unique n'était pas voilée du tout, et le préchargement du fil ne regardait pas la protection.

Le correctif retire le contenu du rendu au lieu de le voiler :

- `MeeshyMessage.isViewOnceSealed` / `sealedForDisplay` (SDK) : tant que le lecteur n'a pas ouvert le message, texte, pièces, sticker, lieu et citation sortent du modèle. Une pièce à vue unique scelle aussi la légende du message.
- `BubbleContent` naît de ce message scellé : nouveau `Kind.viewOnceSealed`, sans texte, sans pièce, sans traduction. Bulles, Focal et Script rendent la seule puce **`(1) · Touchez pour afficher`** (`ViewOnceChip`, MeeshyUI) ; le chrome ne répète pas la vue unique (#7619).
- Le libellé accessible dit « Message à vue unique, touchez pour afficher », l'heure et l'éphémère éventuel, jamais le contenu (Focal/Script : `MessageAccessibilityLabelComposer` ; Bulles : la puce ; Rivière : sa bulle).
- La Rivière projette un texte vide et monte la même puce ; l'action « Copier » n'y existe plus pour un message scellé.
- Le préchargement du fil (`ConversationMediaHandler.prefetchCandidates`) saute les vues uniques, et le plein écran ne les fait plus défiler depuis une autre photo.
- L'ouverture est une donnée de la visite, tenue par le ViewModel (`openViewOnce`, `revealedViewOnceIds`) et posée sur la cellule, qui lit GRDB : un média s'ouvre en plein écran (consommé à la fermeture, #7499) ; un texte se révèle à sa place (consommé à la sortie, #7500). La Rivière consommait au toucher : elle passe par le même canal.

## Témoins (rouges avant, verts après)

- SDK `ViewOnceSealTests` : le sceau, la pièce à vue unique, la projection vidée, le média ouvrable, le chrome sans doublon.
- App `ViewOnceSealedRenderingTests` : un témoin par mode — le modèle commun Bulles/Focal/Script (texte, légende, pièce), le libellé accessible Focal/Script, la Rivière (texte et clé de mémo), le préchargement, le plein écran, et l'ouverture par le ViewModel.

## Ce que la recette doit regarder à l'écran

Sur un simulateur connecté à staging, A envoie à B une vue unique texte, une photo à vue unique AVEC légende, et un sticker à vue unique ; B ne touche rien.

- En **Bulles, Focal, Script, Rivière** : chaque message n'affiche qu'une puce `(1) · Touchez pour afficher`, sans texte, sans légende, sans vignette, sans puce « 1 » séparée au-dessus.
- VoiceOver sur chacun : « Message à vue unique, touchez pour afficher », jamais le texte ni la légende.
- Journal réseau à l'ouverture de la conversation : aucun `GET /attachments/file/…` pour le sticker ni la photo.
- Toucher la puce du texte : le texte s'affiche à sa place. Toucher la puce de la photo : plein écran ; à la fermeture, la vue unique est consommée.

La suite (état « déjà ouvert » par personne, purge locale, appui long réduit, bascule du texte au retoucher et à la sortie d'écran, flou de la ligne) est le lot #7579 / #7619.

Closes #7618
Refs #7619

body:
<!-- Commits must be signed to merge — see CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-signing if you haven't set this up. -->

## What and why

`.clickable-link` hardcoded `#3f51b5` in `clients-list.component.ts` and `client-view.component.ts`, so it never picked up the dark theme and rendered at 2.43:1 against the `#1e1e1e` card — well under the 4.5:1 WCAG AA minimum for normal text. Both are swapped to `var(--primary-text)`.

That's the token `_common.scss` already documents for exactly this case — "a palette colour drawn as text on a page or card surface" — rather than the issue's suggested `var(--primary-color)`: `--primary-color` measures 3.15:1 on the light theme's white card (see the comment on it in `_common.scss`), so that swap would have traded the dark-mode failure for a new light-mode one. `--primary-text` keeps light mode's current ~8:1 (`#2471a3` on white) and brings dark mode to a measured 5.29:1 (`#3498db` on `#1e1e1e`), both comfortably clearing AA. It's the same token `header.component.ts` and `tabs.component.ts` already use for this exact pattern.

Closes #575

## Verification

- `npm run lint` — no new findings on the changed files (repo-wide exit reflects a pre-existing stale-suppressions condition already present on `main`, confirmed by diffing lint output against an unmodified checkout byte-for-byte).
- `npm run format:check` — pass.
- `npm run test:unit` — pass (247 files, 1518 tests).
- `npm run build` — pass (the one budget warning is pre-existing, on `header.component.ts`, unrelated to this change).
- `npm run typecheck:e2e` — pass.
- `npx playwright test --project=mocked e2e/accessibility.spec.ts` — pass, including a new regression test.
- `npx playwright test --project=mocked e2e/client.spec.ts` — pass (real client-creation flow through the changed components).

**New regression test** (`e2e/accessibility.spec.ts`, "client list links meet color contrast in dark mode"): populates one client row, switches to dark mode via the header toggle — the issue's own repro steps — and asserts axe-core's `color-contrast` check passes for `.clickable-link`. Confirmed both directions manually:

- Against the unfixed colour: fails with `Element has insufficient color contrast of 2.42 (foreground color: #3f51b5, background color: #1e1e1e...)`, matching the issue's own 2.43:1 measurement.
- Against this fix: passes.

**Manual verification** (mocked UI, dark mode, real browser via Playwright, not just the unit/e2e assertions): read `getComputedStyle` on both live `.clickable-link` elements after logging in, populating a client row, and toggling dark mode —

```
accountNo link: color=rgb(63, 81, 181) bg=rgb(30, 30, 30) contrast=2.43:1   (before)
accountNo link: color=rgb(52, 152, 219) bg=rgb(30, 30, 30) contrast=5.29:1  (after)
name link:      color=rgb(63, 81, 181) bg=rgb(30, 30, 30) contrast=2.43:1   (before)
name link:      color=rgb(52, 152, 219) bg=rgb(30, 30, 30) contrast=5.29:1  (after)
```

Full-page screenshots of both states were captured locally during verification (not attached here, to keep the PR diff limited to the actual code/test change) — happy to post them in a comment if a reviewer wants the visual alongside the measured values above.

**Not run:** the real-backend Playwright project and the CI license/RAT/security jobs — no dependency, license, or generated-file changes here, and this change touches no route the `backend` project's specs cover.

author: paulmking
body:
Cleaned up version of the MOLLERADC decoder changes from PR#302
This PR preserves the old_mock MOLLER ADC decoder and adds support for the
reshuffled hardware data format. The decoder is selected using 'decode_mode'
in the detector map.

Main changes include:

 *   Add enum-selected legacy and reshuffled decoding paths.
 *   Make channel count, word count, module-header size, buffer offset, and block
     count depend on the selected decoder.
 *   Preserve the old_mock 8-channel, 30-word, four-block layout.
 *   Support the reshuffled 16-channel, 14-word layout.
 *   Decode reshuffled sums, sample counts, sum-of-squares, minimum/maximum values,
     block indices, and RMS values.
 *   Generate mode-specific ROOT branches.
 *   Add detector maps for reshuffled hall and injector data.

This does not include the MOLLERADC header decoding from PR#302.
