author: itismyfield
body:
## 무엇
`promote_task_complete_fallback_text`(`src/services/codex_tui/rollout_tail.rs`)는 스트리밍 assistant 텍스트가 있을 때 `last_agent_message` 가 상위집합(supersedes)이 아니면 로그 없이 버렸다. 두 분기를 하나의 "항상 소비" 정책으로 합쳤다.

| 형상 | 동작 |
|---|---|
| `final_text` 비어있음 | append |
| 상위집합(스트리밍 tail 로 끝남) | replace (INFO, 기존 로그 유지) |
| 이미 반영됨(동일/메시지 경계 접미사) | drop — #3343 중복 제거 유지 |
| 그 외(서로소·부분겹침) | 경계 구분 append + **WARN** `agentdesk::codex_rollout_handoff` |

## (a)/(b) 판정 — 측정된 (b), 수리는 전달 쪽
로컬 Codex rollout 전수(읽기 전용) `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` **1927 파일 / task_complete 턴 4183** 을 파서와 같은 술어로 분류:
- already_mirrored **4096**, fallback_empty 87, supersedes **0**, commentary-only 0
- **서로소/부분겹침(기존 폐기 대상) 0건**

실제 Codex 는 스트리밍의 마지막 메시지를 `last_agent_message` 로 낸다 → E-25 의 서로소 형상은 현장에서 관측되지 않았다(b).
그래도 폐기 비용(메시지 유실, 무고지)이 append 비용(현장 0건인 형상에서의 문장 중복)보다 크므로 무음 폐기 대신 전달 + WARN 으로 관측 가능하게 했다. E-25 notes 에 이 근거를 적고, E-25 는 이 방어 경로를 고정하는 픽스처로 재정의했다.

## E-25 ↔ 프로덕션 정합

author: ohdearquant
body:
Adds Appendix A to ADR-105's 2026-09-14 amendment: version 1 of the node wire protocol that the node channel adapter and the hosted service's node ingress exchange.

## What the appendix fixes

- A.1-A.3: scope and versioning, the device key bundle (one Ed25519 signing key and one X25519 KEM key per key epoch), and the replay-identity rules (a key change starts a new epoch, a device's epochs only increase, a device identifier is never reassigned).
- A.4: request authentication (headers, signing input, the timestamp window, nonce memory and the floor that stops a replay across a loss of nonce memory; the operator states the clock bound B, which must be a true bound, and only the service computes the floor).
- A.5-A.6: contact key lookup, envelope submission with its replay identity and one lock per logical message, delivery polling, and recipient receipts. A pair's contact generation is never reused, and every revocation, block, unblock and re-acceptance moves it above all earlier ones. A sender's receipt `seq` only increases and is assigned above a per-agent high-water kept in directory state, so it is never reused after receipts expire.
- A.7-A.9: client outcomes, sender-side status, and how service answers map onto `khive-channel` results.
- A.10: limits. A.11: shared test vectors (HPKE, signatures, digests, and negative cases), which are part of the specification. A.12: what the appendix does not change.
- A conformance table covering each refusal and each concurrency case.

The hosted product contract stays where the amendment already points (line 218); the appendix cites it by the same name.

## Two mechanical notes

- The appendix sits between `deno-fmt-ignore-start` and `deno-fmt-ignore-end` markers. Its test vectors state the exact UTF-8 bytes that were signed and digested, and `deno fmt` would re-indent those JSON lines, so the stated bytes would no longer be the signed ones. Formatting is suspended for the appendix only; the rest of the file is formatted as before.
- `.gitleaks.toml` exempts one value on one path: the HPKE shared secret in the published test vector, an intermediate derived from test seeds the appendix also publishes. It is exempted by value and by path, like the existing entries: a different value on that line, or the same value in another file, is still refused (checked both ways).

## Verification

- `deno fmt --check` passes on the file, and the same check on the appendix without the markers fails.
- `scripts/lint-adr-refs.sh`: 445 files, 254 titled references OK; anchor lint OK with its must-fail fixtures.
- The staged diff passes the gitleaks pre-commit scan.

No code changes.

Scope: 2 files, 3 commits.

Refs: #1172, #1272, #1205

## What this does

This is the Launch-pack conformance lane for `@clossys/publisher`. It covers three things:

- #1172: `outputs`, `feeds` and `fit` in the `foundry` manifest block.
- #1272: a dedicated qualification case for every capability that a real command exercises. Every other capability drops to `planned` with `proofCase: null`.
- #1205, the part in scope: `clossys/publisher/surfaces` is added to the consumer layout contract as Publisher-owned.

## Base composition

Until they land, this branch merges in two approved PRs:

- #1258 at `feabf0415293b8a91865799758718d2221838fab` (capability maps)
- #1376 at `cb7f6d0cd72fb0f28a6302f44d30af25b7744800` (skills cite the strategist handoff)

Both were still open at the latest push. Once they merge, `git merge origin/main` shrinks this diff to this lane's own commits.

## #1172: declared fields and their evidence

| Field | Value | Derived from |
|---|---|---|
| `outputs` | `clossys/publisher/pack.json`, `clossys/publisher/surfaces/` | `pack.json`: `src/pack/index.ts:3` and `src/pack/validate.ts:145` name it as the manifest `validatePackManifest` checks. `surfaces/`: `src/surfaces/ownership.ts:26` (`PUBLISHER_SURFACES_DIR`), and the shipped site template reads it at build time (`templates/site/app/page.tsx:5` and the four sibling routes). |
| `feeds` | `{ artifact: "surface-documents", path: "clossys/publisher/surfaces/" }` | The `surface-documents` capability's own output. Customer's `keep-verdict` capability consumes it (`packages/customer/package.json:36-37`). |
| `fit` | `fit-signals.json`, new and added to `files` | Two signals. `audience-facing-surface` (`repository-structure`) is the example `docs/contracts/package-framework.json` itself gives for Publisher. `release-must-be-proved` (`consumer-answer`) is the role's job question in `docs/contracts/role-loop-archetypes.json`. |

**`outputs` is deliberately narrower than the capability map.** It lists only the paths that shipped code fixes. Seven capability-map output paths are not in `outputs`, and the reason differs by path:

- `record.json` and `asset-roster.json`: `publisher-record-check` and `publisher-media-check` take caller-supplied paths. No source fixes those two locations.
- `routes.json`: the shipped site template's route manifest is `templates/site/web-route-manifest.json`. It lands in the consumer's app directory, not under `clossys/publisher/`. This mismatch predates this PR and is filed as a follow-up.
- `templates.json`, `materials/index.json`, `channel-kits.json`, `site.json` and both `.generated/` reports: nothing reads or writes them yet.

### Prepared, pending catalogue fix

`needs` and `solves` are NOT declared in this PR. `scripts/lib/capability-catalogue.mjs` and `packages/advisor` read both fields in a different shape from the one `docs/contracts/package-framework.json` requires (see #1398's "Blocker" section). With either field declared, `npm run test --workspace=packages/advisor` fails. A separate infra PR will align the catalogue. These are the prepared values:

```json
"needs": [
  { "producerRole": "@clossys/strategist", "artifact": "strategy-brief" },
  { "producerRole": "@clossys/designer", "artifact": "components-and-blocks" },
  { "producerRole": "@clossys/designer", "artifact": "token-contract-and-brand-overlay-binding" },
  { "producerRole": "@clossys/designer", "artifact": "logo-and-identity-files" },
  { "producerRole": "@clossys/writer", "artifact": "copy-registry" },
  { "producerRole": "@clossys/customer", "artifact": "keep-verdict" }
],
"solves": [
  {
    "problem": "publisher-verified-release",
    "statement": "We're not sure what's actually live, or that it matches what we approved.",
    "metric": "verified publication rate",
    "proofCase": "rate-violated",
    "evidence": "designed",
    "capability": "sealing-and-the-publication-record"
  }
]
```

**`needs`.** This is the capability map's `inputs` from other roles, limited to producers whose own capability is `built` or `partial` today.

- `brand-kit-assembly` and `messaging-kit` are excluded because both are `planned` in the Designer and Writer maps.
- Source evidence for each entry:
  - `strategy-brief`: `skill/SKILL.md:29` (seal against strategy provenance) and `src/record/types.ts:82` (`strategyRevision`).
  - `components-and-blocks`: `src/` imports `@clossys/designer/blocks` 12 times.
  - `token-contract-and-brand-overlay-binding`: `publisher-preview` binds a consumer `brand.css`.
  - `logo-and-identity-files`: the `channel-kits` input.
  - `copy-registry`: `src/core/resolve-surface.ts:1` imports from `@clossys/writer`.
  - `keep-verdict`: `skill/SKILL.md:10` ("seal ... after a keep").

**`solves`.** `problem` and `statement` are the seed entry in `docs/contracts/client-problems.json`. `metric` is Publisher's own metric. `proofCase` is `rate-violated`, which shows `publisher-rate-check` actually detecting an intent that has no matching immutable record. `evidence` is `designed` because no retained qualification record includes the new case yet.

**Expected cycle.** Customer's lane declares `needs: @clossys/publisher surface-documents`, and the prepared `needs` above includes `@clossys/customer keep-verdict`. Once both are declared, the current gate's `--enforce` will report a Customer↔Publisher `needs-graph-cycle`. That cycle is the legitimate judge-then-seal loop that #1387 (framework v4) judges per capability.

**Deferred: `intake` and `status`.** Neither is declared.

author: gracepriest
body:
Six fixes, each with its own tests run through the optimizer. Master is merged in (`c8acb2f`). Master had independently landed an overlapping float fix (`3e6dd7f`, `8ff4f3b`), and `IROptimizer.cs` uses master's version of those hunks; only what master lacked is added here.

## 1. Floating `x + 0` and `x - (-0)` (IR optimizer)
Master left `x + 0 → x` ungated. In IEEE 754, `-0 + 0` is `+0`, so the fold returned `-0`: measured on C# and C++, with `x = -0`, `1 / (x + 0)` printed `-Infinity` instead of `Infinity`. `x + 0`, `0 + x` and a `-0.0` subtrahend now fold only for integral arithmetic. `x - (+0)`, `x * 1` and `x / 1` are exact and still fold.

**Tests:** `FloatingPointIdentityFoldTests.cs`.

## 2. Re-point consumers when a fold or CSE removes a value (IR optimizer)
**Peephole.** The pass replaced a folded value with an assignment to a temp no backend declares, and never re-pointed its consumers. Measured with Integer `Show(n - n)`:
- **C++:** undeclared temp.
- **C#:** CS0103.
- **JavaScript:** `ReferenceError: t0 is not defined`.

On C# and JavaScript, `Show(P() * 0)` also ran `P()` **twice**. A folded temp now passes its value straight to its consumers; a named local is still an assignment.

**CSE.** Its private `ReplaceAllUses` skipped compares, call arguments and `Return`, so C++ got an undeclared temp. It now uses the base `ReplaceUses` over the whole function.

**Tests:** `OptimizerOrphanedTempTests.cs`. 18 of 21 fail without the fix.

## 3. `x / x`
Master removed this arm independently. This branch's hand-built IR pin, that Integer and Long `x / x` must not fold, still holds on the merged tree.

## 4. C#: a constant zero divisor is CS0020, not a run-time throw
Roslyn rejects a constant over a constant zero as a *compile* error; .NET throws `DivideByZeroException` at run time. Copy propagation produces that shape often: `Dim z = 0 : 5 \ z` → `5 / 0`. A constant-zero integral or Decimal divisor is now emitted as `new[] { 0 }[0]`, which is not a constant expression.

**Tests:** `CSharpConstantDivideByZeroTests.cs`. 8 of 10 fail without the fix.

## 5. C++ and JavaScript: integer `\` and `Mod` by zero throw `DivideByZeroException`
Measured on master:
- **C++:** the process died with `SIGFPE` (exit 136) before any `Catch` ran.
- **JavaScript:** no throw at all. `7 \ 0` gave `Infinity` and `7 Mod 0` gave `NaN`, stored in an Integer.

**C++:** integral `\`/`Mod` go through `BasicLang::CheckedDiv`/`CheckedMod`. They throw the typed `NetException` the `Catch` ladder already matches, so `DivideByZeroException`, `ArithmeticException` and `Exception` all catch it.

**JavaScript:** integer-family `\`/`Mod` go through `__blIntDiv`/`__blIntMod`, emitted only when used, together with the `DivideByZeroException` class chain.

**`When` guards** skip the semantic analyzer, so their operator trees are untyped; an untyped `\` is now always checked.

Floating division is unchanged, and so are nonzero results (truncation toward zero, and `Mod` taking the dividend's sign), checked against the C# backend.

**Tests:** `IntegerDivideByZeroTests.cs`. 8 of 11 fail without the fix. Two `CppIntegerDivisionTests` expectations moved from `a / b` to `BasicLang::CheckedDiv(a, b)`.

## 6. `Select Case` (and `If`) inside `Try` / `Catch` / `Finally`
Measured on master:
- **C#:** `Try : Select Case n …` emitted an empty `try { }`. The whole `Select` vanished, with a green build. A `Finally` followed no terminator at all, so an `If` there vanished too.
- **C++:** "jump to label 'switch0_end'". `ControlFlowTargets` ignored `IRSwitch.PatternCases`, where the parser puts every `Case`, so the case bodies landed outside the try braces.
- **C++:** with that fixed, a `Select` inside `Finally` looped forever. The two `Finally` copies fell out of their region; they now jump to an exit label, like the existing `_fnex` copy.
- **All backends:** the semantic analyzer never visited a `Finally` body. An `If` there was untyped (`cannot convert 'bool' to 'void*'` on C++), and an undeclared name compiled successfully. `Finally` bodies are now analyzed; the full suite shows nothing in the repo relied on the old behaviour.

**Tests:** `SelectInsideTryTests.cs`. A 22-line probe (`Select` in try, catch and finally, `If` in finally, a loop in a try) is identical on C#, C++ and JavaScript. Reverting all fixes fails 5 of 7; reverting only the analyzer fix, or only the `Finally` labels, fails exactly its own pins.

## Gate (Linux container), full suite (fast subset plus Integration)
| | Passed | Failed | Skipped | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| master `5114dd8` | 6257 | 0 | 679 | 6936 |
| this branch `c8acb2f` | 6341 | **0** | 679 | 7020 |

- **Both tiers:** green, with zero failures. The 84 extra tests are this branch's.
- **Not covered:** a Windows run, and the C++ `.blproj` project route, which needs MSVC.

## Found, not fixed
- **C++ Decimal division by zero** throws a plain `std::runtime_error`, so only `Catch … As Exception` catches it, not `DivideByZeroException`. The Decimal runtime is spliced before `NetException`, so fixing it means reordering the runtime splices.
- **`Integer.MinValue \ -1` and `Mod -1`:** .NET throws `OverflowException`; C++ and JavaScript don't.

author: bytemastermike
body:
Follow-up to #48. It closes both gaps listed there.

## 1. Model tool calls cannot narrow a resolved range
When `resolve_time` produced a multi-day span, `apply_harness_years(..., hold_window=True)` applies to any model tool call whose years all fall inside the resolved years. If the call sends a single year or a different window, it gets the resolved `start_date` and `end_date` instead.
- `2021 to 2025` with a model `year=2023` becomes `2021-01-01..2025-12-31`.
- `from January 2024 up to today` with a model `year=2024` or `2024-01-01..2024-01-31` becomes `2024-01-01..<today>`.
- A single-year question stays single-year. A span that is exactly one calendar year is written as `year=`, so `year=2024` for "in 2024" is untouched. A narrower June window becomes `year=2024`.
- A weekly time series over a multi-year span switches to monthly, since weekly requires one year. This is the same rule the router applies.
- A year outside the range keeps the existing rules. `2019` is overridden and `2030` is rejected, with identical results with and without the hold.
- Each correction is logged as a `harness_time_correction` event (resolved, requested, applied) and listed under `time_corrections` on the `tool_attempt` event.

**Every provider:** the rule lives in `apply_harness_years`, which `ToolExecutor.execute` and `preview_arguments` run for all model tool calls. That covers Ollama, the hosted OpenAI-compatible path, Jev tool pick, and the slot-grounded rescue. Router-built deterministic calls pass `harness_call=True` and are exempt, so a deliberate per-year router call is not collapsed. Caveat companion calls are qualification calls and skip the guard, as before.

## 2. Bare pre-2000 years
A bare `19xx` year (for example `How many CPUC ignitions were there in 1999?`) now resolves to `out_of_coverage` and gets the same clarify as `'99`: "Year 1999 is outside warehouse coverage 2014-2026". On main it resolved to `none` and the year was ignored. Decimals (coordinates like `38.1985`), thousands separators, `$`, and acreage (`1950 acres`) are not read as years. 18xx years are not handled.

## Verification
- Tests: 12 new tests in `tests/agent/test_model_date_range.py`. They cover the three requested questions, the window form, a matching window left alone, the weekly-to-monthly switch, out-of-range parity, the router exemption, and two `ToolExecutor.execute` tests on a mock transport. Those check the backend request params and the logged correction. Two more tests in `test_time_resolve.py` cover 1900s years and the number guards.
- `pytest tests/agent`: 318 passed, 1 failed. Main: 306 passed, 1 failed. The failure is the same test on both: `test_cpuc_vs_us_companion_attaches_sample_caveat_without_us_primary`.
- Full suite: 352 passed. Main: 340 passed. Both have the identical 11 failures and 31 errors, which need the DB and the risk service running.
- Route report against main, running `route_question` and `resolve_time` over `cases.json` (107), `jev_paraphrases.json` (41), `jev_holdout.json` (97), `jev_holdout_raw.json` (100), and `jev_blind_questions.json` (0 questions). Result: **0 route changes and 0 time-resolution changes across 345 questions.** No question in those sets contains a 1900s number. The v2 and v3 holdout files that CLAUDE.md lists are not on main yet, so they were not part of this run. No model or Jev calls were made.

## Per-year questions keep per-year calls
The hold applies only when the question asks for one continuous span. `resolve_time` sets `per_year` when the question names years other than a span's own endpoints (`in 2021, 2022, and 2023`) or uses a breakdown word (each year, every year, per year, by year, year by year, year over year, annual, annually, yearly). In that case a call for one named year, or for one year inside the requested range, stands unchanged. A year outside the question's years is still corrected or rejected by the existing rules. Without this, `each year from 2018 to 2020` would have returned the same three-year total three times under different year labels.

Tests: `PG&E ignitions in 2021, 2022, and 2023` and `PG&E ignitions each year from 2018 to 2020` keep one call per year. A year outside a per-year range is still corrected, and 2030 is still rejected. `2021 to 2025` still widens a single-year call, and `in 2024` is unchanged. `pytest tests/agent`: 322 passed, 1 failed (the same test that fails on main).

Route report after this commit: 0 route changes and 0 time-resolution changes across the same 345 questions, not counting the new `per_year` key. 26 questions set `per_year`. Four of them combine a range with breakdown words (holdout ho_005, ho_008, ho_032, ho_077) and would have been collapsed by the first commit.

## Listed years reject unlisted ones
When the question lists separate years and names no span (`PG&E ignitions in 2021, 2022, and 2023`), a call filtered on a year outside the list (2019) now returns `year_not_derived` ("Year 2019 is not one of the years named in the question (2021, 2022, 2023)"). Before this commit it passed through unchanged. With no span to substitute, correcting it to one of the listed years would be a guess, so the call is rejected rather than corrected. Calls for each listed year stand. Comparison period keys keep their existing rewrite.

Tests: 2019 is rejected, as a bare year and as a start/end window, with and without the hold. 2021, 2022, and 2023 each stand. The executor returns `year_not_derived`. The range and single-year tests still pass. `pytest tests/agent`: 325 passed, 1 failed (the same test that fails on main).

Route report after this commit: 0 route changes and 0 time-resolution changes across the 345 questions. I also ran all 137 deterministic router tool calls from those questions through `apply_harness_years` on main and on this branch. The output was identical and there were no errors, so no router call is newly rejected.

author: agentydragon
body:
## Problem

`//agentplane/app:test_thread_browser` runs 27 items on 4 shards against a 300 s `medium` limit. pytest-shard places each item on a shard by a hash of its node ID, so the shards got 8, 9, 5 and 5 items. Cost here is driven by item count more than by which tests run. Each item pays about 6–7 s of fixture setup (fresh Postgres, Electric and nginx containers, an app process and a browser) plus 0.5–3 s of test body. Only three items run longer than 5 s: `archived_thread…` about 7–14 s, `switching_threads…` about 10–17 s, and `projected_browser…` about 10–12 s. On both devel invocations measured below, the 8- and 9-item shards had the slowest median times and the 5-item shards the fastest.

## Change

`py_test(shard_count = N)` now loads `util/testing/sharding.py` in place of pytest-shard. Collected item `i` runs on shard `i % N`. Sharding happens after `-k`/`--test_filter` deselection, so a filtered item still runs on some shard. The JS visual sweep already shards this way in `util/testing/frontend_visual/sharding.mjs`.

pytest_bazel touches `TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE` only when it can import `pytest_shard`, so the plugin touches the file itself. `util/testing/test_sharding.py` checks three things: the position assignment, sharding after filtering, and the status file.

Sharding by position suits this file without tuning. The three items with long test bodies are at collection positions 1, 2 and 4, so they land on shards 1, 2 and 4. The three `replay_after=4` cases land on three different shards too. The result is 7/7/7/6 items. A new test shifts later assignments by one, but shard sizes always stay within one item of each other.

This affects the only other sharded `py_test`, `//agentplane/runner:test_native_resources` (6 items, 2 shards). It passed with 3 items per shard in invocation `7bb616cc-5ef6-410c-919a-71e3418756ca`, together with the new unit test.

## Measurement

Every run used `--nocache_test_results --runs_per_test=3 --test_timeout=900`. The table shows the test attempt time, which is the clock the 300 s timeout counts, in seconds for runs 1/2/3:

| shard | devel `08cdf0bb` | devel `71f12be9` | branch `a7c440a8` | branch `76295348` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 8 items: 116/143/146 | 8: 125/212/235 | 7: 119/130/178 | 7: 111/183/226 |
| 2 | 9 items: 122/164/193 | 9: 172/200/232 | 7: 126/128/185 | 7: 148/194/212 |
| 3 | 5 items: 99/102/141 | 5: 98/122/134 | 7: 98/108/139 | 7: 108/128/142 |
| 4 | 5 items: 119/125/133 | 5: 128/145/221 | 6: 124/132/161 | 6: 123/156/229 |

The full invocation IDs are `08cdf0bb-ca70-492a-a2fb-d1cf3603a4c5` and `71f12be9-089a-49b1-adbe-26193d52ba69` for devel (`d900157d`), and `a7c440a8-f2ef-4b67-b474-98f8ce8dcff6` and `76295348-008e-4a3e-ac45-fa372327926c` for this branch (`31f85735`; the later commit only corrects a comment). `71f12be9` and `76295348` ran at the same time; the first pair ran about 20 minutes apart.

Median of the six runs per shard:

| | shard 1 | shard 2 | shard 3 | shard 4 | slowest − fastest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| devel | 144.5 | 182.5 | 112 | 130.5 | 70.5 s |
| this branch | 154 | 166.5 | 118 | 144 | 48.5 s |

The median of the slowest shard fell from 182.5 s to 166.5 s. The slowest single attempt fell from 193 to 185 s in the first pair and from 235 to 229 s in the concurrent pair. The total amount of work did not change: the median over all 24 shard runs was 137.5 s before and 135.5 s after.

Shard sizes are now balanced, but the time saved is small compared with run-to-run noise. The same shard varies by up to about 120 s between runs, mostly because the first test's image loads are slow on a busy executor. **I did not measure a change in the timeout rate and do not claim one.** The slowest attempt in these runs was 235 s.

## Left out

- **Moving the slow tests into their own target**, as `test_thread_window_browser` did. The slow items are few and are already spread out by position. A new target would pay about 25 s before pytest starts, plus 30–50 s of image loads, to run about 50 s of tests.
- **More shards.** Each shard pays the same fixed start-up cost before its first test.
- **Duration-weighted assignment** (pytest-split with a checked-in durations file). Per-item cost is uniform enough here that balancing by count gets most of the benefit, and a durations file is one more thing to keep up to date.
- **Removing `pytest-shard` from `pyproject.toml` and the lockfile.** Nothing depends on it after this change, but regenerating `requirements_bazel.txt` and the Gazelle manifest is a separate change.
- **The fixed per-shard costs**: Python bytecode compilation before pytest starts, and image loads on the first test. Most of the shard-to-shard variance is how long those image loads take on a given executor (postgres alone took 8–35 s). Ryuk's Docker Hub pull is handled in #7743.

## Summary

Four separate "send this to Compose" buttons navigated to `/compose?content=<text>` (Clips' Schedule, the Templates library's Use button, Trend Scout's Draft Post) or `/compose` with nothing at all (Creator Studio's "Schedule this video") — Compose only ever read `?draft=`, `?id=`, `?template=`, and `?starterTemplate=`. body:
## Root cause
CI's 8-run flaky-coverage sweep on main (825693b) found these `internal/orchestrate/ciwait.go` statements whose coverage flips run to run:
- `waitForCommitChecks`: 132.5-134.1 (1/8), 153.5-155.1 (6/8)
- `commitChecks`: 477 (3/8), 487 (3/8), 491 (3/8)
- `commitCheckRuns`: 894 (2/8), 905 (1/8)

None of these branches had a test built to hit them on purpose. The only prior coverage came by accident: a signal-killed subprocess or a slow CI host occasionally tripped the same transient-retry / hard-failure branch while a different assertion was the point of the test, so whether the branch fired depended on real-world timing noise, not on test design. This is a test-coverage gap, not a production timing bug — no seam or clock injection is needed.

## Fix (test-only, no production code changed)
- Three new `WaitForCommitChecks` tests force the transient-retry-exhausted pending path deterministically with an always-killed fake `gh`, one for each of the candidate (pull-request) path's reads: `pullRequestIdentity` and `candidateContainsTarget` (the direct-target sibling and the `targetHead` twin were already covered by an existing test).
- Five new direct `commitChecks`/`commitCheckRuns` tests force each hard, non-retryable failure (a malformed body or an authoritative HTTP error) on the pull-request identity, check-runs, statuses, and Actions-runs reads those functions call, using the same fake-`gh` pattern already used elsewhere in this test file.

## Evidence
- `go test ./internal/orchestrate/... -run '<new+related tests>' -p 1 -parallel 1 -timeout 20m -count=20`: all pass.
- 5 independent `-coverprofile` runs (`-count=1` each, targeted `-run` over all ciwait_*_test.go tests) confirm every one of the 8 previously flaky statements (ciwait.go:132-134, 153-155, 477, 487, 491, 894, 905) is covered (count>0) on all 5 runs.
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/orchestrate/...`: 0 issues.

## Diff size
2 files changed, 224 insertions(+), 0 deletions. Test-only.

author: millzach
body:
## What changed

- **Add host connects before it saves (#206).** Settings > Hosts > **Add host** is now variant A of the prototype. It has one "SSH host or alias" combobox and optional Username and Port. The install and data folders sit under "Folders on the host", with the current defaults (`~/.local/share/sotto-host`, `~/.sotto`). Pressing Add host connects from inside the dialog. The dialog says it is connecting, asks SSH's host-key, passphrase or password question itself, and saves the host only when it answers and pairing succeeds. On failure nothing is saved, the pairing credential is removed, a pairing the host already recorded is revoked, and the dialog says what happened, that nothing was saved, and to add the host again. The name defaults to the alias.
- **Suggestions from the SSH setup.** Main reads `~/.ssh/config`, following `Include` and skipping wildcard and negated patterns, and `~/.ssh/known_hosts`, skipping hashed and marked lines. This is T3 Code's `discoverSshHosts`. The window reaches the result only through a new `hosts:ssh-suggestions` preload bridge. Nothing read is logged or leaves the computer. An end-to-end run reads a stand-in SSH folder in its own profile.
- **The saved host row.** Each row reads "SSH forge · Connected", "Reconnecting…", "Switched off", or "Needs attention" with the sentence under it. It has an On/Off switch named "Keep forge connected, now and when Sotto starts" and a More menu: Stop host (for a host Sotto started and can reach), Rename, Edit connection and Forget. Save, Connect, Disconnect and "Use this host" are gone. A host that needs attention offers **Connect again**, or Stop host when its sentence asks for that.
- **Switched on, switched off, and reconnect at launch.** Saved hosts carry an `enabled` flag, written only when a host is off, so old files read as on and forge starts on. Hosts that are on connect in the background at start with Reconnecting… and the 3/4/8/16 s backoff, and a typed final failure still stops the retries. Switching off disconnects and cancels any retry, and keeps the row, the pairing and a host Sotto started running. Switching on connects now and at every launch.
- **The host where work happens.** Once a remote host is connected, each project row in the Threads sidebar has a host badge, "This computer" included, and the composer footer shows "Runs on forge". With more than one host listed, New thread starts with a row of host buttons, and choosing one lists that host's projects.
- **After review.** Switching on now reads Connecting… for its first attempt, not Reconnecting…. A drop during an add no longer schedules a reconnect for an unsaved host. New thread always has a host pressed, even if a second host connects while it is open.
- **After the second review.**
  - A host switched off while a reconnect is closing the old session stays off. Before, it could connect with its switch reading Off. The retry timer and a drop now skip a host that is off.
  - A host switched off mid-connect reads Switched off, not "Needs attention: The SSH connection was cancelled."
  - Cancelling Add host after pairing revokes the pairing over the open tunnel. Quitting mid-add cancels the add and waits for its credential to be cleared.
  - A saved host's SSH question (password, passphrase, new host key) is now asked over whichever page is open, not only on Settings > Hosts. Before, a launch reconnect that needed an answer timed out into Needs attention if the user was on the Threads page. The question waits while a Hosts dialog is open.
  - The badge follows the owner's rule: it shows once a remote host is connected, including when the local host is off.
  - A host name longer than 80 characters is cut to 80 for the default name. A username and host that together exceed 256 characters get a plain sentence instead of a raw validation error.
  - An SSH `Include` with a wildcard in a folder name (`~/.colima/*/ssh_config`) is followed, as OpenSSH does.

### What I worked out

- **Username and Port** reach ssh by the routes it already had. Username builds `user@alias`, and a username typed in the field wins over one typed in front of the host. Port is the existing `sshPort` (`-p`). The identity file comes from the SSH configuration. An identity file saved by an earlier Sotto still shows in Edit connection, so it can be cleared.
- **How a new thread starts today.** New thread creates the thread on its project's host before the first message is written, and the composer then belongs to that thread. So no composer ever exists without a host. The host is chosen in New thread's Host row, and the composer shows it fixed as "Runs on forge" instead of a "Run on" menu. When a new folder is added as a project, New thread first selects the chosen host in the router, so the project lands there. With "Use this host" gone, that is the only way to choose. New thread offers "Local folder" only for this computer, because a remote host has no folder here to browse.
- **Stop host switches the host off.** A host left on would be started again at the next launch, which would undo the stop.
- **Version mismatch on add.** A host that answers with another Sotto version is still saved, so its row can say which side to update and offer Stop host, as before.
- **A second route to a saved host is refused**, whether it matches by target or by host ID.
- **Edit connection** saves and then reconnects a host that is on. It also shows this computer's client ID, which the README's `--revoke-client` instructions point to.
- **Copy changes from the prototype**, made where the plain-words rule asks for them. The failed-add sentence says "add the host again" in place of the launcher's "reconnect". A reconnect prompt's cancel reads "Switch it off", because that is what the press does. The empty New thread list for a remote host reads "No projects on this host yet." I left out the version number the prototype shows on connected rows, because the host status does not carry it.

### Docs amended

- `docs/plans/forge-clients-134.md` records the pick: variant A, September 23, 2026, from `prototype/hosts-add-206`, with the owner's two decisions.
- ADR-0025 has a new September 23 amendment covering Add host connecting first, the `enabled` flag, reconnect at launch, and Stop host switching the host off.
- `CONTEXT.md` has new entries for "Switched on, switched off (a saved host)" and "Host for new work", and an updated Askpass helper entry.
- The README's remote hosts section is rewritten.
- The verification note is `docs/verification/hosts-add-206-2026-09-23.md`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run notices:verify` (rerun on acf09e54): clean (174 notice components).
- `npm test -- --maxWorkers=2` (rerun on acf09e54): 386 files passed, 20 skipped. 4992 tests passed, 47 skipped, 0 failed.
- New tests:
  - `tests/unit/main/sshSuggestions.test.ts` covers Include, wildcards, Match blocks, several aliases on one Host line, hashed known_hosts lines and a missing folder.
  - `tests/integration/desktopHosts.test.ts` covers add saving only on success, no credential on failure, revocation after a failure that follows pairing, in-dialog questions and cancel, rename, the switch, Stop host switching off, and reconnect at start for hosts that are on (not for ones that are off). It also checks the backoff and final failure at launch, and that a saved-hosts file from before the switch still reads.
  - `tests/unit/renderer/hostsSettings.test.tsx` covers the dialog, combobox keys, the switch, the menu and Connect again.
  - `tests/unit/renderer/hostVisibility.test.tsx` covers the badge, the New thread Host row and the "Runs on" chip.
  - `tests/integration/realSshd.test.ts` now adds its host with Add host. It runs only on the Linux CI job, not locally.
- `npm run build && npx playwright test tests/e2e/hosts.spec.ts` (rerun on acf09e54): 1 passed. It covers the switched-off row, the dialog's

author: eljaguaro-gitdown
body:
## What happened

On dead-set.org in iPhone Safari, with the ringer switch on **silent**, the player ran (clock moving, pause button showing) and made **no sound**. Turning silent off made it audible. Reported by Jay on 2026-09-23 on the "Gilded Grits and Red Rock Goodbyes" setlist.

## Why, when iOS already uses `<audio>`

`GaplessEngine` already sets `webAudioIsDisabled` on iOS, so playback goes through a plain `<audio>` element, which normally ignores the silent switch. But the `gapless` library still **creates an `AudioContext`**:
- on every `resumeAudioContext()`, which we call on every play tap
- in its own track-fetch path

Safari puts any page holding an `AudioContext` into the **"ambient"** audio session. Ambient obeys the silent switch, and for the **whole page**, including the `<audio>` element.

## Fix

`src/lib/player/audioSession.ts` sets `navigator.audioSession.type = "playback"`, the session music apps use. `GaplessEngine` calls it at the top of `unlock()` and `play()`, before anything can resume the context.

- **Safari 17+:** plays through the silent switch.
- **Older Safari:** has no API for this, so it's unchanged.
- **Native iOS app:** unaffected, since its `AVAudioSession` is already `.playback`.

## Verification

- **New tests:** they check the session is `"playback"` **at the moment the queue resumes audio**, via `unlock()` and via `play()`, and that browsers without the API are untouched. **The two session tests fail without the fix.**
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`: 0 errors. `eslint src/lib/player`: clean.
- `vitest run`: 29 files, 186 tests pass. `anonDraftRls` was excluded because it needs live Supabase.
- **Not verifiable here:** only a real iPhone on silent can confirm the fix works. After publish, play a setlist on dead-set.org with the switch on silent.

## Also found while debugging (not in this PR)

The play log showed all 13 tracks of the setlist starting and ending in 6 seconds. Two bugs made that look worse than it was:
1. **The 3-error cap never trips.** `AudioPlayerContext` resets `consecutiveErrorsRef` on every slot change, so after an error, advancing to the next track resets the count. A broken source runs the whole setlist instead of stopping on "That tape won't play".
2. **Fast errors are logged as skips.** When a track errors before its `play_events` row is inserted, `finalizePlayEvent("error")` finds no active event. The next start then records the row as `"skipped"`.

author: primex-tech
body:
## Summary

Importing the same repository or archive multiple times no longer silently creates duplicate projects: a match is detected and the caller is asked to confirm before a second copy is stored.

Closes #87

## Changes

- `Project.content_hash` (SHA-256 of the archive payload) and `Project.default_branch` (migration `c1a2b3c4d5e6`).
- **Archive imports**: compare the archive content hash against existing projects in the same workspace.
- **GitHub imports**: compare `owner/name` (case-insensitive) plus the default branch; the repository payload is fetched once and reused for the import.
- On a detected duplicate the API returns **409** with `{duplicate: true, match, duplicate_of}` and stores **nothing**; the caller may resend with `confirm` to import anyway.
- Import UI (`workspace_detail.js`): on 409 it asks the user to confirm, then re-submits with `confirm` when accepted (or cancels).

## How tested

- `pytest tests/test_project_import_duplicates.py tests/test_project_import.py` - 33 passed (9 new: archive hash, GitHub repo+branch matching, confirmation, workspace scoping).
- `ruff check .` and `black --check .` - clean.

Note: `tests/test_workspaces_api.py::test_list_own_workspaces` is a pre-existing flake on `main` (it fails when run alone; `api_list_workspaces` orders by `updated_at.desc()` and equal timestamps fall back to insertion order). It is unrelated to this change.

author: gouarin
body:
Tutorials 02 to 07 and the tutorials index, rewritten for flows. Every frame and number on these pages now comes from a real pi 0.85.1 run on a small open-weight model. The "frames predate the switch" notes are gone.

Two commits. The repository squash-merges.

## What each page teaches now

- **02 Three scouts, one answer**: `cat flows/explore.md`, then `/run explore`. It shows the plan drawn live, the answer with its `ok · runs/…` line and last frame, the run directory as a flow writes it, and `usage.json`. The captures found two new things. All nine line numbers the scouts cited were wrong again. The docs scout read tutorial 03 and took its quoted frame as documentation. And a follow-up question made the session read `src/usage.ts` and `src/subagent.ts` itself, taking the window from 0.2% to 18.4%.
- **03 Keep the session out of it**: `/step scout`, `/step reviewer`, `/chain`, `/quote`, with a new section where a stage is a flow (`/step explore`). Asked "what did the reviewer say?", the session listed `runs/` with `bash` and grepped the reviewer's transcript. `/step` keeps a result out of the context, not off the disk, and the page now says so.
- **04 Write the chain down**: now teaches writing a flow, `.pi/flows/docs-drift.md` with a `parallel` and a synthesiser. It covers `/flows` with the bound, `/flows docs-drift` with the plan, the run, what the last turn receives under `reads:`, a typo refused before any spawn (`compare.agent: synthesizer is unknown; did you mean synthesiser?`), a missing section listed as broken, and what a flow cannot say (invariant 3).
- **05 An agent that cannot do harm**: same lesson, recaptured. The same "rename" request went two ways. The first time, the session passed it on and nothing changed. The second time, the session rewrote the task and called `edit` itself.
- **06 Teach it a house rule**: none of three runs opened the skill unprompted. With the sentence added to the prompt, both runs did, and one named a smell by the skill's own name. With the skill misspelled, the session deleted the `skills:` line from the agent file so the call would pass. The page now says that.
- **07 Two agents arguing until LGTM**: recaptured the loop and the diff. The cap is now shown from a real run: `until APPROVED` with a cap of two ends "Glad it works for you." / "You're welcome.", `2 iterations NOT converged`. The page used to say every workflow hands a reviewer its `verdict` tool. That is wrong, and it is corrected.
- **index**: entries 3 and 4 follow.

## Product defect fixed

`fix(language)`: English tasks came back in French. Both halves of the language rule pointed away from English: the closing line said "not in the language of these instructions", and the standing rule said the prompt is "always written in English". Measured with a scout and a test reader, 3 in 6 and 4 in 6 English tasks were answered in French. With the new wording, which points only at the work and names no language, 12 of 12 English tasks came back in English and 8 of 8 French ones in French. A test now holds both lines to that. Pages 02 to 05 were captured with the closing-line half of the fix in place. Pages 06 and 07 were captured with both halves.

## Product defects seen, not fixed here

- **A dangling `verdict` tool.** The shipped `reviewer` declares `verdict`, but only a flow node with `verdict:` registers the tool. In `/step` and in the `subagent` tool's `loop`, the reviewer still calls it. It got `Tool verdict not found` five times in one `/step`, and the tool row shows those refused calls as ordinary calls. The same can happen to `split`'s reviewer workers.
- **`↑0 ↓0` while a subagent works.** Usage only arrives when a turn ends, so every live row reads `↑0 ↓0` for the whole turn, which looks like a measured zero. The plan's summary line at the start reads `0 visits · 0s · ↑0 ↓0` the same way.
- **`$0.0000` in the tool row** for a provider that reports no cost. The live row leaves the cost out in that case.
- **`/flows` paints the whole listing in the warning colour** as soon as one file is refused, the valid flows included.
- **The `subagent loop` header** reads `coder [workflow]` when the model passes `agent` beside `steps`, and `coder → reviewer [workflow]` otherwise.
- **A model the session makes up.** Twice the session filled the tool's `model` with a model from a provider it had no key for, and the call failed at once. The row shows it in brackets, which is the only hint.
- **Lookups walk past a repository root.** In a checkout nested under another one, `.pi/pipelines/` is picked up from the outer checkout, and `/flows` lists its files as refused.

## Checks

`npm run docs`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and the sphinx build with `-W` pass.

author: trevorotts1
body:
**Stacked on #1243. The base is `fix/combined-script-defects`; retarget to `main` once #1243 merges.**

This is the second half of the class A sweep: every other script that read the agent roster from `agents.list[]` only. I found them by searching all `*.sh` and `*.py` files in the repo. On OpenClaw 2026.9.x, where agents live in `agents.entries` keyed by id, each of these saw zero agents.

**Why a second PR:** together with the fixes in #1243, this would have been about 57 files, well past the ~40-file limit for one PR. #1243 carries the named defects for all seven classes, with one test per class and the CI guard. This PR carries the extra readers the search turned up, plus one test file. It also adds this test and these files to the #1243 CI guard.

## Fixed
**Resolving the main agent's workspace.** These fell through to `agents.defaults.workspace` and so edited the wrong AGENTS.md:
- `07-kie-setup`, `63-agnes-image`, `64-agnes-video`, `66-kie-image`, `67-kie-video`, `68-kie-audio` `wire.sh`
- `scripts/onboarding-state.sh`
- `scripts/qc-assert-platform-facts-stamped.sh`

**`scripts/grant-ceo-consent.sh`:** it found no CEO agent ("NO_CEO"), so granting or revoking consent did nothing. It now edits the CEO entry in whichever shape the config uses.

**Provider-capability QC:** `scripts/qc-assert-provider-capability-invariants.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test-provider-capabilities.sh` checked no agents on these boxes, so their per-agent multimodal checks passed falsely. On `entries` boxes the settings they check are under `entry.memory.search`.

**Model pins:** `shared-utils/select_model.py` (`_list_available_models`) and `shared-utils/assert_model_sovereignty.py` (`scan_config`). Per-agent model pins were invisible to the model selector and to the sovereignty gate.

**`32-…/register-routing-dept.py`:** its "already registered" check never matched on these boxes.

**`32-…/run-full-install.sh` phase 4:** it counted `["agents"]["list"]`. On an `entries` box that raised KeyError, the count came out 0, and **every fresh install failed there**. The jq lookups for the sovereign model and the pinned models also read `list` only.

**`23-…/verify-wiring.sh`:** the registration check reported every department "not found".

**`scripts/qc-system-integrity.sh`:** checks 2.4, 2.5 and 9.2, and the main-workspace lookup.

**`58-…/install-podcast-department.sh`:** the `agentDir` lookup and the `entry_present` read-back.

**`32-…/add-department.sh`:** `_runtime_present` never found the entry, so the script always fell through to its inline fallback. That fallback then **wrote `agents.list`** on an `entries` box, which the gateway rejects with `Unrecognized key "list"`. The fallback now writes `entries[<id>]` the same way `materialize-dept-agents.sh` does: no `"id"` field in the body, settings under `memory.search`, and `ownership="explicit"` when the write makes the roster multi-agent.

## Found but not fixed
- `31-upgraded-memory-system/scripts/activate-memory-stack.sh` reads and creates `agents.list`. But the whole script writes `agents.defaults.memorySearch`, and the 2026.9.4 schema has no such key, so it needs a real migration for 9.x. A patch limited to `agents.list` would leave it broken, so it needs its own change.
- `add-department.sh` has a Telegram-bindings lookup, around line 588, that reads `agents.list` only. `telegram` is not a key an entry has in the 9.x schema, so there is nothing to find on those boxes.
- Scripts that already read both shapes were left alone: `materialize-dept-agents.sh`, `guard-department-runtime-parity.py`, `update-skills.sh`, `oc-schema-migrate.py`, `oc-atomic-upgrade.sh`, `ceo_execution_policy.py`, `build-workforce.py`, and others.

## Tests
`tests/unit/agents-entries-remaining-readers.test.py` has 13 cases. Each runs a script's real code against a config that has only `agents.entries`, and each fails on the unpatched file: 8 of 8 against the first commit's files, 5 of 5 against the second's. All 13 pass here.

All changed shell files pass `/bin/bash -n` with macOS bash 3.2. The first version of this change put an apostrophe inside a heredoc within `$(...)`, which bash 3.2 cannot parse. The same bug in #1243's retire script is fixed in #1243 as commit cf89e7d65.

**Related suites, green here with /bin/bash 3.2 first on PATH:**
- provider-capability-guard, test_shared_client_paths, both model-selector suites, test_onboarding_qc_deadline
- onboarding-state-obs-api (18/18), state-mark-field-silent-noop, install-state-fail-open (12/12), test-ceo-tool-gate
- test-smoke-provider-internal-channel, test_register_routing_sidecar, test_f31_model_policy, test_model_router (116)
- test_add_department_runtime (8/8), podcast-activation-install-path (39), test_install_podcast_department (35), test-podcast-provision-activation (20)
- test-net-new-department (16), test-board-join-chain, bounded-workforce-build-resume, standard-first-cron-awareness, cc-done-degraded-retry-gate

**Already failing on `main`, with identical results here:** system-integrity-warning-promotion, test-wiring-gate-role-dir-walk, test-trio-gate, qc-podcast-activation-gate (7 of 29).

## Overlap with open PRs
- **#1239** (`update-skills.sh`): no overlap; this PR does not touch that file. A test merge was clean.
- **#1240** (`run-full-install.sh`): no shared hunks. This PR changes lines ~534, ~627 and ~2375; #1240 changes around line 2870. A test merge conflicts only in `test-sop-library-phase-wiring.sh`, which #1240 already conflicts with on `main` and this PR does not touch.
- **#1241** and **#1237** (to be re-landed): test merges were clean.
- **Command Center #416**: a different repo.

Not merged, not tagged, and no client box was touched.

author: ksquared-16
body:
Completes the lifecycle doctrine for records created by mistake. Two commits, 25 files, no unrelated lane work.

**A change and a mistake are different truths.** Supersession requires the replacement to start strictly after the row it replaces and closes that row the day before, so the superseded row always asserts a non-empty period during which it was the truth. No arithmetic makes that window empty. Correct for "the child moved rooms"; a lie for "this was recorded against the wrong child".

**Placement and schedule cancel** reach `canceled`, which was already in both status vocabularies, both CHECK constraints, excluded from the operational unique index and excluded from the schedule-day projection — it simply had no writer.

**Enrollment void** adds a distinct terminal state. `canceled` was deliberately not widened: it means a commitment withdrawn before service began, and both the visibility law and the column comment lean on that. An agreement created in error could previously only be `ended`, which asserts service happened and keeps the child on the partner roster as genuine history. The guard is evidence, not time — if the attendance ledger holds an effective fact, a child actually arrived and the void is refused with 409. Dependent placements and assignments are cancelled in the same act.

**Schedule operational uniqueness** restores the invariant the canonical reader still assumes. `getOperationalScheduleAssignmentForAgreement` finishes with `.maybeSingle()`, which errors on a second match; the slice-1 index was dropped when assignments became multi-subject but the reader was never narrowed, so two concurrent creates could wedge an enrollment into permanent 500s. The new partial unique index is the reader predicate term for term, so staff, secondary and proposed rows are untouched. Censused first: zero violating agreements on the deployed primary.

No new scopes. No DELETE. Partner doctrine now names the six corrections: end, cancel, supersede, void, correct, reverse.

Gates: typecheck, typecheck:tests, production build, prebuild 5/5, partner package current. 516/517 across three consecutive full runs; the single red is the pre-existing attendanceEventsRead page-bound test, untouched.

## Qué
El asistente de bienvenida (logo → ~10 preguntas → resumen) solo emitía eventos de **salida** (`bienvenida_saltada`, `bienvenida_recortada`): se sabía cuánta gente se iba, no **dónde**. Con 5 de 7 estudios sin ninguna clase programada, recortarlo sin ese dato es adivinar.

## Eventos (PostHog, navegador)
| Evento | Cuándo | Props |
|---|---|---|
| `bienvenida_iniciada` | se enseña el primer paso (el logo) | — |
| `bienvenida_paso` | la 1.ª vez que se llega a cada pregunta | `paso` (id), `n`, `total`, `retomado?` |
| `bienvenida_resumen` | llega al resumen | — |
| `bienvenida_completada` | sale con el estudio montado | `destino` |
| `bienvenida_saltada` (ya existía) | «Ahora no» | + `en` (pantalla) |
| `primer_horario_visto` | ve la propuesta del calendario | `faltan_preguntas` |
| `primer_horario_propuesta` | llega a la propuesta de horario | — |

Lo siguiente (programarlo) ya lo mide el servidor con `horario_creado`. Ninguno lleva lo que la persona contestó: solo dónde está.

La regla «una vez por pantalla, volver atrás no cuenta doble, retomar se marca» vive en `lib/onboarding/embudo-wizard.ts`, con 6 tests.

Typecheck EXIT=0, lint limpio, unit 174/174, e2e Chromium de onboarding-valor, onboarding-datos y calendario-primer-horario (19/19; los primeros intentos de este último fallaron por timeout de compilación del dev server bajo carga, con `--timeout=150000` pasan 8/8).

## Cómo leerlo
Funnel en PostHog sobre esos eventos, por `paso`: dará la pantalla donde cae más gente. Con ~4 altas al mes no hay significación: se lee cualitativamente y sirve para decidir qué recortar.

author: copilot
body:
O Perfil IA refletia majoritariamente o perfil de marketplace e deixava de fora sinais já disponíveis no ERP, nas automações ETL e no resumo ERP do Cloud Engine. Esta mudança passa a compor o perfil consolidado com esses dados e corrige diferenças de shape entre payloads legados e atuais.

- **Composição do Perfil IA**
  - `ai_profile` passa a ser enriquecido dentro de `getCustomerProfile` com sinais de ERP e ETL já agregados no perfil consolidado.
  - O resumo e os insights agora consideram consumo de orçamento, saldo do mês, pagamentos ERP, sincronizações ETL, Open Finance, saldo OAuth e saldo projetado do Cloud Engine quando disponível.

- **Normalização de payloads ETL**
  - Open Finance agora aceita payloads em `camelCase` e `snake_case` para cartões e transações.
  - A leitura do saldo OAuth passa a suportar tanto `balance.available_balance` quanto campos de topo equivalentes.
  - A normalização preserva valores explícitos do payload de origem, inclusive strings vazias.

- **Merge com Cloud Engine**
  - Após mesclar `erp.cloud_engine`, o `ai_profile` é reprocessado usando o perfil bruto de marketplace como base.
  - Isso evita duplicar insights previamente enriquecidos ao incorporar os dados adicionais do ERP remoto.

- **Compatibilidade retroativa**
  - O perfil consolidado continua aceitando formatos legados de Open Finance sem exigir migração prévia dos dados persistidos.
  - As métricas derivadas passam a usar a mesma coleção normalizada em toda a cadeia de agregação.

```js
{
  ai_profile: {
    segment: "Perfil 360° conectado",
    summary: "Perfil 360° conectado · ERP 13.6% do orçamento consumido · ETL ativo com 1 despesa(s) sincronizada(s) · Open Finance com 1 cartão(ões) · saldo OAuth R$ 500.00",
```

author: gharlan
body:
Follow-up to #6690: identity of the installation lives in the project, runtime state of the current process stays in `Core`.

- `Core::getInstanceId()` → `AbstractProject::$instanceId`. Defaults to the env var `REX_INSTANCE_ID` (still required), the project can override it in code — the same pattern as `$instanceName`.
- `Core::getEnvironment()` (and with it `isBackend()`/`isFrontend()`) reads `$project->environment` instead of the `redaxo` property that `boot/core.php` used to set. The environment is runtime state of the process, so the accessors stay in `Core`, but the project is the single source now.
- The `$REX` array passed from `AbstractProject::bootCore()` to `boot/core.php` is gone: after dropping `REDAXO` it only carried the two path providers, which `boot/core.php` now creates from `Core::getProject()` itself. This also removes five psalm baseline entries.

`getMode()` stays in `Core` on purpose: the runtime reads `REX_MODE` before the project even exists.

### BC notes
- `Core::getProperty('redaxo')` now returns `null`; use `Core::isBackend()`/`Core::getEnvironment()`.
- There is no rector rule for `Core::getInstanceId()` → `Core::getProject()->instanceId` (like for `getServerName()`), it needs manual migration.
- In PHPUnit, `Core::getEnvironment()` now returns `Console` (the environment of the bootstrap project) instead of `Backend`. At runtime nothing changes, the `console` property is only set by `boot/console.php`.

author: arbeitandy
body:
## Why

normalise() stripped every combining mark, which folded ñ into n. So a definition that used ano passed the vocabulary check whenever año was in the frequency list. Ñ is a separate letter in Spanish, and render.sort_key already treats it as one. This brings validate.py in line.

A second commit, prompted by an independent Codex review, composes the definition to NFC before splitting it into words. Without that, a decomposed ñ (n + U+0303) was split into two words before normalise() ever saw it, so the fix did not reach unknown_words() or is_circular().

Fixes #4

## What this does not change

- **Stress accents still fold.** esta and está still count as the same word. Whether they should is a tolerance question, and it belongs to accept_definition, which is still yours to decide.
- **The 38 collision groups in #4 are all stress-accent groups:** 36 pairs and two triples (esta/está/ésta, este/esté/éste), 40 surplus forms in all. None involve ñ, so the current list still normalises to 2,960 keys. The fix matters for definition text, not for the list itself.
- **ü still folds to u.** Unlike ñ, it is not a separate letter.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests: año and ano stay distinct; knowing año does not make ano known; ñ survives case folding; a decomposed ñ equals a precomposed one; stress accents still fold. The first four failed before the fix.
- [x] Caller-level tests: a decomposed año is known to unknown_words() and caught by is_circular(). Both failed before the second commit.
- [x] mise run test and mise run lint pass

author: cassiqueiro
body:
## Summary

Makes the Web profile-switch endpoint describe what actually happened: the switch was accepted and queued, not completed successfully.

### Changes
- keeps existing validation for application context, profile id and profile existence;
- schedules `connect_profile()` on the wx thread as before;
- returns `202 Accepted` with `Profile switch started.` instead of `200 Ok`;
- adds API coverage proving the switch is queued through `wx.CallAfter()`.

### Why

`connect_profile()` only starts an asynchronous worker. The real client connection may fail later, so returning `200 Ok` implied a completed successful connection when the server had only accepted the request.

The existing Web UI treats any 2xx response as accepted and already announces “Switching client profile...”, so no frontend behavior change is required.

Based on current upstream main `b725bb2`.

author: vilenarios
body:
## Problem

CodeRabbit posts an auto-generated **Plan Mode** comment on every new issue. The comments carry nothing about the issue itself — a plan-generation checkbox, a list of loosely related issues and PRs, and suggested assignees.

They actively hurt backlog triage: an issue with zero human engagement still shows a comment count of 1, so there's no way to tell at a glance which issues have been discussed. #571, #572, and #573 each have exactly one comment, and in all three cases it's CodeRabbit's enrichment.

## Change

The repository had **no** CodeRabbit configuration at all, so enrichment was running on defaults. This adds a minimal `.coderabbit.yaml` setting only `issue_enrichment.auto_enrich.enabled: false`.

Everything omitted keeps CodeRabbit's defaults — which is exactly what the repository ran on before this file existed — so **PR review behavior is unchanged**. Enrichment can still be requested on an individual issue when it's actually wanted.

## Verification

Config-only change; no code paths touched. The `yaml-language-server` schema annotation validates the file against CodeRabbit's published v2 schema.

author: nkrishnaswami
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #37: a Chrome Web Store review reported that selecting a new list of links and opening them a few seconds after a prior "open selected links" action would silently do nothing, requiring a retry.
- Root cause: the injected file is a lightweight loader that kicks off an async `import()` of the real content script module and returns immediately, so the module's message listener can still be registering when `executeScript()`'s promise resolves. `OSLSession.setup()` only waited a fixed 10ms after reinjection before proceeding, and the popup called `setup()` a second, redundant time on top of that (`getLinksAndLabels()` already calls it), doubling the race window. When the module wasn't ready in time, `get_links` failed with "Could not establish connection" and the action silently no-opped.
- `setup()` now polls `ping` after reinjection until the content script actually responds instead of guessing a fixed delay, and the popup's redundant `setup()` call is removed.
- Reproduced against real Chrome (Playwright) end-to-end: ~1-in-5 failure rate on a cold content-script injection before this fix (0/6 failures after).

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run test` — all 139 tests pass, including two new regression tests in `test/extractLinks.test.ts` that fail against the pre-fix code with the exact "Could not establish connection" error and pass with the fix.
- [x] Manually reproduced the original failure end-to-end (Playwright driving a real Chrome instance through the popup and background code paths, navigating between two link selections) and confirmed the fix resolves it.

author: gergas3
body:
## Change

`setClientId` previously bound a channel to whatever `clientId` the connected client claimed, with no check against the identity already verified by its JWT during the WebSocket upgrade (`validateAuth`) — that verified identity was discarded right after the upgrade completed.

This threads the authenticated `clientId` through to where `setClientId` is handled and rejects the RPC call if the claimed `clientId` doesn't match:

- `validateAuth` (`server/auth.ts`) now returns the JWT's verified `clientId` instead of `void`.
- `JsonRpcApp`'s upgrade handler passes that value into `JsonRpcServer.handleUpgrade`, which carries it on the request object through to the `"connection"` handler and on into `onChannelConnection`.
- `RemoteClientRpcServer.onChannelConnection` now receives the authenticated `clientId` and its `setClientId` method throws if the client-claimed `clientId` doesn't match it.

## Unit testing

- `server/__tests__/auth.test.ts`: updated the two existing assertions that expected `validateAuth` to resolve `undefined` — it now resolves the verified `clientId`.
- `server/__tests__/e2e.test.ts`: added a new test that authenticates a raw WebSocket connection as `attackerClientId` and calls `setClientId` with a different `victimClientId`. Asserts the RPC call rejects and that `/client/victimClientId` remains unroutable (502) afterward — i.e. no channel gets hijacked.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean and the full suite passes (all existing tests green, including the happy-path e2e flows where a client's claimed `clientId` matches its authenticated identity).

## Manual testing

- [x] Deployed this branch's commit into a local `app` dev environment (bumped the `braekhus` submodule pointer, rebuilt `dist`) and confirmed the fix code was actually loaded by the running process (checked both `src` and rebuilt `dist` for the new logic, and that the process start time was after the rebuild).
- [x] Ran real SSH tunnel clients (two hosts under the same org) against the updated server and confirmed they still connect and successfully call `setClientId` with their own authenticated `clientId`, with pings continuing normally afterward — no regression for legitimate traffic.
- [ ] Manually trigger the rejection path against a live server (deliberate mismatched `setClientId`) — currently only covered by the automated e2e test above.

author: khizzcr7
body:
💡 **What**: Replaced multer's disk storage configuration with `multer.memoryStorage()`, directly passing the file buffer into `pdf-parse` instead of writing to and reading from the disk.

🎯 **Why**: Using disk storage alongside synchronous file system methods (`fs.readFileSync`, `fs.existsSync`, `fs.unlinkSync`) inside an Express route completely blocks the Node.js event loop while the file is processed. This bottleneck forces all concurrent requests to wait sequentially.

📊 **Impact**: Prevents event loop blocking during file uploads. Significantly increases concurrent request throughput and eliminates unnecessary disk I/O operations. Improves server stability by not leaving orphaned files in the event of an unexpected crash before `unlinkSync` is reached.

🔬 **Measurement**: To verify, start the backend and simulate concurrent POST requests to `/api/analyze` using a tool like autocannon or artillery. The new version will successfully handle significantly more requests per second with lower latency compared to the previous disk-blocking version.

`FocusGroupController.handleKeydown` always mapped <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> to the next element and <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> to the previous one, so with `dir="rtl"` horizontal keyboard navigation moved against the visual order. author: balwierz
body:
## Problem

The AnnData summary listed each matrix's encoding and shape only. Telling raw counts from normalised or log values meant opening the matrix and reading values. You need that to choose which layer to export, or to check what `X` holds.

## Change

`matrix_profile()` adds a summary row for `X`, each layer and `raw.X`:

- **dtype**;
- **stored count and fraction**, for sparse matrices;
- **a labelled sample**: the first 100,000 stored values of a CSR / CSC matrix, or a dense matrix's leading rows up to 100,000 values. Over the sample it reports:
  - the **max**, and the **zero share** for dense matrices;
  - whether the values are **whole numbers**: `all non-negative whole numbers (looks like raw counts)` / `all whole numbers` / `not whole numbers (e.g. v)` / `all zero` / `integer dtype`.

If the sample can't be read (e.g. a compression filter this build lacks), the row says `sample unreadable: <reason>` and the summary still opens. Docs: README, man page and CHANGELOG. TODO is updated.

## Evidence

An SRX19235353 AnnData (787 × 36,601, three matrices):
```
X profile                          float32  |  2962007 stored of 787 × 36601 (10.3%)  |  first 100000 values: max 1327, all non-negative whole numbers (looks like raw counts)
layers[UniqueAndMult-EM] profile   float32  |  3069857 stored of 787 × 36601 (10.7%)  |  first 100000 values: max 1327, not whole numbers (e.g. 2.5)
```
Opening it (`-n 3`) takes 0.09–0.10 s, both with the profile and on `main`.

- **Tests:** `tests/run_tests.sh` passes 1045/1045. The 4 new tests assert the exact rows for a log-normalised dense `X`, CSR raw counts, a CSC layer and a dense layer.
- **Sanitizers:** ASan/UBSan are clean on the hostile and compressed fixtures (badsparse, badfilter, badlzf, lzf, csc, nullstr, bigobs, raw, obsp).

author: atendimentoxburguer-arch
flock-leader
body:
## What happened

`POST /deploy/promote` for `operator@88f9040a` returned **200**. The workflow checked out that sha. Every job went green — **including `verify-deploy`**. The deploy pin never moved, the host stayed on its previous sha, and nothing said so.

```
##[warning] Image not found: ghcr.io/cogni-dao/cogni-template:sha-88f9040a (not built — skipping operator)
PROMOTED: false
run conclusion: success          ← and verify-deploy passed
```

That is a promote reporting success for doing nothing — the bug.5121 silent-no-op family. It cost real time tonight while poly's candidate lane sat burning a paid Console call every ~30s waiting for the fix that promote was supposed to ship.

## Cause

`promote-and-deploy.yml` answers "image not found" two different ways:

| artifact | missing image | result |
|---|---|---|
| remote-source (fork node) | `::error` + `exit 1` | 🔴 loud, correct |
| **in-repo** (operator, scheduler-worker) | `::warning` + `promoted=false` + `exit 0` | 🟢 **green, silent** |

`promoteNode`'s own doc asserts *"Image existence is NOT gated in-app … the workflow's own 'image not found' hard-fail is the loud backstop."* That's true for one branch and false for the other, so the documented backstop didn't exist on the path that needed it.

## Why the skip is still right sometimes

A **fleet fan-out** (`nodes` empty ⇒ every target) legitimately reaches nodes this affected-only build never rebuilt. Skipping those is correct and stays.

It's a lie for a **named** target — and the operator API always names exactly one (`nodes: input.slug`, `github-repo-write.ts`). `88f9040a` was a catalog/GitOps-only merge (`infra/catalog/`, an appset, overlays — zero app code), so **no app image is ever built for it** and that promote could not have done anything.

## The fix

- **`scripts/ci/lib/image-tags.sh`** — `missing_image_action <explicit_targets_csv>`: `fail` when the caller named its targets, `skip` when the list is empty. A lib primitive rather than more inline workflow shell (bug.5139 freeze).
- **`promote-and-deploy.yml`** — the in-repo branch consults it and hard-fails a named target. The error names the catalog-only-merge case explicitly, so the next caller fixes it in one read instead of ten minutes of log archaeology.
- **`scripts/ci/tests/image-missing-action.test.sh`** — covers both directions, including the absent-argument default.

## Scope

This makes the *outcome* honest. The deeper fix is failing closed **at dispatch** — an image manifest probe before the run is even created, so the caller gets a 4xx instead of a green run — which is **story.5023**. Cited, not duplicated.

Note: `workflow-check.mjs` reports one pre-existing failure (`pr-build.yml unexpectedly has workflow_dispatch`) on clean `main` as well; unrelated to this change.

Work item: bug.5248

Session **Loom**, at the owner's request. **Do not merge until Lighthouse confirms the Section 4 deploy is done.** Browser-only, one fragment (`050`).

## Why
Each Analytics "What's Working This Month" content summary is a paid model call, through the `generate-content-summary` n8n webhook. `buildContentSummarySection` **started one automatically whenever a client profile was rendered** and that client had no summary, or the saved one was older than the latest TopVideos scrape. That happened for any viewer, including automated test sessions, that merely opened the profile. The owner doesn't use the feature and doesn't want it spending on its own.

## Change
- **No automatic start.** Rendering a profile never calls `generateContentSummary`.
- **The empty state is now a "✦ Generate summary" button.** The existing **Update** link (stale summary) and **↻ Regenerate** button are unchanged.
- **A "loading" state restored from localStorage after a reload** (no request behind it) shows the button, instead of a skeleton that never resolves. Before, the automatic trigger restarted those.
- **Nothing else in the briefs feature changes.** Competitor, market, general and tab briefs were already click-only. `_autoSummaryAttempted` stays declared, because the client-entry reset in `260` still clears it.

## Test
New `test/analytics-content-summary-click-only.js`, **16 checks**, using the built page's own `buildContentSummarySection` and `generateContentSummary` with the webhook intercepted:
- no request when rendering with no summary, a stale summary, or a restored loading state;
- a click sends exactly one request, and the result renders.

**Against main's page it fails** at "rendering a profile has no path that starts a generation".

`client-entry-preflight`, test routing, `build:index`/`check:index` and the identity check all pass.

author: nikitakarpei
body:
PR D of the ADR 0007 stack. Base: PR C (nikitakarpei/my-yacy-node#219).

## Summary

- **A searched empty answer covers a word partition.** YaCy peers send `searchtime=0` in the default response they give to a rate-limited, unauthenticated or Robinson-refused search. A peer that searched and holds nothing sends the time it spent. The wire now carries `PeerSearched`. In the open replica-ask run from PR B, an answer from a peer that searched covers the word partition even if it lists nothing. An empty answer without a search still asks the next replica at once. Before this, a word no peer holds walked every replica of every partition: up to 48 calls for one missing compound word.
- **A searched empty answer is a sample of 0.** This change is on PR C's sampling. Such an answer lists no documents and has no index count, so the sample used to treat it as incomplete and the word could not lead. The peer searched, so the answer is complete: the word holds no documents in the sampled partition, and it can lead with a sample of 0. The other words are then not asked in partitions where the leading word has no candidates.
- **yacynode sends a search time above zero for every search it ran.** The duration is rounded up to the next millisecond, so a fast lookup of a missing word no longer sends `searchtime=0`, which peers read as a refusal. A request for another network still sends 0.

## Test plan

- `make verify` is green.
- New tests:
  - the wire reads `PeerSearched` from `searchtime`;
  - a searched empty answer settles the word partition;
  - an empty answer without a search asks the next replica;
  - a word that a peer searched and holds nothing for is sampled and leads;
  - yacynode reports a search time for a search that found nothing, and 0 for a network mismatch.

author: profalfailakawi
body:
## لماذا
مراجعة سجلّ الورك-فلو كشفت أمرين:
1. **لم يُنشر شيء تلقائياً قط**: خطوة النشر «متخطّاة» في كل تشغيل (هوية النشر غير مُعدّة) — والعلامة الخضراء كانت للاختبارات وحدها.
2. **لا طريق لأي إعداد إلى الخادم**: `deploy-vm.sh` يشغّل الحاوية بـ`NODE_ENV` ومسار القاعدة فقط. مفاتيح الدفع والبريد والتواصل والذكاء لا تصل أبداً — أي أن **ربط الدفع مستحيل** حتى بعد إعداد النشر.

وأن الفحوص تعمل بعد الدمج لا قبله: دمج #29 مرّ أخضر ثم فشل نشره باختبارين.

## ما تغيّر
### إعدادات الخادم
- `deploy-vm.sh`: ملف `/var/nahj/nahj.env` على القرص الدائم يُمرَّر بـ`--env-file` (يُنشأ 600 إن غاب). الأسرار لا تغادر الخادم وتبقى بعد كل نشر. و`NAHJ_PUBLIC_URL` يُشتقّ من النطاق تلقائياً ما لم يُضبط.
- **`scripts/server-env.sh`** (من Cloud Shell): `list` (أسرار مُقنَّعة) · `set` · `unset` · `restart` · `check` (فاحص الإعداد داخل الحاوية). قائمة إعدادات معروفة: الخطأ الإملائي يُرفض، و`NODE_ENV`/`PORT`/مسار القاعدة خارجها. القيم تُنقل base64 فلا يكسرها اقتباس، والسطر الجديد مرفوض (لا حقن إعداد ثانٍ).
- `Dockerfile`: `verify-env.mjs` داخل الصورة؛ وقسم «الموقع والتواصل» في الفاحص.

### خادمٌ لكل عميل
- `NAHJ_MARKETING=off`: الجذر يفتح التطبيق، لا صفحة تسويق ولا نموذج طلبات ولا فهرسة، وشاشة الدخول بلا روابط التسويق. ونشر العميل يُطفئ العرض أيضاً ما لم يُضبط.
- `deploy.yml`: متغيّر `NAHJ_CUSTOMERS` (سطر لكل عميل: `الخادم النطاق [المنطقة]`) — كلٌّ يُحدَّث بالصورة نفسها بعد نشرك (`SKIP_BUILD=1`)، وفشل عميلٍ لا يوقف الباقين ويُعلن في النهاية.

### فحوص كل طلب دمج
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: الأنواع والاختبارات والبناء على `pull_request`.

### الواجهة
- المالك يبلغ لوحته قبل إعداد المؤسسة («افتح لوحة المالك أولاً») — في إطارٍ لا يعرض بذرة العرض.
- الشريط الجانبي بأسماء الأقسام على الشاشات ≥1200px (وأيقونات مع تلميح بين الهاتف والعريض).

### التوثيق
- **`docs/domain.md`**: ربط النطاق خطوةً خطوة (سجل A، `NAHJ_DOMAIN`، الشهادة، عنوان إشعار الدفع، بريد النطاق، استكشاف الأعطال).
- `docs/deploy-nahj.md`: الإعدادات على الخادم، النطاق، خوادم العملاء. `GO-LIVE.md`: الخطوات بترتيبها الفعلي.

## الاختبارات

body:
## Summary
The owner's merge rule is now **rebase merges only, with linear history**: no squash merges and no merge commits (dougborg/dougborg-dot-net#511). With rebase, every commit in a pull request lands on `main` as written, and release-please derives versions and changelogs for `client`, `mcp`, and `ts` from each one. Today nothing lints commit messages here.

- **Commit check:** adds `.github/workflows/commitlint.yml` (workflow `Commit conventions`, job `Conventional commits`). It runs `@commitlint/cli` 21.2.3 (pinned) over `base..head` of the pull request. Top-level `permissions: {}`, job-level `contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false`.
- **Action pins:** this repo still references `actions/checkout@v6` / `actions/setup-node@v6` by tag, so there was no SHA pin to reuse. The new job pins the same SHAs as katana-openapi-client and site-analytics: `checkout` v7.0.1 and `setup-node` v7.0.0, with `node-version: "22"` (no `.nvmrc` here).
- **Linter config:** `commitlint.config.mjs` extends `@commitlint/config-conventional` with a type list matching the `changelog-sections` in `release-please-config.json` (build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test). Body and footer line length are unlimited, because Dependabot bodies carry release notes.
- **Dependabot:** every entry now uses `prefix: chore` with `include: scope`, so commits read `chore(deps): …` / `chore(deps-dev): …` instead of the double-scoped `chore(deps)(deps): …` / `chore(ts)(deps-dev): …`. The ecosystem is still visible from the labels. The workflows README documents the new job.

**Dependabot capitalization:** Dependabot copies the capitalization of its previous commits on `main` (the last Dependabot commit among the latest 100), and this repo's say `Bump …`, so its next PRs would read `chore(deps): Bump …` and fail `subject-case`. The rules therefore live in `commitlint.config.mjs` instead of `.commitlintrc.json`, with `ignores: [(message) => /^chore\(deps(-dev)?\): Bump /.test(message)]`. Only Dependabot's `chore(deps…): Bump` subjects are exempt; every other commit, including `feat: Add thing` or `chore(ci): Bump z`, still fails `subject-case`. The open Dependabot PRs (#133 to #142) still carry the old double-scoped prefixes (`chore(deps)(deps): Bump …`), which the ignore does not match, so they fail this check until Dependabot rebases or recreates them with the new prefix.

After this merges and the check is green, dougborg/dougborg-dot-net#511 switches this repository and its `Protect Main` ruleset to rebase-only, and adds `Conventional commits` as a required check.

## Test plan
- [x] `commitlint` over the whole history (58 commits): 19 commits with errors, 1 with a warning only (`footer-leading-blank`). Errors are historical and informational: `subject-case` 18 (mostly Dependabot `Bump …`), `header-max-length` 1.
- [x] A Dependabot-style `chore(deps): bump x from 1 to 2` message with a >100-character body line passes; a bare "Update the readme" fails
- [x] With `commitlint.config.mjs`: `chore(deps): Bump x from 1 to 2` and `chore(deps-dev): Bump y` pass; `feat: Add thing` and `chore(ci): Bump z` fail `subject-case`; `wip: thing` fails `type-enum`; `--print-config` shows the extended config-conventional rules resolved under `npx`
- [x] `actionlint`, `yamllint`, and `prettier` (Markdown) pass on the changed files
- [ ] The new `Conventional commits` job passes on this PR
